~~~text
\chapter{Translating a banking decision into a causal question}
\label{la:translation}

The preceding evidence review leaves a practical starting point: assistance
must preserve the question before it can improve an answer. This chapter
builds that question from population, action, outcome, loss and information
time. Incentive and servicing examples expose common substitutions; a
literature-graph study separates extracted claims from hypotheses; the
formulation workflow then leads to robust population comparisons and goal
clarification. Together these treatments explain which commitments an analyst
must resolve and which alternatives an assistant must retain.

\section{A business sentence can contain several questions}

``Should we increase the deposit offer?'' sounds like a single question, but
it leaves several choices unresolved. The intended action could be a change
in the quoted rate, the eligibility rule, the message shown to a customer or
the allocation of a fixed promotional budget. The outcome could be a new
deposit, retained balances, funding cost or total relationship value. The
population could be existing customers, applicants who received an offer or
everyone eligible under a proposed rule. Each choice defines a different
causal problem.

A language assistant can expose these alternatives and organize the evidence
needed to resolve them. It should not choose the easiest target to estimate
and silently treat that target as the owner's decision. In the project funding
case, the response of balances to a 25-basis-point increase and the change in
net funding cost over thirty days are retained as separate candidates. Their
business motivation is shared; their outcomes and decision consequences are
not identical. The unresolved choice is useful information, not a failure
that must be hidden by returning a number.

The co-pilot roadmap discussed by Alaa and colleagues motivates this progression
from a scientific question through assumptions, statistical targets and
interpretation. Their illustrative medical examples attend to eligibility,
baseline time, treatment and follow-up. The inspected paper also reports that
generic uncued answers can omit relevant design concerns. Applying those
principles to banking is a project proposal; the medical examples do not
validate banking clocks or interventions. \cite{v12_la_2407_19118}

\section{A question as a collection of commitments}

The project represents a question as
\begin{equation}
 Q=(\mathcal U,P,\mathcal A,\pi,\pi_0,Y,H,\nu,\ell,\mathcal I).
 \label{la:question}
\end{equation}
Here \(\mathcal U\) is the unit of analysis; \(P\) is the target population;
\(\mathcal A\) is the feasible action set; \(\pi\) and \(\pi_0\) are the
policy and comparator; \(Y\) is the outcome; \(H\) is the horizon; \(\nu\)
is the measure used to average over the population; \(\ell\) is the loss,
including its units; and \(\mathcal I\) specifies information available at
each action. This notation defines the project's declaration contract. It is
not an identification theorem.

The unit needs particular care. An account can be an observation while a
customer is the decision unit and a household is the unit within which actions
interact. An assistant can ask which role each identifier plays, but a column
called customer ID does not certify ownership or stable linkage. If several
accounts share a budget or pricing rule, an account-level action may also be
an infeasible description of the intervention. The feasible action set should
reflect what the responsible institution can actually change.

The comparator must be as explicit as the intervention. ``No treatment'' might
mean no new contact, continuation of the current contact policy, no rate
increase, or a different offer under a fixed budget. A dynamic policy can
include future actions conditional on history, so its comparator is also a
history-dependent rule. An effect relative to one comparator cannot be
reused for another solely because the same treatment variable appears in the
dataset.

The outcome and loss should also remain separate. A change in balances has
units of currency held over a horizon; funding expense combines balances,
rates and time. A larger deposit balance can have a positive acquisition
interpretation and an unfavorable net-cost implication. If \(g(a)\) is a
specified gross benefit and \(c(a)\) is a specified cost, the decision may
depend on \(E[g(a)-c(a)]\), not on \(E[g(a)]\) alone. The definitions and
valuation assumptions must be supplied before that subtraction is meaningful.
The assistant should make missing costs visible rather than invent prices.

\section{Changing a population measure changes the answer}

Let \(X\) denote baseline features and let
\(\tau(x)=E[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid X=x]\). A weighted target can be written
\begin{equation}
 \theta_w=\frac{E[w(X)\tau(X)]}{E[w(X)]},\qquad E[w(X)]>0.
 \label{la:weighted-target}
\end{equation}
Uniform, treated-population, overlap and trimmed targets use different
weights. Under the conditions that make a propensity \(e(x)=\Pr(A=1\mid X=x)\)
appropriate for the intended population, familiar choices are \(1\),
\(e(x)\), \(e(x)(1-e(x))\) and
\(1\{a\leq e(x)\leq b\}\), respectively. The formula records which average
is wanted. It does not establish exchangeability, support, estimation rates
or coverage.

An exact project example makes the distinction visible. Let two strata have
equal population probability, with propensities \(0.2\) and \(0.5\), and
effects \(0\) and \(10\). Trimming to \([0.1,0.9]\) keeps both strata, so
the trimmed-population effect is \(5\). Overlap weights are \(0.16\) and
\(0.25\), giving
\[
 \theta_{\mathrm{overlap}}=
 \frac{0.16(0)+0.25(10)}{0.16+0.25}=\frac{250}{41}
 =6.09756\ldots.
\]
Both calculations can be exact and still answer different questions. A label
such as ``overlap population'' is insufficient if its underlying weighting
rule is not retained.

This issue is directly relevant to the inspected OCI agent paper. Chou and
colleagues describe a principal/actor/critic workflow, reproducible notebooks,
point-in-time estimation and overlap diagnostics. The inspected trimming
passage uses a target label that must be reconciled with the actual weighting
rule before mapping it to conventional overlap weighting. The proposed
architecture is informative, but an assistant should not inherit a target
label without checking its definition. \cite{v12_la_2607_22443}

Changing the target to remove unsupported accounts can be scientifically
reasonable, but it is a new decision question. A bank owner may care about
precisely those accounts for which treatment support is weak. An honest report
can say that a narrower target is estimable under the supplied assumptions
while the original target remains unresolved. It should show the excluded
population, the new averaging rule and the implications for the decision.

\section{Information is governed by an availability clock}

The date on which an event occurred differs from the date on which an analyst
or policy could observe it. For a recorded variable \(V\), write \(e_V\) for
event time and \(a_V\) for availability time. The finite project fixtures
require \(e_V\leq a_V\), and a policy acting at time \(t\) can use the value
only if \(a_V\leq t\). A derived feature becomes available no earlier than
its required inputs. These rules prevent an apparently historical feature
from leaking future information into a decision.

In the servicing fixture, an account condition occurs at day ten but becomes
available at day eleven. A rule acting on day eleven may use it; a rule acting
on day ten may not. The distinction matters even when both values later appear
in the same warehouse table. A language assistant should request the recording
and availability convention, rather than infer it from a field name or a
sorted timestamp.

Advance announcements and forecasts require different variable definitions.
A forecast observed today of next month's condition is a current forecast
variable, not a measurement of a future realized condition with an impossible
availability time. Revised historical data similarly require a vintage or
revision convention. The project's finite validator does not implement every
revision protocol. It checks the stated recorded-value contract and leaves
more complex clocks as explicit extensions.

Equal timestamps do not determine direction. Two columns aggregated to the
same day may hide a finer action sequence or a common cause. The assistant
can propose a finer clock and identify the evidence needed to support it.
It cannot establish temporal precedence by placing one variable first in a
diagram. When the granularity is insufficient, the ambiguity should survive
into the model class.

\section{An available covariate is not automatically an adjustment variable}

In a sequential servicing model, \(A_0\) changes an intermediate condition
\(L_1\), which affects both a later action \(A_1\) and the outcome \(Y\).
The same \(L_1\) is a mediator for the first action and a common cause of the
second action--outcome relation. Its appropriate use depends on the target.
Including every available column in one regression does not preserve all
possible total, direct and policy effects.

The project declaration therefore distinguishes a policy-history purpose
from an ordinary adjustment purpose. A simple directed-path diagnostic flags
a post-treatment descendant proposed as an ordinary total-effect control.
It does not declare all post-treatment conditioning invalid. Controlled
direct effects and longitudinal procedures need their own question and
formal analysis. A warning from a declaration validator is not a replacement
for an adjustment criterion or an identification algorithm.

Observation processes can alter the target in a similar way. Suppose only
successfully linked records enter an analysis and both action and repayment
affect successful linkage. The selection indicator is part of the causal
problem, and an effect among linked records may differ from an effect in the
original population. A record-link score is an observed proxy; it is not
verified ownership. The observation fixture deliberately retains a latent
ownership variable, a selection node and an unresolved population choice.

CausalDS provides a useful literature distinction here: its conceptual SCM
variables and its separate observation model are not interchangeable. The
paper's narrated synthetic scenes can test how an agent handles that
distinction, but they do not supply authentic banking semantic or assignment
truth. \cite{v12_la_2607_08093}

\section{The handoff to formal analysis}

The assistant's useful output is a reviewable declaration and a record of
what remains unresolved. A selected declaration contains one explicit target,
its population measure, the intervention and comparator, clocks, feasible
actions, outcome and loss. An ambiguous declaration retains candidate targets
without covertly selecting one. A contradicted assumption cannot be left as
an inconsequential note while the calculation proceeds as if it held.

The local project validator exercises these distinctions with four synthetic
banking cases and adverse contract tests. It checks declared identities,
types, references and selected clock/graph conditions. It does not authenticate
an institution, certify a reviewer, determine whether a causal assumption is
true, or implement every MAG/PAG/CPDAG validity condition. A declaration ready
for formal analysis is ready for the next conditional operation, not a
qualified bank recommendation.

This boundary also explains the limited scope of the executable operation
tested with these declaration fixtures. A declaration can describe a dynamic
regime while that selected operation supports only a static binary population
ATE. The correct handoff then reports unsupported target mapping. Later
fitted-summary and servicing studies have their own declared regimes; their
existence does not qualify this particular mapping. Translating that request into a
static regression would produce a result at the cost of changing the user's
question. The appropriate remedy is to qualify a longitudinal operation or
obtain an explicit new target decision, with the original question preserved.

\chapter{Translating a banking decision into a causal question}
\label{la:translation}

The preceding evidence review leaves a practical starting point: assistance
must preserve the question before it can improve an answer. This chapter
builds that question from population, action, outcome, loss and information
time. Incentive and servicing examples expose common substitutions; a
literature-graph study separates extracted claims from hypotheses; the
formulation workflow then leads to robust population comparisons and goal
clarification. Together these treatments explain which commitments an analyst
must resolve and which alternatives an assistant must retain.

\section{A business sentence can contain several questions}

``Should we increase the deposit offer?'' sounds like a single question, but
it leaves several choices unresolved. The intended action could be a change
in the quoted rate, the eligibility rule, the message shown to a customer or
the allocation of a fixed promotional budget. The outcome could be a new
deposit, retained balances, funding cost or total relationship value. The
population could be existing customers, applicants who received an offer or
everyone eligible under a proposed rule. Each choice defines a different
causal problem.

A language assistant can expose these alternatives and organize the evidence
needed to resolve them. It should not choose the easiest target to estimate
and silently treat that target as the owner's decision. In the project funding
case, the response of balances to a 25-basis-point increase and the change in
net funding cost over thirty days are retained as separate candidates. Their
business motivation is shared; their outcomes and decision consequences are
not identical. The unresolved choice is useful information, not a failure
that must be hidden by returning a number.

The co-pilot roadmap discussed by Alaa and colleagues motivates this progression
from a scientific question through assumptions, statistical targets and
interpretation. Their illustrative medical examples attend to eligibility,
baseline time, treatment and follow-up. The inspected paper also reports that
generic uncued answers can omit relevant design concerns. Applying those
principles to banking is a project proposal; the medical examples do not
validate banking clocks or interventions. \citep{v12_la_2407_19118}

\section{A question as a collection of commitments}

The project represents a question as
\begin{equation}
 Q=(\mathcal U,P,\mathcal A,\pi,\pi_0,Y,H,\nu,\ell,\mathcal I).
 \label{la:question}
\end{equation}
Here \(\mathcal U\) is the unit of analysis; \(P\) is the target population;
\(\mathcal A\) is the feasible action set; \(\pi\) and \(\pi_0\) are the
policy and comparator; \(Y\) is the outcome; \(H\) is the horizon; \(\nu\)
is the measure used to average over the population; \(\ell\) is the loss,
including its units; and \(\mathcal I\) specifies information available at
each action. This notation defines the project's declaration contract. It is
not an identification theorem.

The unit needs particular care. An account can be an observation while a
customer is the decision unit and a household is the unit within which actions
interact. An assistant can ask which role each identifier plays, but a column
called customer ID does not certify ownership or stable linkage. If several
accounts share a budget or pricing rule, an account-level action may also be
an infeasible description of the intervention. The feasible action set should
reflect what the responsible institution can actually change.

The comparator must be as explicit as the intervention. ``No treatment'' might
mean no new contact, continuation of the current contact policy, no rate
increase, or a different offer under a fixed budget. A dynamic policy can
include future actions conditional on history, so its comparator is also a
history-dependent rule. An effect relative to one comparator cannot be
reused for another solely because the same treatment variable appears in the
dataset.

The outcome and loss should also remain separate. A change in balances has
units of currency held over a horizon; funding expense combines balances,
rates and time. A larger deposit balance can have a positive acquisition
interpretation and an unfavorable net-cost implication. If \(g(a)\) is a
specified gross benefit and \(c(a)\) is a specified cost, the decision may
depend on \(E[g(a)-c(a)]\), not on \(E[g(a)]\) alone. The definitions and
valuation assumptions must be supplied before that subtraction is meaningful.
The assistant should make missing costs visible rather than invent prices.

\section{Changing a population measure changes the answer}

Let \(X\) denote baseline features and let
\(\tau(x)=E[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid X=x]\). A weighted target can be written
\begin{equation}
 \theta_w=\frac{E[w(X)\tau(X)]}{E[w(X)]},\qquad E[w(X)]>0.
 \label{la:weighted-target}
\end{equation}
Uniform, treated-population, overlap and trimmed targets use different
weights. Under the conditions that make a propensity \(e(x)=\Pr(A=1\mid X=x)\)
appropriate for the intended population, familiar choices are \(1\),
\(e(x)\), \(e(x)(1-e(x))\) and
\(1\{a\leq e(x)\leq b\}\), respectively. The formula records which average
is wanted. It does not establish exchangeability, support, estimation rates
or coverage.

An exact project example makes the distinction visible. Let two strata have
equal population probability, with propensities \(0.2\) and \(0.5\), and
effects \(0\) and \(10\). Trimming to \([0.1,0.9]\) keeps both strata, so
the trimmed-population effect is \(5\). Overlap weights are \(0.16\) and
\(0.25\), giving
\[
 \theta_{\mathrm{overlap}}=
 \frac{0.16(0)+0.25(10)}{0.16+0.25}=\frac{250}{41}
 =6.09756\ldots.
\]
Both calculations can be exact and still answer different questions. A label
such as ``overlap population'' is insufficient if its underlying weighting
rule is not retained.

This issue is directly relevant to the inspected OCI agent paper. Chou and
colleagues describe a principal/actor/critic workflow, reproducible notebooks,
point-in-time estimation and overlap diagnostics. The inspected trimming
passage uses a target label that must be reconciled with the actual weighting
rule before mapping it to conventional overlap weighting. The proposed
architecture is informative, but an assistant should not inherit a target
label without checking its definition. \citep{v12_la_2607_22443}

Changing the target to remove unsupported accounts can be scientifically
reasonable, but it is a new decision question. A bank owner may care about
precisely those accounts for which treatment support is weak. An honest report
can say that a narrower target is estimable under the supplied assumptions
while the original target remains unresolved. It should show the excluded
population, the new averaging rule and the implications for the decision.

\section{Information is governed by an availability clock}

The date on which an event occurred differs from the date on which an analyst
or policy could observe it. For a recorded variable \(V\), write \(e_V\) for
event time and \(a_V\) for availability time. The finite project fixtures
require \(e_V\leq a_V\), and a policy acting at time \(t\) can use the value
only if \(a_V\leq t\). A derived feature becomes available no earlier than
its required inputs. These rules prevent an apparently historical feature
from leaking future information into a decision.

In the servicing fixture, an account condition occurs at day ten but becomes
available at day eleven. A rule acting on day eleven may use it; a rule acting
on day ten may not. The distinction matters even when both values later appear

revision convention. The project's finite validator does not implement every

more complex clocks as explicit extensions.

Equal timestamps do not determine direction. Two columns aggregated to the
same day may hide a finer action sequence or a common cause. The assistant

It cannot establish temporal precedence by placing one variable first in a
diagram. When the granularity is insufficient, the ambiguity should survive
into the model class.

\section{Tigramite as a temporal reference: preserving the meaning of the result}
\label{exec23:tigramite-scope}
A bank comparing deposit rates and subsequent balances needs to distinguish a conditional-dependence statistic, an unresolved endpoint, a fitted intervention response and uncertainty about that response. Tigramite offers explicitly differentiated methods for these stages. The selected January 2026 source declares version 5.2.10.1. PCMCI, PCMCI+, LPCMCI, RPCMCI and J-PCMCI+ differ in contemporaneous-link, hidden-variable, stationarity and context assumptions. The conditional-independence test adds its own restrictions: ParCorr uses linear residual correlation, whereas other tests require their own treatment. These are distinct scientific choices within one package, not interchangeable routes to a monetary effect. \cite{exec23_tigramite_reuse_source,exec14_pt_tigramite}

The proposal selects Tigramite as a method-specific reference, with a conditional route to an isolated Python worker. Prior installed-version operations remain relevant within their recorded scope, including the finite-DAG oracle comparison. A matching version string does not establish byte identity with the selected repository tree, and those operations do not qualify every delegate considered here. \cite{runtime_tigramite_scope,runtime_networkx_dynamic} The additional evidence below is static source inspection and independent exact examples, not another native trial.

\subsection{A statistic, a graph and a dollar response}
\label{exec23:tigramite-statistic}
Let $X_t$ denote a centered rate intervention in specified rate units, $Y_{t+1}$ a balance response in dollars and $Z_t$ the chosen history. Consider a stipulated linear population,
\begin{equation}
 Y_{t+1}=100+20X_t+\gamma^\top Z_t+\epsilon_{t+1},\qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(X_t\mid Z_t)=1,\quad
 \operatorname{Var}(\epsilon_{t+1}\mid Z_t)=225.
 \label{exec23:tigramite-dollar}
\end{equation}
Assume independent residualized exposure and error, an intervention-invariant mechanism, a history sufficient for adjustment, and intervention support. The residual covariance is $20$ and the residual variance of $Y$ is $625$. Thus the partial correlation is $20/25=4/5$, whereas the stipulated causal slope is 20 dollars per rate unit. A one-unit change with stipulated cost 12 dollars has net value 8 dollars. Reading $4/5$ as a dollar gain instead gives $-56/5$ dollars. These are authored population values, not observed bank returns; their disagreement demonstrates the units lost in an invalid conversion. \cite{exec23_tigramite_reference}

PCMCI labels its \texttt{val\_matrix} as test-statistic values and its optional \texttt{conf\_matrix} as intervals for those values. ParCorr fits ordinary least-squares residuals and returns their Pearson correlation. Its analytic test uses $T-d$ degrees of freedom for $d$ array rows and $T$ usable observations, returning a nonfinite p-value when degrees of freedom are insufficient. The CI base also supplies a constant-variable shortcut. An adapter must report degeneracy and invalid arithmetic rather than interpret every returned entry as scientific evidence of absence. The \texttt{run\_pcmci} signature defaults FDR to \texttt{none}, although the parameter prose says \texttt{fdr\_bh}; a profile must set this argument explicitly. The correction helper distinguishes lagged-only and contemporaneous-inclusive test families. A corrected edge p-value is not a portfolio-response interval. \cite{exec23_tigramite_reuse_source}

\subsection{Endpoint ambiguity is a substantive output}
\label{exec23:tigramite-graph}
PCMCI+ can return contemporaneous ambiguity and conflict marks; LPCMCI returns a temporal partial ancestral graph. The selected effect class accepts DAG and ADMG variants, including temporal and stationary forms, but does not enable its commented-out PAG graph types. A wrapper cannot bridge these interfaces by replacing circles or conflicts with arbitrary arrows. It must retain the compatible graph family, justify additional scientific restrictions where possible, and determine identification or set identification under those restrictions. A graph-conditioned adjustment fit does not solve that preceding problem. \cite{exec23_tigramite_reuse_source}

Even a summary frequency requires its exact definition. The default graph-summary routine chooses a modal endpoint string but, in a tie, reports the sum of tied modal counts divided by the resample count. Five resamples with one direction and five with the reverse can produce a conflict mark with reported frequency one, although none of the ten inputs contains that conflict mark. In a second stipulated ensemble, four absent links and three of each direction make absence the most frequent individual string, while adjacency has total frequency $6/10$. The alternative adjacency-first aggregation answers the latter question. These finite examples do not establish discovery failure; they show why the counts, aggregation rule and emitted mark must accompany the summary. Such frequency is neither the posterior probability of an arrow nor a calibrated graph confidence level. \cite{exec23_tigramite_reuse_source,exec23_tigramite_reference}

\subsection{An intervention prediction still needs a contrast}
\label{exec23:tigramite-intervention}
For a supplied admissible graph and valid adjustment set $Z$, the unconditional adjusted response is
\begin{equation}
 \mu(x)=\int E[Y\mid X=x,Z=z]p(z)\,dz,\qquad
 \Delta(x,x_0)=\mu(x)-\mu(x_0).
 \label{exec23:tigramite-contrast}
\end{equation}
This requires identifying graph and sampling assumptions; fitting regression does not supply them. The inspected prediction delegate aggregates predictions over stored adjustment observations. For an illustrative zero-mean adjusted history in the linear population, predictions at zero and one are 100 and 120 dollars; the contrast is 20 dollars. Calling 120 the gain includes the baseline. A caller must preserve that baseline, adjustment distribution, units, transforms and conditioning target. The effect class checks adjustment validity by default but exposes a bypass for a user-supplied set. An accepted product profile should not silently enable that bypass. \cite{exec23_tigramite_reuse_source,exec23_tigramite_reference}

The hard intervention sets an exposure value; the source's soft option adds an amount to each observed exposure. For nonlinear responses these policies differ. If $Y=X^2$ and the stipulated reference population places equal mass at zero and two, the hard zero-to-one contrast is $1$, whereas adding one to everyone's observed exposure gives
\begin{equation}
 E[(X+1)^2-X^2]=2E[X]+1=3.
 \label{exec23:tigramite-policy}
\end{equation}
Here soft denotes that additive implementation, not every stochastic intervention in causal inference. Conditional nested regression and alternative estimators need separate review. \cite{exec23_tigramite_reuse_source,exec23_tigramite_reference}

The effect bootstrap refits the selected effect procedure and takes percentiles of intervention predictions, retaining the supplied graph. Discovery bootstrap summaries instead concern graphs and statistics. Neither bootstrap code nor a nonempty interval establishes joint validity after graph discovery, graph or policy selection, or under arbitrary dependence. Specify the uncertainty target and sampling law before choosing which stages to resample. \cite{exec23_tigramite_reuse_source}

\subsection{Calendars, masks and resampling belong in the scientific contract}
\label{exec23:tigramite-calendar}
The data layer constructs lagged arrays from integer reference positions, dataset offsets and a cutoff. Its ordinary twice-maximum-lag cutoff and the effect fitter's maximum-lag cutoff can retain different observations. Masks apply to selected variable roles, separately from missing-value handling. Calendar gaps, reporting delays and multiple panels require explicit time-grid conversion and effective-sample records. The earlier inspected RPCMCI implementation replaces a supplied mask, requiring a distinct admission rule. \cite{exec23_tigramite_reuse_source}

Several static edge cases warrant native oracle tests. The selected data-layer bootstrap draws starts from \texttt{arange(n-L)} for $n$ retained positions and block length $L$. For $n=6,L=2$, these are $0,1,2,3$; the complete nonwrapping set includes start 4. Position 5 is absent from the first expression's reachable indices. This enumeration describes the inspected expression, not an executed failure or quantified inference bias. Nonconsecutive retained positions also need not be adjacent calendar times. \cite{exec23_tigramite_reuse_source,exec23_tigramite_reference}

The missing-value extension constructs later position indices without clipping before assignment. Missing position 5 in a six-position array, extended through lag two, yields $5,6,7$; the last two exceed the bounds. The source writes the used-indices attribute after its dataset loop while concatenating samples from all datasets. A multi-panel adapter must verify complete panel provenance rather than assume this attribute records every panel. These observations motivate narrow replay cases and separately reviewed patches; they do not establish that all package analyses fail. \cite{exec23_tigramite_reuse_source,exec23_tigramite_reference}

\subsection{The reuse choice and the work needed to change it}
\label{exec23:tigramite-choice}
Whole-package adoption is premature because method assumptions, graph conversion, uncertainty and these edge cases require distinct contracts. Porting to R, Java or C++ is not justified by a measured benefit here: orientation rules, tests and resampling would acquire a second maintenance burden. A selected Python worker is the candidate to test, preserving endpoints and counts, effective observations and transforms, warnings and failures, and refusing unsupported graph-to-effect requests. These requirements describe proposed capabilities.

The repository declares GPL version 3 or later and contains GPLv3 text. Setup specifies minimum dependencies rather than a locked environment; optional algorithms add packages. This records licensing evidence, not clearance of a future distribution. Process isolation alone does not settle rights. A maintainer must bind artifacts and versions; a scientific owner must choose the sampling law, target and tests; an operator must address custody, failure budgets and distribution. Comparison should include installation, search, ambiguous and failed queries, resampling, serialization, upgrade regression and human review. Reconsider integration when a permissible pinned profile passes the exact oracles and registered public or synthetic trial. Later bank experiments should be justified by prototype merit rather than required to finish this proposal decision. \cite{exec23_tigramite_reuse_source,exec23_tigramite_reference}

Here soft denotes that additive implementation, not every stochastic intervention in causal inference. Conditional nested regression and alternative estimators need separate review. \citep{exec23_tigramite_reuse_source,exec23_tigramite_reference}

The effect bootstrap refits the selected effect procedure and takes percentiles of intervention predictions, retaining the supplied graph. Discovery bootstrap summaries instead concern graphs and statistics. Neither bootstrap code nor a nonempty interval establishes joint validity after graph discovery, graph or policy selection, or under arbitrary dependence. Specify the uncertainty target and sampling law before choosing which stages to resample. \citep{exec23_tigramite_reuse_source}

\subsection{Calendars, masks and resampling belong in the scientific contract}
\label{exec23:tigramite-calendar}
The data layer constructs lagged arrays from integer reference positions, dataset offsets and a cutoff. Its ordinary twice-maximum-lag cutoff and the effect fitter's maximum-lag cutoff can retain different observations. Masks apply to selected variable roles, separately from missing-value handling. Calendar gaps, reporting delays and multiple panels require explicit time-grid conversion and effective-sample records. The earlier inspected RPCMCI implementation replaces a supplied mask, requiring a distinct admission rule. \citep{exec23_tigramite_reuse_source}

Several static edge cases warrant native oracle tests. The selected data-layer bootstrap draws starts from \texttt{arange(n-L)} for $n$ retained positions and block length $L$. For $n=6,L=2$, these are $0,1,2,3$; the complete nonwrapping set includes start 4. Position 5 is absent from the first expression's reachable indices. This enumeration describes the inspected expression, not an executed failure or quantified inference bias. Nonconsecutive retained positions also need not be adjacent calendar times. \citep{exec23_tigramite_reuse_source,exec23_tigramite_reference}

The missing-value extension constructs later position indices without clipping before assignment. Missing position 5 in a six-position array, extended through lag two, yields $5,6,7$; the last two exceed the bounds. The source writes the used-indices attribute after its dataset loop while concatenating samples from all datasets. A multi-panel adapter must verify complete panel provenance rather than assume this attribute records every panel. These observations motivate narrow replay cases and separately reviewed patches; they do not establish that all package analyses fail. \citep{exec23_tigramite_reuse_source,exec23_tigramite_reference}

\subsection{The reuse choice and the work needed to change it}
\label{exec23:tigramite-choice}
Whole-package adoption is premature because method assumptions, graph conversion, uncertainty and these edge cases require distinct contracts. Porting to R, Java or C++ is not justified by a measured benefit here: orientation rules, tests and resampling would acquire a second maintenance burden. A selected Python worker is the candidate to test, preserving endpoints and counts, effective observations and transforms, warnings and failures, and refusing unsupported graph-to-effect requests. These requirements describe proposed capabilities.

The repository declares GPL version 3 or later and contains GPLv3 text. Setup specifies minimum dependencies rather than a locked environment; optional algorithms add packages. This records licensing evidence, not clearance of a future distribution. Process isolation alone does not settle rights. A maintainer must bind artifacts and versions; a scientific owner must choose the sampling law, target and tests; an operator must address custody, failure budgets and distribution. Comparison should include installation, search, ambiguous and failed queries, resampling, serialization, upgrade regression and human review. Reconsider integration when a permissible pinned profile passes the exact oracles and registered public or synthetic trial. Later bank experiments should be justified by prototype merit rather than required to finish this proposal decision. \citep{exec23_tigramite_reuse_source,exec23_tigramite_reference}

\hypertarget{temporal-predictions-and-interventions-on-conversations}{%
\section{Temporal predictions and interventions on
conversations}\label{temporal-predictions-and-interventions-on-conversations}}

\label{exec13:census-temporal}

A time series can support a useful prediction without identifying a
useful intervention. The distinction remains necessary when a language
model produces a graph and an accompanying explanation. Augur offers a
concrete example: a teacher model proposes relations between covariates,
a student learns from selected explanations, and the downstream task
predicts a future trend. The inspected preprint evaluates air, power,
traffic and finance settings, using classification F1 and AUROC for
prediction. These are relevant forecasting outcomes; they do not
estimate the value of a deposit rate change or a sequence of servicing
actions. \cite{exec13_census_augur_arxiv}

\hypertarget{what-a-temporal-graph-proposal-establishes}{%
\subsection{What a temporal graph proposal
establishes}\label{what-a-temporal-graph-proposal-establishes}}

Augur first retains highly correlated pairs using Spearman ranks, asks a
language model to choose among directed, confounded and spurious
relationships, and repairs graph cycles. Its stability score measures
agreement across candidate graphs. Its groundedness score checks that a
summary agrees with the graph from which it was generated. Each
component has a clear engineering purpose, but the latter two can be
high when all candidates share the same wrong causal premise. Acyclicity
is a structural property; agreement with one's own graph is an internal
consistency property. \cite{exec13_census_augur_arxiv}

The authors explicitly acknowledge causal sufficiency and the
possibility that correlation pruning misses nonlinear or lagged
dependence. Asking the model to output ``confounded'\,' does not
independently demonstrate hidden-state identification. Nor does a
chronological train/test split create exchangeability of a proposed
action. In a deposit application, funding cost and deposit outflow may
respond to an unobserved liquidity shock. A predictor can exploit that
relationship while remaining unable to answer what outflow would have
been under a different offered rate.

The proposal should retain this architecture as a forecasting and
hypothesis generation comparator. A causal evaluation needs a separate
target and separate truth: for example, generated lagged mechanisms with
known interventions, omitted common causes and nonlinear dependence
deliberately missed by marginal screening. Report predictive performance
and intervention performance separately. A failure of intervention
recovery can coexist with a useful forecast and should lead to a
restricted product role, rather than erasing the forecast result or
relabeling it as policy evidence.

\hypertarget{a-directly-relevant-longitudinal-method}{%
\subsection{A directly relevant longitudinal
method}\label{a-directly-relevant-longitudinal-method}}

Zhang, Wang and Dhillon study sequences of human edits and model
replies. Their CausalCollab method proposes an Incremental Stylistic
Effect (ISE), uses a conditional variational autoencoder to represent
editing styles, and combines a fitted outcome model with Monte Carlo
evaluation of a longitudinal functional. Their identification theorem
explicitly assumes sequential exchangeability and positivity for the
style interventions. Thus there is a concrete literature route for
studying longitudinal human--LM collaboration; its existence should not
be obscured by a search that returns mostly generic causal-inference
papers. \cite{exec13_census_collaboration}

For clarity, let \(L_t\) denote information presented before editing
step \(t\), \(A_t\) the human edit, and \(H_t=(\bar L_t,\bar A_{t-1})\)
the recorded history. A potential terminal outcome is \(Y(\bar a_T)\).
Exchangeability requires the recorded history to remove the common
causes of the edit and its downstream outcome. An analyst's private
customer knowledge, skill or intention can violate this requirement even
when every message has been logged. The low dimensionality of a style
score also does not establish overlap: legally required text may allow
little variation in some histories, and certain kinds of edit may never
occur for distressed customers.

The source defines the outcome associated with a style functional
through a conditional mixture over text versions having that style. This
matters for implementation. A learned coordinate and an instruction such
as ``make this more reassuring'\,' need not describe the same
intervention. A model can make a response more reassuring by changing
tone, by promising compensation, or by omitting a warning. Those changes
can have different effects and costs. Before adopting the estimand, the
proposal must specify which distribution of complete edits implements
the change and which content must be held fixed.

Consider a second project-generated reference example. Two proposed
messages receive the same ``polite'\,' label. Their stipulated response
probabilities are \(1/5\) and \(4/5\), while the reference message has
response probability \(1/10\). Suppose an editing policy selects the
second message with probability \(q\). Its effect against the reference
is

\[
 (1-q)\frac15+q\frac45-\frac1{10}
 =\frac1{10}+\frac35q.
\]

The effects are \(1/10,2/5,7/10\) at \(q=0,1/2,1\), respectively,
despite an identical style label. These are exact values under an
invented law, not observed customer effects. They show why the mixture
is part of the intervention definition. A randomized choice among fixed
text variants is a substantive alternative to inferring a latent
stylistic effect. It has a narrower target but makes treatment versions
directly inspectable.

\hypertarget{what-the-available-evidence-leaves-open}{%
\subsection{What the available evidence leaves
open}\label{what-the-available-evidence-leaves-open}}

CausalCollab constructs counterfactual edits with ChatGPT, uses
model-assigned outcome labels, and changes the association between a
confounding signal and the outcome in its evaluation data. Its three
sources include human--model collaborative writing, model self-chat, and
a hybrid dialogue setting. They should not all be described as
independently observed human intervention outcomes. Performance under
this constructed design is useful evidence about that design, but is not
a direct measurement of how real users would have responded to unchosen
edits. \cite{exec13_census_collaboration}

This supports an affordable proposal-stage evaluation. Begin with public
or generated interaction histories, fix a small set of
content-preserving edit policies, and expose the evaluator to known
latent intentions and missing history in deliberately adverse cases.
Compare a fixed editing policy, an observed-association rule, a
correctly specified numerical longitudinal method, and the proposed
representation-based method. Keep the true generator inaccessible to the
method. Assess policy-value error, support, refusal and total review
effort, in addition to language quality. Generated labels should be
identified as such and their sensitivity to a second label rule should
be reported.

A live human or bank experiment becomes valuable when this work
identifies a consequential uncertainty that the generated law cannot
answer. It is not a prerequisite for specifying the architecture or
exposing its failure mechanisms. Conversely, neither the inspected
theorem nor a generated experiment entitles the proposal to claim
identification under unrecorded human intentions. Direct replication
still requires review of the exact representation training, integration
scheme, outcome labels and source-code versions.

\label{exec13:census-temporal-end}

~~~

## Edit 245
docs/release/2026-10-29/source/docs/writing-repair/2026-10-29/src/41d61ab9a3845f5b.tex

Use parenthetical supporting citations at the individually inspected non-subject occurrences; bare cite renders author names as stray prose.

Substantive destination: All substantive text remains at the same position. The only replacement is the citation command name cite→citep. Every equation, numeric input, citation key, label, assumption, negative result and alternative survives in order.

Before:
~~~text
\hypertarget{agent-architectures-must-preserve-scientific-uncertainty}{%
\subsection{Agent architectures must preserve scientific
uncertainty}\label{agent-architectures-must-preserve-scientific-uncertainty}}

\label{exec13:census-agents}

Several systems now make causal analysis a sequence of tool-supported
decisions. Their strongest contribution is often a concrete
representation of the intermediate work: a dataset, a graph, an
estimand, a proof statement or a failed tool call. Comparing these
systems requires examining what each intermediate object means and which
transformations are allowed. A graph stored in agent memory can prevent
a variable-name error while still carrying an unsupported orientation
into every later calculation.

\hypertarget{causal-agent-useful-tool-boundaries-and-unequal-baselines}{%
\subsubsection{Causal Agent: useful tool boundaries and unequal
baselines}\label{causal-agent-useful-tool-boundaries-and-unequal-baselines}}

Han and colleagues store causal graph objects in a dictionary that
agents address by name. This connects independence tests, graph
questions and effect calculations without requiring each operation to
reconstruct the graph from prose. Their CausalTQA examples combine small
generated nonlinear additive Gaussian mechanisms with medical and
marketing vocabulary. The vocabulary tests a language interface; it does
not turn the generated mechanism into a medical or marketing
observation. \cite{exec13_census_causal_agent}

The paper documents informative failures: requesting conditional rather
than marginal independence, passing the wrong variable name, using the
wrong graph operation, and building unnecessarily long tool chains.
Typed variable references and explicit tool signatures are plausible
remedies. The main code-generation baseline, however, executes once,
whereas the agent uses specialized tools and iterative reasoning. Its
measured advantage therefore combines tool design, supplied knowledge
and opportunities for repair. An evaluation intended to isolate
orchestration should give a deterministic workflow and a simpler agent
the same tool implementations and permitted repair budget.

The reported average cost of 3.37 seconds, 2.51 iterations and 5,308
tokens comes from 100 sampled variable, edge and graph questions with a
maximum iteration count of 15. It does not establish the cost of the
full effect workflow, rare failures or deployment under a different
model and platform. An average well below a limit is also insufficient
evidence to remove that limit. The prototype should retain explicit
budgets and report tails, timeouts, failed requests and review effort.
The source's effect-answer tolerance and benchmark oracle require code
inspection before its reported 157 correct answers out of 160 become a
reproduction target. \cite{exec13_census_causal_agent}

\hypertarget{orca-shared-state-without-silently-choosing-a-causal-world}{%
\subsubsection{ORCA: shared state without silently choosing a causal
world}\label{orca-shared-state-without-silently-choosing-a-causal-world}}

ORCA organizes analysis of relational databases around dataset
exploration, discovery and inference. It records table choices, joins,
variable roles, candidate graphs and estimation configurations, with
opportunities for human review. Its REEF benchmark uses a specified
structural causal model inside a relational e-commerce database. This is
directly relevant to a banking proposal: a mistaken join or aggregation
can change the unit of analysis before a causal estimator is called.
\cite{exec13_census_orca}

The important limitation lies between graph discovery and inference. The
paper describes a consensus PAG that retains uncertain endpoints,
followed by a separate ``actionable'\,' DAG. Uncertain directions are
resolved using the highest-ranked candidate, cycle-safe orientation,
reversal or edge removal. Acyclicity does not establish that the
selected orientation is true. An effect computed from this one DAG is
conditional on choices added during that conversion, and cannot
automatically represent all models encoded by the uncertainty-preserving
graph.

For a servicing decision, suppose distress and contact intensity remain
ambiguously related. Directing the edge one way can make distress an
adjustment variable; directing it the other can make it a treatment
descendant. The proposed interface should retain the original graph
object and give every added orientation an explicit assumption record.
It should compare identification across compatible models, return an
effect set where appropriate, or state that a scalar target is not
identified. Ranking an orientation for display is not authorization to
treat it as scientific fact. This is a proposed restriction on reuse,
not behavior shown to exist in ORCA's implementation.

The reported user study also requires careful interpretation. Twelve
participants used ORCA and a baseline with tools, step gates and minimal
state in counterbalanced order. Table 1 gives rounded completion rates
of 0.83 and 0.75. The abstract's 42-percentage-point completion gain is
not consistent with that table; it should not be repeated as a verified
result. Appendix E defines completion as producing an ATE regardless of
accuracy, and discovery success as including both treatment and outcome
nodes. Neither definition establishes correct discovery.
\cite{exec13_census_orca}

The paper's ``CI coverage'\,' description counts an estimated ATE
falling within an interval around a ground-truth effect. That wording
differs from the usual repeated-sampling event in which an estimated
interval contains a fixed true effect. Its exact oracle and
implementation require clarification. Likewise, the full-data test for
the ATE-error condition effect has \(p=.321\), whereas the analysis
excluding large configuration-error outliers reports \(p=.020\) under
OLS. Configuration failures are central outcomes for a workflow product.
They should remain in the primary comparison, with conditional numerical
accuracy reported separately.

\hypertarget{causalpulse-operational-success-has-a-different-denominator}{%
\subsubsection{CausalPulse: operational success has a different
denominator}\label{causalpulse-operational-success-has-a-different-denominator}}

CausalPulse supplies another concrete design: agents coordinate semantic
descriptions, domain rules and causal tools through a utility layer that
includes MCP. Such interfaces can make tools accessible and operations
traceable. The inspected manufacturing study nevertheless distinguishes
successful operation from successful root-cause attribution. Its PSE
example reports Hits@1 of .44, precision .46, recall .40 and F1 .39
despite much higher operational success. Tool availability and
completion are necessary engineering outcomes, but substituting them for
causal correctness would misstate the evidence. \cite{exec13_pulse}

This distinction determines the proposed monitoring interface. It should
record whether the request was parsed, whether the analysis was
admissible, whether the tools completed, whether the scientific target
was answered, and whether the decision was useful under the declared
loss. These events need separate denominators. A scientific refusal can
be a correct answer, while a complete report can be wrong. Banking
acceptance would additionally need appropriate target-bank evidence; the
public prototype can already test these distinctions with generated
known-truth cases.

\hypertarget{causalsmith-a-checked-proof-still-needs-a-checked-statement}{%
\subsubsection{CausalSmith: a checked proof still needs a checked
statement}\label{causalsmith-a-checked-proof-still-needs-a-checked-statement}}

CausalSmith combines a Lean library with proposal, formalization, proof
and presentation stages. Its paper reports 8,179 declarations and a
catalog of 144 runs: 14 accepted, 59 downgraded and 71 failed. Those
counts include reruns as separate entries and exclude a legacy track.
They describe one campaign with changing model versions, not independent
draws from a fixed research-task population. The authors explicitly
acknowledge that research quality ratings lack independent human
validation and that the error rate of their LLM statement-match audit is
unknown. \cite{exec13_census_causalsmith}

The source's most useful distinction is between checking a proof against
a formal statement and checking whether that statement expresses the
intended claim. A compiled artifact can assume a hard step as an axiom,
weaken a conclusion, strengthen an assumption or make a predicate
vacuous. The paper describes mechanical scans and dependency checks
alongside language-model statement review. These are complementary
checks with different assurances. The latter does not acquire a formal
guarantee merely by sitting next to a proof checker.

For a proposed bank-effect theorem, the statement record should expose
the unit, intervention, estimand, time ordering, conditioning
information, positivity and dependence assumptions. The proof
environment should bind the toolchain, imported definitions and axioms.
A separate review should compare the English claim with that exact
formal statement and test whether its assumptions are satisfiable in the
intended model. A theorem conditional on observed confounders cannot be
presented as solving unmeasured confounding in operational data. Formal
correctness, semantic fidelity and scientific relevance each need their
own evidence.

The near-term reuse choice is therefore selective. Retain typed graph
memory, explicit intermediate state, preserved failures, and formal
statement/dependency records as design candidates. Defer executable
adoption of these newly inspected systems until exact code,
dependencies, licenses and relevant numerical or proof paths have been
reviewed. This permits a concrete prototype architecture now without
claiming that paper descriptions have already been integrated or
independently reproduced.

\label{exec13:census-agents-end}

~~~

object and give every added orientation an explicit assumption record.
It should compare identification across compatible models, return an
effect set where appropriate, or state that a scalar target is not
identified. Ranking an orientation for display is not authorization to
treat it as scientific fact. This is a proposed restriction on reuse,
not behavior shown to exist in ORCA's implementation.

The reported user study also requires careful interpretation. Twelve
participants used ORCA and a baseline with tools, step gates and minimal
state in counterbalanced order. Table 1 gives rounded completion rates
of 0.83 and 0.75. The abstract's 42-percentage-point completion gain is
not consistent with that table; it should not be repeated as a verified
result. Appendix E defines completion as producing an ATE regardless of
accuracy, and discovery success as including both treatment and outcome
nodes. Neither definition establishes correct discovery.
\citep{exec13_census_orca}

The paper's ``CI coverage'\,' description counts an estimated ATE
falling within an interval around a ground-truth effect. That wording
differs from the usual repeated-sampling event in which an estimated
interval contains a fixed true effect. Its exact oracle and
implementation require clarification. Likewise, the full-data test for
the ATE-error condition effect has \(p=.321\), whereas the analysis
excluding large configuration-error outliers reports \(p=.020\) under
OLS. Configuration failures are central outcomes for a workflow product.
They should remain in the primary comparison, with conditional numerical
accuracy reported separately.

\hypertarget{causalpulse-operational-success-has-a-different-denominator}{%
\subsubsection{CausalPulse: operational success has a different
denominator}\label{causalpulse-operational-success-has-a-different-denominator}}

CausalPulse supplies another concrete design: agents coordinate semantic
descriptions, domain rules and causal tools through a utility layer that
includes MCP. Such interfaces can make tools accessible and operations
traceable. The inspected manufacturing study nevertheless distinguishes
successful operation from successful root-cause attribution. Its PSE
example reports Hits@1 of .44, precision .46, recall .40 and F1 .39
despite much higher operational success. Tool availability and
completion are necessary engineering outcomes, but substituting them for
causal correctness would misstate the evidence. \citep{exec13_pulse}

This distinction determines the proposed monitoring interface. It should
record whether the request was parsed, whether the analysis was
admissible, whether the tools completed, whether the scientific target
was answered, and whether the decision was useful under the declared
loss. These events need separate denominators. A scientific refusal can
be a correct answer, while a complete report can be wrong. Banking
acceptance would additionally need appropriate target-bank evidence; the
public prototype can already test these distinctions with generated
known-truth cases.

\hypertarget{causalsmith-a-checked-proof-still-needs-a-checked-statement}{%
\subsubsection{CausalSmith: a checked proof still needs a checked
statement}\label{causalsmith-a-checked-proof-still-needs-a-checked-statement}}

CausalSmith combines a Lean library with proposal, formalization, proof
and presentation stages. Its paper reports 8,179 declarations and a
catalog of 144 runs: 14 accepted, 59 downgraded and 71 failed. Those
counts include reruns as separate entries and exclude a legacy track.
They describe one campaign with changing model versions, not independent
draws from a fixed research-task population. The authors explicitly
acknowledge that research quality ratings lack independent human
validation and that the error rate of their LLM statement-match audit is
unknown. \citep{exec13_census_causalsmith}

The source's most useful distinction is between checking a proof against
a formal statement and checking whether that statement expresses the
intended claim. A compiled artifact can assume a hard step as an axiom,
weaken a conclusion, strengthen an assumption or make a predicate
vacuous. The paper describes mechanical scans and dependency checks
alongside language-model statement review. These are complementary
checks with different assurances. The latter does not acquire a formal
guarantee merely by sitting next to a proof checker.

For a proposed bank-effect theorem, the statement record should expose
the unit, intervention, estimand, time ordering, conditioning
information, positivity and dependence assumptions. The proof
environment should bind the toolchain, imported definitions and axioms.
A separate review should compare the English claim with that exact
formal statement and test whether its assumptions are satisfiable in the
intended model. A theorem conditional on observed confounders cannot be
presented as solving unmeasured confounding in operational data. Formal
correctness, semantic fidelity and scientific relevance each need their
own evidence.

The near-term reuse choice is therefore selective. Retain typed graph
memory, explicit intermediate state, preserved failures, and formal
statement/dependency records as design candidates. Defer executable
adoption of these newly inspected systems until exact code,
dependencies, licenses and relevant numerical or proof paths have been
reviewed. This permits a concrete prototype architecture now without
claiming that paper descriptions have already been integrated or
independently reproduced.

\label{exec13:census-agents-end}

\chapter{What additional information buys}
\label{integrated:master_execution}

\begin{quote}\small
A causal banking service must return a decision quantity together with the information and uncertainty that make it defensible. Funding responses, sequential servicing, temporal relationships and verified customer histories reveal different limits on that information. A funding experiment uses supplied action randomization and independent calendars to remove a fitted-ratio mean shift. A nonlinear servicing extension evaluates a fixed observable policy using truthful state audits and supplied action probabilities. Both meet a preregistered minimum-coverage screen on selected synthetic grids with conservative 99\% critical values. A joint pair/calendar/gold-label experiment still fails finite calibration in important regimes. A corrected temporal graph union retains effects but can return the whole real line. A corrected sparse learner fails qualification at higher dimension or support. Full linked-outcome streaming agrees with its dense reference and survives real local process failures, without a consistent measured performance gain. These are research findings from specified experiments. Their use in a bank requires independent review, credible assignment and observation information, suitable operating performance and a defensible economic case.
\end{quote}

\section{One decision, several kinds of evidence}
A bank deciding whether to raise a deposit rate, change a collections policy or act on a discovered relationship needs a target with units and timing. It also needs an observation model: a row may not identify the customer whose balance matters; a public signal may omit the private state used by a historical decision maker; an apparent edge may permit several intervention effects. Computation cannot supply missing identity, assignment or exclusion information.

The experiments ask whether changing the available information improves
a stated banking comparison. A negative result can explain which information
is missing. An uncertainty set can be statistically defensible yet too wide
to distinguish a profitable action from a loss. Scientific validity and
useful precision therefore need separate attention.

Every table cell has 512 fresh Monte Carlo requests. Covers uses all requests, including refusals. MC lower is a simultaneous one-sided exact-binomial 95\% lower bound, Bonferroni-adjusted over all method/cell comparisons in the study. The minimum screen is .95. These screens do not prove uniform coverage or validate supplied scientific assumptions. Primary methods use frozen 99\% critical values or covariance regions; some challengers use 95\% critical values. Width and coverage have a disclosed tradeoff.

\section{Funding: change information to remove an error}
\subsection{Target, linked audits and pilot bias}
The target is a one-month ten-basis-point increase over $H=6$ future months. With two equally weighted strata,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 V&=\tfrac12(\theta_0+\theta_1)-C,\qquad \theta_s=w'\beta_s,\\
 w_h&=48\cdot10^6\{.002(.99)^h-(.001/12)1\{h=0\}\},\quad C=400{,}000.
\end{aligned}
\]
A balance unit is USD one million and the synthetic account has 48 branches. Future margin is discounted once. Response $2(.82)^h$ gives approximately USD 375,149; persistence .96 gives USD 751,749. These are reproducible accounts, not bank profits.

Let $F_t$ be the focal response and $Y_{t1},Y_{t2}$ candidate histories. A truthful identity audit $R_t$ has known inclusion $q_t>0$. Conditional on complete histories $\mathcal H$, assume $\E[R_t\mid\mathcal H]=q_t$ and set
\[
 B_t=(Y_{t1}+Y_{t2})/2,\qquad Z_t=B_t+R_t(F_t-B_t)/q_t.
\]
Then $\E[Z_t\mid\mathcal H]=F_t$, without division by identity rank $2p_s-1$. Each origin audit resolves a horizon vector, not seven independent labels. Truthful links are additional information beyond correctness counts.

For the inherited independent-pilot ratio, define $d_m=\widehat m-m$ and $d_\ell=\widehat\ell-\ell$. With innovation variance one, the conditional population slope is
\[
 \frac{\theta_s+\E[d_md_\ell\mid P]}{1+\E[d_m^2\mid P]}.
\]
A residual calendar variance does not estimate this pilot-dependent mean shift. Orthogonal-score product conditions support a growing-pilot argument \cite{dml2018}; the cited iid result does not prove finite dependent-calendar calibration here.

\subsection{Known randomization and independent calendars}
Suppose the true assignment is supplied as $A=m(X)+v$, with $\E[v\mid X]=0$ and $\E[v^2\mid X]=1$. The synthetic law uses $m(W)=.5W+.2(W^2-1)$. An independent pilot produces an outcome prediction $\widehat\ell$ and scalar control $\widehat b$. Define
\[
 G_t=v_t\{w'Z_t-\widehat\ell(X_t)\}-\widehat b(v_t^2-1).
\]
Conditional on the pilot, $\E[v\widehat\ell(X)]=0$ and $\E[v^2-1]=0$. Exogeneity and truthful inclusion give $\E[G_t\mid P]=\theta$. The pilot affects variance, but not the mean. The fitted-action error and ratio denominator disappear because assignment information is supplied. The study has equally sampled strata and a common response; unequal sampling would need explicit weights.

With $K$ independent calendars and $L$ consecutive origins each, let $U_k=L^{-1}\sum_tG_{kt}$. Then
\[
 \widehat V=K^{-1}\sum_k U_k-C,\qquad
 \widehat s^2=\frac1{K(K-1)}\sum_k(U_k-\overline U)^2.
\]
The variance contains all within-calendar covariance. Its conditional mean is constant, so no pilot-dependent mean variance is omitted. An iid-calendar CLT as $K\to\infty$ justifies the limit; Student critical values are asymptotically equivalent, not exact pivots for these non-Gaussian means.

The frozen design has $K=24$, $L=50$ (12 for the short cell), a fourfold pilot and 99\% Student intervals. Adjacent blocks of one bank series are not independent calendars, nor are branches sharing a national shock. This requirement has real feasibility and cost implications.

Table widths are USD. The challenger is the inherited stacked-calendar ratio using a 95\% interval.

reflects that design, its estimator and its more conservative critical value.

False exogeneity, wrong inclusion and label errors fail visibly. Wider critical values cannot repair those population errors. This is a scoped added-information route, not a universal correction or evidence that the bank can acquire independent economic calendars.

\section{Persistent maps, common dates and imperfect gold truth}
\subsection{One joint sampling law}
After multiplying outcomes by randomized signed actions, let focal and companion responses be
\[
 F_{it}=\beta+U_i+C_t+E_{it},\qquad D_{it}=\delta+V_i+C_t+J_{it}.
\]
Pair effects are iid across pairs; $C_t$ is an independent stationary Gaussian AR(1); cell disturbances are independent. Candidate order persists within a pair. A Bernoulli pair audit $R_i$ has known $q$, and its label independently flips with probability $e<1/2$. An independent representative sample of $M$ gold labels estimates $e$. This is a specific experiment, not arbitrary multiway dependence.

Let $\xi_i=1$ for a correct audit label and $-1$ for a flipped label. At the true $e$, $W_i=R_i\xi_i/[q(1-2e)]$ has mean one and second moment $a=1/[q(1-2e)^2]$. For $d=(\beta-\delta)/2$, the corrected score has decomposition
\begin{align*}
 Z_{it}&=\beta+P_i+C_t+H_{it},\\
 P_i&=(U_i+V_i)/2+W_i(U_i-V_i)/2+d(W_i-1),\\
 H_{it}&=(E_{it}+J_{it})/2+W_i(E_{it}-J_{it})/2.
\end{align*}
Pair and cell projections are uncorrelated. With pair variance $\sigma_p^2$ and cell variance $\sigma_e^2$,
\[
 \Var(P)=\sigma_p^2(1+a)/2+d^2(a-1),\quad
 \Var(H)=\sigma_e^2(1+a)/2.
\]
Thus the known-error variance of the mean is
\[
 \frac{\Var(P)}N+\frac{\sigma_c^2}{T^2}\left[T+2\sum_{k=1}^{T-1}(T-k)\rho^k\right]+\frac{\Var(H)}{NT}.
\]
Gold estimation adds $g^2e(1-e)/M$ at first order, $g=(\beta-\delta)/(1-2e)$. Curvature and random-derivative terms require a fixed rank margin and comparable pair/date/gold growth; their constants diverge near $e=.5$.

Persistent audits contribute to pair variance and cannot be averaged away merely by adding dates. Independent origin audits instead add a diagonal cell component. At $q=1,e=0$ the expression reduces to complete truth. Binary enumeration and direct Toeplitz covariance sums independently check the limits.

\subsection{Feasible precision still fails}
Row-mean variance and date HAC each count cell interaction. Subtracting its double-demeaned estimate once addresses that duplication under this law. It is not a generic dependent-panel repair. Rank uncertainty can cause refusal; Bartlett calendar variance remains biased at high finite persistence.

The reported monetary target is $1000\beta$ USD; interval widths are USD. The challenger retains the inherited double-counted interaction and a 95\% critical value.

\section{Nonlinear servicing with a supplied private logger}
\subsection{State, signal, action and reward}
The selected17 extension adds a nonlinear action reward to the inherited action-variance family:
\begin{align*}
 S_{t+1}&=\rho S_t+\gamma\tanh(S_t)+bA_t+\sqrt{q_{A_t}}\epsilon_{t+1},\\
 O_t&=S_t+\sqrt{v_o}\nu_t,\\
 p_t(1\mid S_t,O_t)&=.05+.9\operatorname{logistic}(\lambda_0+\lambda_sS_t+\lambda_oO_t),\\
 R_t&=\eta_0+\eta_sS_t+\eta_aA_t+\eta_{sa}S_tA_t+
 \eta_{\tanh}A_t\tanh(S_t)+\sqrt{v_R}\zeta_t.
\end{align*}
The private state precedes signal, historical action and reward. A deployed policy observes $O_t$, not $S_t$. Representative truthful full-state audits fix state scale/orientation; logger probabilities are actual supplied records. With full support and positive action probabilities, the transition/reward regressors are linearly independent and their Gaussian conditional laws identify this finite family. A noisy audit or guessed logger is a different experiment.

The complete likelihood multiplies initial, observation, Bernoulli action, reward and transition densities. Hidden-state likelihood fitting remains an efficiency alternative; this estimator uses extra logger information instead. Mechanism replacement supplies the intervention interpretation \cite{pearl2009}; the new numerical/inferential composition is project work.

\subsection{Sequential weighting and uncertainty}
For a policy chosen independently of evaluation,
\[
 W_t=\prod_{j\le t}\frac{1\{A_j=\pi_j(O_j)\}}{p_j(A_j\mid S_j,O_j)},\qquad
 V(\pi)=1000\E\left[\sum_{t=0}^2.97^t W_tR_t\right].
\]
Integrating each historical action cancels its denominator and replaces that action by the policy. This sequential change of measure covers the nonlinear transition and reward under the supplied true logger. It remains valid with a misspecified parametric transition if logger and audit truth remain correct.

One trajectory contributes one discounted weighted reward. Its sample variance retains within-path dependence. The fixed horizon and probability floor bound weights by $.05^{-3}$; Gaussian moments give finite variance. The trajectory CLT motivates 99\% Student intervals, not an exact finite $t$ law. Poor overlap can still make convergence slow. Thresholds $(0,.2,.4)$ are independently frozen; no unknown optimal value is inferred.

\section{Temporal discovery: retain the class before answering}
\subsection{A stationary finite temporal law}
Let $X_t=(Z_t,A_t,Y_t)'$ satisfy
\[
 X_t=rX_{t-1}+\epsilon_t,\qquad r\in\{0,.4,.8\},
\]
with invariant Gaussian initialization and iid innovations. Innovation structure is
\[
 z=e_z,\qquad a=kz+l_au+e_a,\qquad y=\tau a+cz+l_yu+e_y.
\]
The latent root and errors are independent. The instantaneous intervention coefficient is $\tau$. In structural form the lag matrix is $r(I-B)$: a real restriction, not an arbitrary VAR. Unknown continuous lag and long-run interventions are different questions.

For every candidate $r$, form $E_t(r)=X_t-rX_{t-1}$. At the true candidate these are iid Gaussian innovations. Nine simultaneous variance bands---three coordinate variances and six signed pair sums/differences---give covariance inclusion by chi-square inversion and Bonferroni. Propagate each covariance box through all compatible graphs and union over all lag candidates.

Only inclusion at the true candidate is needed. Wrong-lag data need not be iid, and no selected lag is falsely treated as fixed. The finite innovation classes contain the inherited 40 broad latent structures or eight encouragement/sufficiency structures per lag. Graphs are removed only when necessary restrictions cannot intersect their covariance region. On true-law inclusion the true graph and effect survive.

With valid encouragement exclusion, $c=0$ and the latent root does not cause $Z$, so $\Cov(Z,Y)/\Cov(Z,A)=\tau$. Interval ratio propagation imposes no positive first-stage floor and preserves disconnected or unbounded sets. Broad latent models admit equal-covariance witnesses with arbitrary effect, giving $\R$. Extra scientific information must exclude those alternatives; selecting a convenient graph does not.

Widths are outcome/action units, conditional on finite returned sets. The challenger selects one lag before propagating its graph class.

\section{A learner whose code matches its argument}
The residualized IV score is
\[
 \E[(Z-m_Z(X))\{Y-m_Y(X)-\theta(A-m_A(X))\}]=0.
\]
Independent-training nuisance errors shift the conditional moment by $\E[\delta_Z(\delta_Y-\theta\delta_A)]$. This is the inherited orthogonal-score principle \cite{dml2018}; dependent separation and actual selection need their own proof.

The corrected procedure has two outer calendar blocks separated by a gap. Inside each training block a further separated split selects a shrinking lasso grid. Inner training controls standardization; selected models are refit using only outer training data. Evaluation labels never tune penalties. Bartlett products stay within evaluation folds, never across the omitted gap. Actual feature/support overrides are honored.

For fixed dimension, a correct linear nuisance, positive Gram eigenvalues and fixed geometric mixing give root-sample moment/coefficient rates. A finite shrinking grid preserves that rate, including at selection boundaries. Products are then second order. A sufficiently increasing gap and growing covariance window supply a conditional asymptotic route. Growing dimension additionally needs restricted-eigenvalue and approximation/product-rate control. Prediction accuracy alone proves none of these. The grid has 20 or 60 controls, support three or eight, 640 origins and ordinarily a 40-origin gap.

Widths are outcome/action units. The challenger fits an unpenalized dense reference on the same permitted training folds.
