The selected Gaussian failures here retain their original scope and outcomes.

~~~text
\section{Keeping uncertainty visible in the reported result}
Each A-D result carries actual bounds or a refusal reason, units, assumptions and capability disposition. Finite intervals, disconnected sets, whole lines, empty sets and unavailable computations remain distinct. Computed sets without bounds reject. Null endpoints denote infinity only in the explicit extended-real schema, never zero or absent evidence.

The full linked method streams both pilot and evaluation pseudo-outcomes. Chronological pilot halves are compressed into augmented QR factors and online target moments. Validation uses the same fixed penalty losses, followed by full-pilot refit; bounded passes then compute estimates and covariance. Twelve dense-equivalence cases span chunks 1/37/257, low audit, identity rank and persistence. Relative tolerance $10^{-9}$ and absolute USD $10^{-6}$ assess numerical equivalence, not bank usefulness.

Complete workloads include input generation, tuning/refit, inference, serialization and total process memory. At 120,000 evaluation and 480,000 pilot origins, dense and streamed runs take about 1.08 and 1.71 seconds, with roughly 409 MiB peak RSS each. The streaming fit is slower. Input generation dominates memory; reduced auxiliary storage does not imply a large total RSS reduction. No consistent performance advantage is claimed, and a dense fallback is retained.

Recovery binds code/input hashes, seed and request count. Local locking, fsync, atomic record rename and a final manifest prevent partial publication. Real process deaths during fitting, a partially written checkpoint and final publication recover the same 12 requests on restart, replay without duplication and reject changed identities. This is local single-process evidence; multi-host coordination and bank service levels need their platform operators.

\section{Financial value and unresolved evidence}
If $\Delta L$ is held-out improvement in bank decision loss over an accepted workflow, then
\[
 \mathrm{Net\ value}=\Delta L-C_{\rm audit}-C_{\rm calendar}-C_{\rm integration}
 -C_{\rm compute}-C_{\rm review}-C_{\rm operation}.
\]
The research supplies synthetic precision and local computing measurements, not bank values for these costs. Linked histories, correctness labels and full-state audits are different services. A label count is not a market price; a faster fit is not ROI. Width, availability and decision loss need matched information and actual prices.

Verified customer histories provide a restricted way to learn funding
responses, and the nonlinear servicing study supports one specified policy
comparison. Several causal graphs can still fit the same observations.
Assignment, audit inclusion and label accuracy require substantive evidence.
Joint dependence and high-dimensional learning retain adverse findings, while
local computing results do not establish bank operating performance. Useful
precision and the full financial case depend on the institution and decision.

A bank study would need the relevant decision makers and data owners
to establish assignment rules, observation quality, required precision and
costs. The information requested should be specific to the proposed study.

\section*{Evidence and reading guide}
The five current studies contain 22,528 final requests: 4,608 funding, 5,632 joint dependence and 4,096 each for servicing, corrected graph inference and corrected learning. Another 4,096 earlier learner requests remain exploratory. Complete journals reconstruct saved summaries; 15 first/middle/last representative requests are regenerated. Twenty-five master-control tests pass.

Primary texts support only stated inherited roles. New derivations, fixtures, synthetic outcomes and engineering measurements remain project evidence. Genuine local PDFs, source versions/hashes, inspected anchors and claim limits are recorded in the release audit. Literature coverage retains the 7 October 2026 cutoff; no exhaustive new search is claimed. Process corrections and exact continuation steps are in the companion review.

The selected experiments establish both useful information designs
and adverse findings. They motivate a restricted prototype; they do not
establish performance or financial returns for an adopting bank.

\section*{From research output to a bounded bank decision}
A deployment question must first specify the unit, decision time, available records and loss from a wrong action. The funding construction requires certified randomization and link inclusion, plus independent calendars whose economic shocks do not overlap. If those inputs cannot be supplied, its calibrated synthetic interval is not a substitute for a bank answer. The servicing construction requires a frozen observable policy, truthful representative state audits and the actual historical action probabilities; otherwise the reported fixed-policy value has a different target or can be severely biased.

For discovery, a bank must specify the scientific restrictions that remove observationally equivalent intervention effects. If its accepted restrictions still permit the whole real line, the service should return that set and withhold a directional recommendation. For shared calendars and dependent learning, the present finite failures require a new variance design or stronger information before qualification. A platform may transmit these limitations faithfully, but cannot turn them into positive scientific evidence.

Finally, independent reviewers must reconstruct each claimed regime and bank owners must measure useful precision, decision loss and complete acquisition and operating costs. Only a bounded release meeting those conditions should enter an institutional acceptance and investment decision. An adverse scientific or economic conclusion is a legitimate output of this program.
~~~

~~~text
A causal banking service must return a decision quantity together with the information and uncertainty that make it defensible. \section{One decision, several kinds of evidence}
A bank deciding whether to raise a deposit rate, change a collections policy or act on a discovered relationship needs a target with units and timing. It also needs an observation model: a row may not identify the customer whose balance matters; a public signal may omit the private state used by a historical decision maker; an apparent edge may permit several intervention effects. Computation cannot supply missing identity, assignment or exclusion information.

The experiments ask whether changing the available information improves
a stated banking comparison. A negative result can explain which information
is missing. An uncertainty set can be statistically defensible yet too wide
to distinguish a profitable action from a loss. Scientific validity and
useful precision therefore need separate attention.

Every table cell has 512 fresh Monte Carlo requests. Covers uses all requests, including refusals. MC lower is a simultaneous one-sided exact-binomial 95\% lower bound, Bonferroni-adjusted over all method/cell comparisons in the study. The minimum screen is .95. These screens do not prove uniform coverage or validate supplied scientific assumptions. Primary methods use frozen 99\% critical values or covariance regions; some challengers use 95\% critical values. Width and coverage have a disclosed tradeoff.

\section{Persistent maps, common dates and imperfect gold truth}
\subsection{One joint sampling law}
After multiplying outcomes by randomized signed actions, let focal and companion responses be
\[
 F_{it}=\beta+U_i+C_t+E_{it},\qquad D_{it}=\delta+V_i+C_t+J_{it}.

Pair effects are iid across pairs; $C_t$ is an independent stationary Gaussian AR(1); cell disturbances are independent. Candidate order persists within a pair. A Bernoulli pair audit $R_i$ has known $q$, and its label independently flips with probability $e<1/2$. An independent representative sample of $M$ gold labels estimates $e$. This is a specific experiment, not arbitrary multiway dependence.

Let $\xi_i=1$ for a correct audit label and $-1$ for a flipped label. At the true $e$, $W_i=R_i\xi_i/[q(1-2e)]$ has mean one and second moment $a=1/[q(1-2e)^2]$. For $d=(\beta-\delta)/2$, the corrected score has decomposition
\begin{align*}
 Z_{it}&=\beta+P_i+C_t+H_{it},\\
 P_i&=(U_i+V_i)/2+W_i(U_i-V_i)/2+d(W_i-1),\\

\end{align*}
Pair and cell projections are uncorrelated. With pair variance $\sigma_p^2$ and cell variance $\sigma_e^2$,
\[
 \Var(P)=\sigma_p^2(1+a)/2+d^2(a-1),\quad
 \Var(H)=\sigma_e^2(1+a)/2.
\]
Thus the known-error variance of the mean is
\[
 \frac{\Var(P)}N+\frac{\sigma_c^2}{T^2}\left[T+2\sum_{k=1}^{T-1}(T-k)\rho^k\right]+\frac{\Var(H)}{NT}.
\]
Gold estimation adds $g^2e(1-e)/M$ at first order, $g=(\beta-\delta)/(1-2e)$. Curvature and random-derivative terms require a fixed rank margin and comparable pair/date/gold growth; their constants diverge near $e=.5$.

Persistent audits contribute to pair variance and cannot be averaged away merely by adding dates. Independent origin audits instead add a diagonal cell component. At $q=1,e=0$ the expression reduces to complete truth. Binary enumeration and direct Toeplitz covariance sums independently check the limits.

\section{Temporal discovery: retain the class before answering}
\subsection{A stationary finite temporal law}
Let $X_t=(Z_t,A_t,Y_t)'$ satisfy
\[

\]

\[
 z=e_z,\qquad a=kz+l_au+e_a,\qquad y=\tau a+cz+l_yu+e_y.
\]
The latent root and errors are independent. The instantaneous intervention coefficient is $\tau$. In structural form the lag matrix is $r(I-B)$: a real restriction, not an arbitrary VAR. Unknown continuous lag and long-run interventions are different questions.

For every candidate $r$, form $E_t(r)=X_t-rX_{t-1}$. At the true candidate these are iid Gaussian innovations. Nine simultaneous variance bands---three coordinate variances and six signed pair sums/differences---give covariance inclusion by chi-square inversion and Bonferroni. Propagate each covariance box through all compatible graphs and union over all lag candidates.

Only inclusion at the true candidate is needed. Wrong-lag data need not be iid, and no selected lag is falsely treated as fixed. The finite innovation classes contain the inherited 40 broad latent structures or eight encouragement/sufficiency structures per lag. Graphs are removed only when necessary restrictions cannot intersect their covariance region. On true-law inclusion the true graph and effect survive.

With valid encouragement exclusion, $c=0$ and the latent root does not cause $Z$, so $\Cov(Z,Y)/\Cov(Z,A)=\tau$. Interval ratio propagation imposes no positive first-stage floor and preserves disconnected or unbounded sets. Broad latent models admit equal-covariance witnesses with arbitrary effect, giving $\R$. Extra scientific information must exclude those alternatives; selecting a convenient graph does not.

\section{A learner whose code matches its argument}
The residualized IV score is
\[

Independent-training nuisance errors shift the conditional moment by $\E[\delta_Z(\delta_Y-\theta\delta_A)]$. This is the inherited orthogonal-score principle \citep{dml2018}; dependent separation and actual selection need their own proof.

The corrected procedure has two outer calendar blocks separated by a gap. Inside each training block a further separated split selects a shrinking lasso grid. Inner training controls standardization; selected models are refit using only outer training data. Evaluation labels never tune penalties. Bartlett products stay within evaluation folds, never across the omitted gap. Actual feature/support overrides are honored.

For fixed dimension, a correct linear nuisance, positive Gram eigenvalues and fixed geometric mixing give root-sample moment/coefficient rates. A finite shrinking grid preserves that rate, including at selection boundaries. Products are then second order. A sufficiently increasing gap and growing covariance window supply a conditional asymptotic route. Growing dimension additionally needs restricted-eigenvalue and approximation/product-rate control. Prediction accuracy alone proves none of these. The grid has 20 or 60 controls, support three or eight, 640 origins and ordinarily a 40-origin gap.

Baseline, long gap and persistence pass. Higher dimension (.9491) and larger support (.9339) miss the .95 lower-bound rule. A failed screen prevents qualification but is not a universal undercoverage theorem. Nonlinear omitted nuisances cover zero targets. Weak IV gives median width 3.836 against true effect 1.2; a small-denominator guard is not weak-IV inference.

An independent constrained convex solver checks lasso, exact soft thresholding checks a selection boundary, and separate matrix algebra checks dense fitted-score covariance. Earlier evaluation-tuned requests remain preserved as exploratory and do not support this corrected argument. Next routes are independent-pilot covariance control, high-dimensional rates, richer prespecified nuisance bases and weak-IV test inversion. Chapter~\ref{exec13:dependent-pilot} develops explicit pilot-error and weak-instrument bounds for a different bounded, finite-dependent law, then assesses their precision before a larger experiment. The selected Gaussian failures here retain their original scope and outcomes.

\section{Keeping uncertainty visible in the reported result}
Each A-D result carries actual bounds or a refusal reason, units, assumptions and capability disposition. Finite intervals, disconnected sets, whole lines, empty sets and unavailable computations remain distinct. Computed sets without bounds reject. Null endpoints denote infinity only in the explicit extended-real schema, never zero or absent evidence.

The full linked method streams both pilot and evaluation pseudo-outcomes. Chronological pilot halves are compressed into augmented QR factors and online target moments. Validation uses the same fixed penalty losses, followed by full-pilot refit; bounded passes then compute estimates and covariance. Twelve dense-equivalence cases span chunks 1/37/257, low audit, identity rank and persistence. Relative tolerance $10^{-9}$ and absolute USD $10^{-6}$ assess numerical equivalence, not bank usefulness.

Complete workloads include input generation, tuning/refit, inference, serialization and total process memory. At 120,000 evaluation and 480,000 pilot origins, dense and streamed runs take about 1.08 and 1.71 seconds, with roughly 409 MiB peak RSS each. The streaming fit is slower. Input generation dominates memory; reduced auxiliary storage does not imply a large total RSS reduction. No consistent performance advantage is claimed, and a dense fallback is retained.

Recovery binds code/input hashes, seed and request count. Local locking, fsync, atomic record rename and a final manifest prevent partial publication. Real process deaths during fitting, a partially written checkpoint and final publication recover the same 12 requests on restart, replay without duplication and reject changed identities. This is local single-process evidence; multi-host coordination and bank service levels need their platform operators.

\section{Financial value and unresolved evidence}
If $\Delta L$ is held-out improvement in bank decision loss over an accepted workflow, then
\[
 \mathrm{Net\ value}=\Delta L-C_{\rm audit}-C_{\rm calendar}-C_{\rm integration}
 -C_{\rm compute}-C_{\rm review}-C_{\rm operation}.
\]
The research supplies synthetic precision and local computing measurements, not bank values for these costs. Linked histories, correctness labels and full-state audits are different services. A label count is not a market price; a faster fit is not ROI. Width, availability and decision loss need matched information and actual prices.

Verified customer histories provide a restricted way to learn funding
responses, and the nonlinear servicing study supports one specified policy
comparison. Several causal graphs can still fit the same observations.
Assignment, audit inclusion and label accuracy require substantive evidence.
Joint dependence and high-dimensional learning retain adverse findings, while
local computing results do not establish bank operating performance. Useful
precision and the full financial case depend on the institution and decision.

A bank study would need the relevant decision makers and data owners
to establish assignment rules, observation quality, required precision and
costs. The information requested should be specific to the proposed study.

\section*{Evidence and reading guide}
The five current studies contain 22,528 final requests: 4,608 funding, 5,632 joint dependence and 4,096 each for servicing, corrected graph inference and corrected learning. Another 4,096 earlier learner requests remain exploratory. Complete journals reconstruct saved summaries; 15 first/middle/last representative requests are regenerated. Twenty-five master-control tests pass.

Primary texts support only stated inherited roles. New derivations, fixtures, synthetic outcomes and engineering measurements remain project evidence. Genuine local PDFs, source versions/hashes, inspected anchors and claim limits are recorded in the release audit. Literature coverage retains the 7 October 2026 cutoff; no exhaustive new search is claimed. Process corrections and exact continuation steps are in the companion review.

The selected experiments establish both useful information designs
and adverse findings. They motivate a restricted prototype; they do not
establish performance or financial returns for an adopting bank.

\section*{From research output to a bounded bank decision}
A deployment question must first specify the unit, decision time, available records and loss from a wrong action. The funding construction requires certified randomization and link inclusion, plus independent calendars whose economic shocks do not overlap. If those inputs cannot be supplied, its calibrated synthetic interval is not a substitute for a bank answer. The servicing construction requires a frozen observable policy, truthful representative state audits and the actual historical action probabilities; otherwise the reported fixed-policy value has a different target or can be severely biased.

For discovery, a bank must specify the scientific restrictions that remove observationally equivalent intervention effects. If its accepted restrictions still permit the whole real line, the service should return that set and withhold a directional recommendation. For shared calendars and dependent learning, the present finite failures require a new variance design or stronger information before qualification. A platform may transmit these limitations faithfully, but cannot turn them into positive scientific evidence.

Finally, independent reviewers must reconstruct each claimed regime and bank owners must measure useful precision, decision loss and complete acquisition and operating costs. Only a bounded release meeting those conditions should enter an institutional acceptance and investment decision. An adverse scientific or economic conclusion is a legitimate output of this program.
~~~

~~~text
\section{A complete translation example: the incentive question}
\label{v13:la-dose}

Suppose a manager asks an agent to ``find the incentive uplift and choose the
best offer.'' The sentence leaves at least three mathematical objects open:
a binary offer effect, a continuous local slope, and a finite-dose policy value.
The agent can help by presenting these alternatives with their populations,
units and action constraints. It should not select whichever object happens
to be exposed by the first available package.

Let $A$ be incentive intensity in a declared unit and let $Y$ be retained net
value over a fixed horizon. The finite question is
$\Delta(a_1,a_0)=\mathbb E\{Y(a_1)-Y(a_0)\}$. A local derivative, where it
exists, is $\mu'(a)$. A covariance slope averages features of the response
under an exposure distribution and need not equal either object. The inspected
grf and dose-response interfaces make this a practical interoperability issue,
not merely a linguistic distinction. \cite{v13_sw_grf,v13_sw_causaldrf}

For the stipulated curve $\mu(a)=20a-3a^2$, a uniform exposure on $[0,2]$
gives covariance slope 14, while moving from dose one to dose two changes the
mean by 11 CNY. An agent that labels 14 as the value of the specified change
has mistranslated the problem even if it calls its numerical tool correctly.
The exact project calculation makes the error detectable without a live model
experiment. \cite{v13_project_exact}

A useful translation record would therefore state: eligible existing customers;
the information available before the offer; current dose one and feasible dose
two; a fixed retention horizon; treatment and outcome currency units; and
whether incentive expense is already included in $Y$. If expense is excluded,
the decision value is $\Delta(a_1,a_0)-\{c(a_1)-c(a_0)\}$. Subtracting it again
when $Y$ already measures net value would double-count cost. The record also
needs account closure/default definitions and a sampling unit for uncertainty.

The agent's role can be useful at each handoff. It can flag unspecified units,
find source definitions, propose alternative causal questions and generate
typed requests. Formal checks can verify that a numerical result matches the
declared query. Domain owners must still confirm the feasible intervention and
measurement meanings; neither fluent prose nor a schema establishes them.

\section{A servicing policy is a rule with an information boundary}

For sequential servicing, an action rule uses $H_t$, the information actually
available at decision time. A data field recorded later may describe an earlier
event while remaining unavailable to the operating policy. An agent assembling
history features must preserve both event and availability times. Otherwise
the proposed policy uses information the bank would not possess when acting.

The causal query should distinguish evaluating a specified rule, choosing among
rules and claiming an optimal hidden-state policy. A longitudinal simulator can
evaluate supplied regimes under its assumptions. Its ability to accept a custom
history function does not identify private customer states or make an unknown
logger known. The inspected pygformula class exposes useful histories, event
and regime options, but its source interface alone establishes neither policy
optimality nor uncertainty under arbitrary dependence. \cite{v13_sw_pygformula}

A concrete policy-selection hazard can be shown without an asymptotic argument.
Suppose two equally valuable policies each have independent evaluation error
equal to minus one or plus one with equal probability. The maximum of the two
errors is minus one only when both are minus one, and plus one otherwise.
Its expectation is therefore $\tfrac34-\tfrac14=\tfrac12$. Reporting the
selected policy's same-data evaluation is optimistic. If the selected policy
is evaluated with a fresh independent error of mean zero, the evaluation error
has mean zero conditional on the selection. Exact enumeration verifies both
claims. \cite{v13_project_exact}

This example does not prove that a particular split is sufficient for a
dependent servicing panel. It explains why the selection and evaluation laws
must be specified. An agent can preserve the split, freeze candidate rules and
refuse reuse of a held-out set for tuning. A scientific argument must still
justify independence or the required dependence control. Training a policy
and then narrating its favorable development score is not an independent
evaluation.

\section{Translation outputs that deserve abstention}

Some business questions should produce a request for more information or a set
of alternatives. If ``the customer'' may mean the legal entity, the beneficial
owner or a linked household, choosing one silently changes both the population
and interference structure. If the intended action is not operationally
feasible, the mathematically optimal action is irrelevant. If the loss function
and costs are unknown, the agent can compare statistical targets but cannot
assert an investment recommendation.

Abstention should be specific. It should identify the missing definition,
record the alternative interpretations and explain which downstream operation
depends on the answer. That is different from a generic refusal to analyze.
For an incentive query, the missing item may be treatment units or whether
cost is already included. For servicing it may be the information clock or
the policy class. For interference it may be network direction or the allocation
policy. These are concrete commitments that owners can resolve and numerical
tools can then preserve.
~~~

~~~text
\chapter{What language models contribute to causal knowledge}
\label{la:frontier}

Section~\ref{scisyn:assistance} gives the principal recommendation for language
assistance. This chapter develops its evidential basis. It first distinguishes
knowledge, formal reasoning, mechanism proposals and workflow support, then
asks how published evaluations transfer to a banking decision. Exact examples
show how task mixtures, shared errors and unresolved causal models can change
that decision. The final comparisons examine consistency judges, orchestration,
literature extraction and the design of a versioned assistance experiment.

\section{Four different questions about cause and effect}

A banker asking why deposit balances fell can be asking for an explanation of
a recorded event, an estimate of a feasible rate intervention, a prediction of
next month's balance, or a diagnosis of an observation error. A fluent answer
can move between these objects without announcing the change. Evaluating assistance therefore starts by distinguishing the task: a proposed scientific question, evidence about a causal model,
a formal calculation conditional on that model, or a recommendation under a
specified loss. Success on one task does not establish success on the others.

The early frontier argument proposes using language models to organize domain
knowledge, draft graphs, critique assumptions and suggest robustness analyses.
It also records the ability to reproduce recognizable public data and
distinguishes transforming known information from discovering a new causal
structure. \cite{v12_la_2305_00050} This distinction is particularly consequential
in banking. A familiar statement about interest rates can be useful prior
knowledge, but the effect of a particular bank's deposit offer depends on its
population, competitors, eligibility rules and information clock. A remembered
relationship does not determine that intervention effect.

Formal benchmarks introduce a second object. CLadder constructs questions from
known causal structures with different verbalizations. Its results concern
answers to those generated questions, including historically specified models
and prompting methods. \cite{v12_la_2312_04350} Such a benchmark can reveal failures
to distinguish observation from intervention. It cannot establish that a model
elicits the right variables from an unfamiliar bank process, measures them
correctly, or returns calibrated uncertainty after fitting to dependent data.
These are additional stages of the proposed product.

Third, a language model can propose a causal mechanism for numerical analysis.
Model Discovery Agent illustrates a separation between executable mechanism
proposals and numerical fitting, evidence approximation and experiment design.
Its finite predictive evaluations explicitly do not establish causal
identification. \cite{v12_la_2608_09696} A mechanism may predict well because
several observationally equivalent models predict equally well. The bank must
still justify which intervention the model represents and which new experiment
would distinguish economically different mechanisms.

Finally, workflow assistance concerns selection and coordination of established
operations. Causal-learn+ describes assistance with diagnosis, assumptions,
method selection and interpretation while retaining algorithm outputs and
graph ambiguity. \cite{v12_la_2606_23608} This is a useful architectural direction.
It changes the analyst's interaction with numerical tools; it does not make a
method's premises true. The comparisons that follow keep these four contributions
separate while studying how they can work together.

\section{Text supplies a different information channel}

Write $D$ for the observed numerical records, $K$ for inspected documentary or
expert evidence, and $\mathcal M(D,K)$ for the models consistent with the
declared interpretation of both. For target $\psi$, a set-valued answer is
\[
 \Psi(D,K)=\{\psi(M):M\in\mathcal M(D,K)\}.
\]
This notation does not assert that finite data identify the population law or
that a statistical confidence procedure has been supplied. It describes which
models the analysis intends to consider. Statistical uncertainty about the law
must subsequently be propagated through the model set.

Additional reliable knowledge may exclude a model that the observed distribution
alone cannot exclude. A contract establishing that an invitation was randomized,
for example, has a different evidential role from a predictive correlation.
But a model-generated sentence repeating that randomization is common practice
does not establish what happened in the bank's historical process. The analysis
must identify the original source, the relevant population and dates, the
interpretation of its claim, and the person or measurement that supports it.

This also explains why retrieving more documents need not improve discovery.
LACR combines background knowledge, retrieved documents and optional numerical
information, and includes an UNKNOWN response. Its reported retrieval effects
differ across benchmarks, with adverse as well as favorable outcomes.
\cite{v12_la_2402_15301} Retrieval changes $K$; it does not certify $K$. Documents
may concern a different treatment definition, contain an association stated as
a cause, or duplicate the same original assertion. Ten repeated documents are
not ten independent confirmations of an edge.

An appropriate evidence object therefore retains the claim, source passage,
date, domain, units and proposed role. A passage may justify a variable
definition without justifying an arrow. A process document may establish that
one action occurs before another without excluding a common cause. A source
about another bank may suggest a hypothesis while leaving transport assumptions
unresolved. These roles determine the strength with which $K$ can restrict the
model class.

\section{Discovery methods use language judgments in different ways}

Three broad routes recur in the inspected literature: direct graph or relation
prediction, refinement of numerical discoveries, and priors or constraints used
within a search. \cite{v12_la_2402_11068} The distinction matters because it locates
where a wrong assertion enters the calculation.

In direct conditional-independence elicitation, chatPC obtains language-model
judgments from descriptions and context. Its statistical calculation concerns
the proportion of YES/NO model responses. \cite{v12_la_2406_07378} Repeated answers
can measure response variability under a prompt. Without a separate argument,
they are not repeated draws of the bank variables and do not yield a sampling
test of independence in the bank population. A highly stable wrong answer can
therefore be more dangerous than a visibly variable one.

Soft guidance provides a different failure boundary. The inspected CD-UCT
method combines language and mutual-information scores to guide graph search
without excluding otherwise valid DAGs. Language-only priors are not uniformly
beneficial in its reported comparisons. \cite{v12_la_2405_13551} Ancestral-path
constraints can likewise enter through a soft log-prior penalty, with reported
degradation under inaccurate prior information. \cite{v12_la_2306_16902} Softness
leaves room for the numerical criterion to resist the suggestion, but it does
not establish that the final graph probabilities are calibrated.

Hard restrictions can be scientifically appropriate when backed by a genuine
design fact. They are more consequential when inferred from prose: deleting a
candidate model deletes every effect value that only that model permits.
Statistical Causal Prompting converts model outputs into forced, forbidden or
unknown prior knowledge using method-specific mappings. The inspected examples
include failures as well as improvements. \cite{v12_la_2402_01454} The interface
must expose both the original assertion and the conversion rule, so a reviewer
can determine whether a numerical threshold has quietly become a scientific
exclusion.

Noisy language priors can also guide a sequential allocation of questions over
edges while retaining PAG representations. \cite{v12_la_2506_16234} This is closer
to a budgeted information problem than to asking for a finished graph in one
prompt. Its relevance to a bank still depends on whether the supplied knowledge
applies to the observed regime, whether latent structure is represented
correctly, and whether the retained ambiguity survives into the effect query.

\section{Temporal discovery is not a change of vocabulary}

A statement that collections activity affects arrears omits the action time,
available history, response horizon and possible feedback. Expanding a variable
name into a paragraph does not supply these missing indices. A temporal graph
needs explicit time labels and a rule governing contemporaneous edges, lag
limits, hidden histories, stationarity and interventions.

RealTCD combines a language-derived initial adjacency with numerical score
optimization over temporal graphs and intervention targets. Its setup includes
causal sufficiency, a known observational regime, finite lag and a DAG on
unrolled variables; its identification statement has further stated premises.
The inspected real-system assessment lacks a ground-truth DAG and evaluates
selected relationships through expert rules. \cite{v12_la_2404_14786} These
qualifications prevent a graph score from being read as a general guarantee
for a bank's latent, irregularly observed time series.

The Large Causal Models work is an adjacent numerical foundation-model route,
not simply a conversational language-model interface. The inspected model
assumes additive noise, stationarity, no latent confounders and no
contemporaneous effects, and does not detect or correct violations of these
assumptions. \cite{v12_la_2602_18662} Distinguishing the two routes avoids treating
the shared word ``model'' as a common scientific contract. One supplies semantic
proposals; the other learns a temporal mapping under a training distribution
and structural restrictions. Either can be useful within its declared regime.

For sequential servicing, a credible workflow starts with the decision history
and feasible intervention. It then asks whether the discovery output expresses
the required variables and whether a policy effect is identified over every
retained graph. An automatically generated lagged graph cannot resolve
unrecorded private information merely by assigning it a latent-node name.

\section{Interactive systems and agents add a review problem}

CausalChat combines graph suggestions, user editing and numerical updates.
Its small nonexpert study uses a fixed sequence of interfaces.
\cite{v12_la_2410_14146} Such evidence can motivate better interfaces, but it does
not isolate every learning, ordering or expertise effect. The proposed bank
evaluation needs qualified reviewers, an explicit task distribution and a
comparison that records the time and information supplied by people.

Debating agents provide another review structure. MAC uses affirmative,
negative and judge roles; its inspected comparisons also report a competitive
single-agent route for simpler graphs at lower cost. \cite{v12_la_2407_15073}
Several personas can share the same mistaken premise or model knowledge.
Agreement among them is not automatically independent corroboration. Their
usefulness should be measured through detected errors, retained correct
alternatives, decision consequences and total cost.

The oci-agent study instead emphasizes an accountable human principal over
actor/critic workflows and deterministic causal libraries. Its critic can
decline analyses with poor overlap. \cite{v12_la_2607_22443} The relevant outcome
then includes correct refusal and what remains possible for the requested
population. Reporting only completed analyses would hide precisely the
difficult cases in which an agent's judgment matters most.

An evidence-auditing agent faces a similar boundary. ARGUS audits reported
support for assumptions rather than adjudicating their truth. Its retrieval
and abstention tradeoffs and small human-label pilot leave substantial
generalization questions. \cite{v12_la_2609_30867} In banking, an omitted document,
a contradicted assumption and an assumption whose truth is unknown require
different responses. A documentation score should not become an identification
certificate.

\section{An evidence standard for the proposed banking product}

The synthesis supports a modular research program. Language assistance proposes
questions, variables, graph alternatives and evidence links. Formal operations
check declared structures and calculate identified functionals or sets in
supported regimes. Numerical procedures estimate those objects with their own
sampling and approximation arguments. Human and institutional evidence supply
facts about assignment, ownership and feasibility that neither interface can
manufacture.

Each interface needs an explicit refusal or unknown state. A retrieved passage
with the wrong unit should fail target review. A graph class outside a backend's
domain should return unsupported. A valid but uninformative effect set should
remain visible. A conflict between textual and numerical evidence should retain
both sources for investigation instead of selecting whichever yields a cleaner
answer.

CausalDS makes narrated mechanisms, observations and private scoring objects
separate parts of a benchmark, and its results distinguish symbolic answers,
uncertainty, abstention and cost. \cite{v12_la_2607_08093} The proposed evaluation
adopts that separation as a design principle. It does not borrow a published
model score as evidence for the local prototype. The remainder of this chapter
makes the comparison explicit: what must stay fixed for a published score to
support a banking capability, and what can fail when assistance stages are
combined? Later chapters develop translation, diagrams, discovery and workflow.
Empirical claims about a chosen backend still require a declared evaluation
on independent mechanisms.
~~~

~~~text
But a model-generated sentence repeating that randomization is common practice
does not establish what happened in the bank's historical process. The analysis
must identify the original source, the relevant population and dates, the
interpretation of its claim, and the person or measurement that supports it.

This also explains why retrieving more documents need not improve discovery.
LACR combines background knowledge, retrieved documents and optional numerical
information, and includes an UNKNOWN response. Its reported retrieval effects
differ across benchmarks, with adverse as well as favorable outcomes.
\citep{v12_la_2402_15301} Retrieval changes $K$; it does not certify $K$. Documents
may concern a different treatment definition, contain an association stated as
a cause, or duplicate the same original assertion. Ten repeated documents are
not ten independent confirmations of an edge.

An appropriate evidence object therefore retains the claim, source passage,
date, domain, units and proposed role. A passage may justify a variable
definition without justifying an arrow. A process document may establish that
one action occurs before another without excluding a common cause. A source
about another bank may suggest a hypothesis while leaving transport assumptions
unresolved. These roles determine the strength with which $K$ can restrict the
model class.

\section{Discovery methods use language judgments in different ways}

Three broad routes recur in the inspected literature: direct graph or relation
prediction, refinement of numerical discoveries, and priors or constraints used
within a search. \citep{v12_la_2402_11068} The distinction matters because it locates
where a wrong assertion enters the calculation.

In direct conditional-independence elicitation, chatPC obtains language-model
judgments from descriptions and context. Its statistical calculation concerns
the proportion of YES/NO model responses. \citep{v12_la_2406_07378} Repeated answers
can measure response variability under a prompt. Without a separate argument,
they are not repeated draws of the bank variables and do not yield a sampling
test of independence in the bank population. A highly stable wrong answer can
therefore be more dangerous than a visibly variable one.

Soft guidance provides a different failure boundary. The inspected CD-UCT
method combines language and mutual-information scores to guide graph search
without excluding otherwise valid DAGs. Language-only priors are not uniformly
beneficial in its reported comparisons. \citep{v12_la_2405_13551} Ancestral-path
constraints can likewise enter through a soft log-prior penalty, with reported
degradation under inaccurate prior information. \citep{v12_la_2306_16902} Softness
leaves room for the numerical criterion to resist the suggestion, but it does
not establish that the final graph probabilities are calibrated.

Hard restrictions can be scientifically appropriate when backed by a genuine
design fact. They are more consequential when inferred from prose: deleting a
candidate model deletes every effect value that only that model permits.
Statistical Causal Prompting converts model outputs into forced, forbidden or
unknown prior knowledge using method-specific mappings. The inspected examples
include failures as well as improvements. \citep{v12_la_2402_01454} The interface
must expose both the original assertion and the conversion rule, so a reviewer
can determine whether a numerical threshold has quietly become a scientific
exclusion.

Noisy language priors can also guide a sequential allocation of questions over
edges while retaining PAG representations. \citep{v12_la_2506_16234} This is closer
to a budgeted information problem than to asking for a finished graph in one
prompt. Its relevance to a bank still depends on whether the supplied knowledge
applies to the observed regime, whether latent structure is represented
correctly, and whether the retained ambiguity survives into the effect query.

\section{Temporal discovery is not a change of vocabulary}

A statement that collections activity affects arrears omits the action time,
available history, response horizon and possible feedback. Expanding a variable
name into a paragraph does not supply these missing indices. A temporal graph
needs explicit time labels and a rule governing contemporaneous edges, lag
limits, hidden histories, stationarity and interventions.

RealTCD combines a language-derived initial adjacency with numerical score
optimization over temporal graphs and intervention targets. Its setup includes
causal sufficiency, a known observational regime, finite lag and a DAG on
unrolled variables; its identification statement has further stated premises.
The inspected real-system assessment lacks a ground-truth DAG and evaluates
selected relationships through expert rules. \citep{v12_la_2404_14786} These
qualifications prevent a graph score from being read as a general guarantee
for a bank's latent, irregularly observed time series.

The Large Causal Models work is an adjacent numerical foundation-model route,
not simply a conversational language-model interface. The inspected model
assumes additive noise, stationarity, no latent confounders and no
contemporaneous effects, and does not detect or correct violations of these
assumptions. \citep{v12_la_2602_18662} Distinguishing the two routes avoids treating
the shared word ``model'' as a common scientific contract. One supplies semantic
proposals; the other learns a temporal mapping under a training distribution
and structural restrictions. Either can be useful within its declared regime.

For sequential servicing, a credible workflow starts with the decision history
and feasible intervention. It then asks whether the discovery output expresses
the required variables and whether a policy effect is identified over every
retained graph. An automatically generated lagged graph cannot resolve
unrecorded private information merely by assigning it a latent-node name.

\section{Interactive systems and agents add a review problem}

CausalChat combines graph suggestions, user editing and numerical updates.
Its small nonexpert study uses a fixed sequence of interfaces.
\citep{v12_la_2410_14146} Such evidence can motivate better interfaces, but it does
not isolate every learning, ordering or expertise effect. The proposed bank
evaluation needs qualified reviewers, an explicit task distribution and a
comparison that records the time and information supplied by people.

Debating agents provide another review structure. MAC uses affirmative,
negative and judge roles; its inspected comparisons also report a competitive
single-agent route for simpler graphs at lower cost. \citep{v12_la_2407_15073}
Several personas can share the same mistaken premise or model knowledge.
Agreement among them is not automatically independent corroboration. Their
usefulness should be measured through detected errors, retained correct
alternatives, decision consequences and total cost.

The oci-agent study instead emphasizes an accountable human principal over
actor/critic workflows and deterministic causal libraries. Its critic can
decline analyses with poor overlap. \citep{v12_la_2607_22443} The relevant outcome
then includes correct refusal and what remains possible for the requested
population. Reporting only completed analyses would hide precisely the
difficult cases in which an agent's judgment matters most.

An evidence-auditing agent faces a similar boundary. ARGUS audits reported
support for assumptions rather than adjudicating their truth. Its retrieval
and abstention tradeoffs and small human-label pilot leave substantial
generalization questions. \citep{v12_la_2609_30867} In banking, an omitted document,
a contradicted assumption and an assumption whose truth is unknown require
different responses. A documentation score should not become an identification
certificate.

\section{An evidence standard for the proposed banking product}

The synthesis supports a modular research program. Language assistance proposes
questions, variables, graph alternatives and evidence links. Formal operations
check declared structures and calculate identified functionals or sets in
supported regimes. Numerical procedures estimate those objects with their own
sampling and approximation arguments. Human and institutional evidence supply
facts about assignment, ownership and feasibility that neither interface can
manufacture.

Each interface needs an explicit refusal or unknown state. A retrieved passage
with the wrong unit should fail target review. A graph class outside a backend's
domain should return unsupported. A valid but uninformative effect set should
remain visible. A conflict between textual and numerical evidence should retain
both sources for investigation instead of selecting whichever yields a cleaner
answer.

CausalDS makes narrated mechanisms, observations and private scoring objects
separate parts of a benchmark, and its results distinguish symbolic answers,
uncertainty, abstention and cost. \citep{v12_la_2607_08093} The proposed evaluation
adopts that separation as a design principle. It does not borrow a published
model score as evidence for the local prototype. The remainder of this chapter
makes the comparison explicit: what must stay fixed for a published score to
support a banking capability, and what can fail when assistance stages are
combined? Later chapters develop translation, diagrams, discovery and workflow.
Empirical claims about a chosen backend still require a declared evaluation
on independent mechanisms.
~~~

~~~text
\section{Contextual bandit reuse requires a different contract from sequential servicing}
\label{exec23:obp-scope}
A one-time offer allocation and a sequence of collection decisions are different
causal products. Open Bandit Pipeline (OBP) is a useful comparator for the former:
the inspected core organizes logged contextual-bandit observations, target
action distributions, propensity-weighted estimators, response regressions and
evaluation wrappers. It does not convert repeated customer histories into a
qualified longitudinal policy analysis merely because each history can be
flattened into rows. The selected revision is dated 5 November 2022, declares
version 0.5.5 and is the revision returned by the cutoff query. Eleven authentic
source/declaration files support this profile; slate, continuous-action,
multiple-logger and action-embedding estimators need separate review.
\cite{exec23_obp_sources}

\subsection{Logging probabilities, clipping and replay change what the number means}
\label{exec23:obp-target}
For one decision, let $X$ denote information available before choosing action
$A$, let $R$ be the subsequent reward, and write $b(a\mid x)$ and
$\pi(a\mid x)$ for the logging and target action probabilities. Under a common
context population, a stable conditional reward law, truthful logging and
support wherever the target acts, the target is
\[
 V(\pi)=\mathbb E_X\sum_a\pi(a\mid X)q(X,a),
 \quad q(x,a)=\mathbb E[R\mid X=x,A=a],
 \quad \mathbb E_b\!\left[\frac{\pi(A\mid X)}{b(A\mid X)}R\right]=V(\pi).
\]
The last equality follows by cancelling $b$ in the conditional sum over $a$.
Its causal interpretation requires that the reward mechanism remains valid
under the proposed assignment; observed association alone is insufficient.
If action effects persist, affect future eligibility or alter later information,
this single-decision target must not replace a sequential target.

The inspected IPW estimator selects supplied or estimated propensity scores
according to an explicit flag, forms the observed-action ratio and applies an
optional clipping threshold. The doubly robust estimator combines a
target-weighted regression prediction with a clipped weighted residual. Its
calculation can be represented as
\[
 \widehat V_{\rm DR}=\frac1n\sum_i\left\{
 \sum_a\pi(a\mid X_i)\widehat q(X_i,a)
 +\min(W_i,c)\big(R_i-\widehat q(X_i,A_i)\big)\right\},
 \qquad W_i=\frac{\pi(A_i\mid X_i)}{\widehat b(A_i\mid X_i)}.
\]
The default unbounded threshold and a finite clipped threshold are distinct
estimating rules. With an exact conditional-mean regression the residual has
zero conditional mean, but arbitrary estimated regressions, fitted propensities
or clipping need their own bias and uncertainty analysis.
\cite{exec23_obp_sources}

Consider two equally common customer types. For type zero, the logging
probability of offer one is $1/4$ and rewards under offers zero and one are
$(0,2)$. For type one, the logging probability is $3/4$ and rewards are $(1,5)$.
The target always gives offer one. Its value is $7/2$, and exact weighting
recovers that value. Clipping the importance ratio at two gives $3$; substituting
a uniform logging probability gives $17/4$. At ten dollars per reward unit and
a stipulated offer cost of 32 dollars, the respective margins are $3$, $-2$ and
$10.50$. An exact response regression restores the DR population value in this
constructed law even with the specified clipped residual. This illustrates
conditional mechanisms; it is not a finite-sample guarantee or an observed
package benchmark. \cite{exec23_obp_reference}

The replay estimator has another contract. It keeps observations whose
observed-action target probability equals exactly one and normalizes by the
sample match rate. Under unequal contextual logging, the matched contexts have
different frequencies from the target population. In the preceding example,
the limiting matched reward is $17/4$, not $7/2$. Appropriate uniform
randomization or another justified replay design is therefore substantive.
For a fully stochastic target with both action probabilities $1/2$, no exact-one
match exists; the selected source leaves an all-zero score vector when there
are no matches. A product must expose unavailable replay evidence rather than
reporting a zero policy value as a scientific result.
\cite{exec23_obp_sources,exec23_obp_reference}

\subsection{A validated array is not a validated causal request}
\label{exec23:obp-uncertainty}
The core expects target probabilities with dimensions round, action and
position. The inspected validator checks the action-axis sum and position/action
indices, and rejects nonpositive supplied propensity values. Its array helper
checks array type and dimension, not general finiteness. The target-distribution
check does not separately impose nonnegative entries: the row
$(-1/10,11/10)$ sums to one but is not a probability law. A nonfinite propensity
also needs an explicit finite-value check; a comparison with zero is not a
complete validator. These are scoped source findings. The proposed adapter
must independently verify common row identities, action/position vocabulary,
finite values, valid probabilities and their scientific provenance.
\cite{exec23_obp_sources,exec23_obp_reference}

The regression wrapper defaults to one fold, fitting and predicting on the
same contexts. Its multi-fold branch uses shuffled row K-fold splits. Such
splits do not preserve customer groups or forward calendar separation by
construction. Missing propensities are replaced with a uniform distribution
inside this regression-preparation path. That fallback does not authenticate a
bank logging policy, especially for importance-weighted or MRDR fitting. The
adapter must bind whether the quantities are true logs, estimates or explicit
design inputs, and justify both the fitting loss and the evaluation law. An
out-of-fold prediction flag alone is not an uncertainty theorem.
\cite{exec23_obp_sources}

Basic estimator intervals first calculate round-level scores and then bootstrap
those fixed scores. The common helper takes percentile endpoints and reports
the mean of bootstrap means. It does not repeat response fitting, propensity
estimation or hyperparameter selection in the selected call. Self-normalized
IPW inherits this interval path, so fixed-score resampling and re-estimating the
normalization are different procedures, as the preceding sequential-library
example already shows. The proposal must state the conditioning argument and
retain the actual number of replications and seed, rather than describing all
such output as full-pipeline uncertainty.
\cite{exec23_obp_sources}

Tuning is another layer. The source offers an estimated-MSE route and a
stability-comparison route, chooses a threshold from candidate scores, and
stores the selected threshold on the estimator object. Later calls reuse it
when the attribute already exists. This may be deliberate state reuse, but an
adapter must distinguish a frozen tuning choice from a new-data tuning request.
The interval call fixes the chosen threshold; it does not repeat the selection
for every bootstrap sample. The scope of the MSE/bias helper also needs its own
source-theorem review before a guarantee is attributed to it.
\cite{exec23_obp_sources}

One apparent defect illustrates why complete argument tracing matters. The
tuned interval constructs a base estimator without forwarding the estimated-
propensity flag. However, it has already selected the intended propensity
array into a local variable and passes that array as the base estimator's
ordinary propensity argument. The selected base interval reads that argument
under its default flag. Thus the inspected chain does not establish a
known-versus-estimated propensity substitution error. The audit retains this
rejected concern, while keeping actual fitting and selection uncertainty open.
Similarly, OBP's Student helper returns a \emph{one-sided} lower bound, so its
$1-\delta$ quantile should not inherit the symmetric-endpoint criticism from
the preceding library. Contract differences must be reviewed individually.
\cite{exec23_obp_sources,exec23_obp_reference}

\subsection{Public benchmark evidence and a deployable worker are separate assets}
\label{exec23:obp-decision}
The inspected dataset class reads campaign data, sorts by timestamp, maps the
position coding, extracts click rewards and supplied propensity columns, and
prepares features before its optional chronological train/test slicing. The
on-policy comparison is the empirical reward mean of the selected logged
policy's full or test sample. It is useful observed benchmark evidence, with
sampling uncertainty and a particular campaign population, not an exact
counterfactual oracle or a bank outcome. Feature vocabularies derived before
the split must be disclosed; timestamp sorting does not by itself establish
training-only preprocessing or independent observations. No dataset was loaded
or executed in this review, and its complete data rights remain unqualified.
\cite{exec23_obp_sources}

The source-level reuse decision is \emph{reference}. An isolated Python worker
could preserve the selected estimator and preparation semantics after a frozen
environment and native qualification, but full adoption would admit unreviewed
families and dependencies. A port to R, Java or C++ currently lacks a measured
benefit that justifies duplicating action-position conversion, nuisance fitting,
tuning state and bootstrap semantics. A minimal independent reference is a
useful oracle, not a full replacement. The selected artifact contains Apache
2.0 text; full dependency/data rights remain a separate obligation. The
Poetry file specifies Python below 3.10 and pins some scientific libraries,
whereas setup metadata uses broader minimum versions. Those declarations need
a concrete resolution, not an assumption of compatibility with the most recent
environment. Named authors and the selected revision do not establish a current
maintenance promise. \cite{exec23_obp_sources}

The proposed request contract carries context and action clocks, immutable row
and customer IDs, the outcome window and monetary units, action/position
mapping, target and logging provenance, fitted-model identities, split design,
clipping rule and tuning state, bootstrap unit and seed. Library, CLI and MCP
must return the same target, denominator, unavailable-result reasons and
qualification limits. A conversational agent may translate a business request
into these fields, but must not invent missing logging truth or treat a
schema-valid probability array as sufficient evidence.

Public qualification should begin with the exact contextual law above, then
vary logging imbalance, stochastic targets, zero matches, clipping, position
permutations, invalid probabilities, nuisance estimation, repeated customers
and temporal drift. Reuse of a tuned object must be compared with a deliberately
fresh object, and score-only intervals with the scientifically justified
resampling procedure. Actual native outputs, refusals and costs must be
measured after environment and source custody are complete. This route can
justify a prototype without claiming that public e-commerce logs already
validate a bank intervention.
~~~

~~~text
\section{Domain knowledge as evidence for a causal graph}
\label{exec22:domain-scope}

A collections manager considering a payment holiday needs to distinguish a
plausible story from an intervention that improves customer outcomes. A language
model may suggest that financial strain affects delinquency, that servicing
changes financial strain, and that earlier delinquency affects the servicing
offer. Each statement needs a population, a time index, a variable definition
and an evidential basis. Joining the three statements without those qualifications
can create a cycle whose meaning is unclear. A retrieval system can help locate
the underlying evidence, but a retrieved sentence does not by itself establish
an invariant structural mechanism. Two recent clinical studies make the promise
and the limitations of this assistance concrete.

\subsection{Graph elicitation and the meaning of completeness}
\label{exec22:domain-elicitation}

Aziz and Brookhart study a hypothetical comparison of statins with no treatment
for preventing cardiovascular disease. They run four prompting strategies on
GPT-4o and a zero-shot strategy on GPT-o1, with three separate conversations per
configuration. Two author reviewers assess consistency, acyclicity, source
accuracy, completeness and prompt adherence. This is a study of fifteen outputs
in one familiar clinical scenario, rather than an estimate of performance over
a population of banking questions. The original was published on 30 October
2025. \cite{exec22_domain_aziz}

Its completeness criterion asks whether the graph contains seven groups of
variables drawn from an ASCVD risk score. This is a useful check for conspicuous
omissions, but it does not validate the graph's arrows or establish that its
adjustment set identifies the statin effect. Predictors can have different causal
roles: a pretreatment common cause, a mediator and a selection variable cannot
be treated interchangeably simply because each predicts the outcome. In a bank,
a strong arrears predictor measured after a servicing offer may be an outcome
of that offer. Including it in a list is different from correctly deciding
whether to adjust for it.

seven graphs containing six of the seven criteria. The seven-of-fifteen count
does not support the abstract's ``more than half'' wording. Race is absent from
all fifteen outputs. That is a reproducible observation about the study's
criterion; it does not establish a universal requirement to insert a particular
attribute into every causal model. A social attribute's role needs an explicit
account of the processes it represents and the target population. Blindly
adding a variable to improve a checklist score could conceal the same scientific
problem as omitting it. \cite{exec22_domain_aziz,exec22_domain_reference}

titles, dates or author details. Chain-of-thought outputs give explanations
without sources in all three runs. The GPT-o1 zero-shot configuration consistently
supplies references and code, yet one code output needs manual repair. Its third
run is described as supplying nine sources and then assessed using denominators
of six; the original outputs are needed before aggregating that run's citation
accuracy. The source assessments described in the paper use title and abstract
review, which is weaker than checking that primary methods and results support
a particular causal arrow. \cite{exec22_domain_aziz}

use and cholesterol. The authors correctly identify the need for temporally
indexed nodes if feedback is intended. The banking counterpart is

before action \(A_t\). Collapsing \(D_t\) and \(D_{t+1}\) into a single
``delinquency'' node loses the information clock. A graph assistant should request
that missing distinction rather than silently reverse an arrow to satisfy a
syntactic check. The study supports a brainstorming and source-checking role;
it supplies no validation of a bank effect estimator.

\subsection{Retrieval helps under a particular reference and query}
\label{exec22:domain-retrieval}

Lin and colleagues combine language models, retrieval and observational discovery
for chronic low back pain. Their February 2026 medRxiv original is a preprint,
not a peer-reviewed result. They use baseline observations from 1,868 participants
and a fourteen-variable expert reference. Crucially, the authors explicitly state
that this reference contains cycles and is not a DAG. The reference was developed
from clinical expertise and a literature synthesis; it is a declared comparison
target, not observed intervention truth. \cite{exec22_domain_lin}

The three knowledge systems share Mistral 7B-Instruct v0.3. Ordinary retrieval
supplies document chunks selected by vector similarity. Knowledge-graph retrieval
extracts entities and relations, merges entities, forms communities and retrieves
entities, attached relations, community summaries and supporting text. The paper
describes 600-token chunks with 100-token overlap, an 8,000-token retrieval budget,
and a pipeline involving constrained extraction, a graph database and community
clustering. These are descriptions of the authors' system; they do not establish
that its dependencies are pinned, licensed for the proposed distribution or
operationally integrated here. \cite{exec22_domain_lin}

Both retrieval systems use the same source articles that the experts used to
construct the comparison graph. This is an informative test of reconstructing
an aligned body of knowledge. It does not measure performance when the literature
is incomplete, contradictory, selected by a different team, or independent of the
reference adjudicators. The authors discuss this alignment explicitly. Their
argument that the model predates publication of the expert graph also does not
by itself authenticate the model's training corpus or exclude related earlier
content. The appropriate extension is a deliberately held-out reference and
document design, not a declaration that contamination has been ruled out.

For the data component, the paper describes hill climbing with local generalized
linear models, BIC scores and 500 bootstrap samples. A thresholded consensus graph
forms the initial model. The system then combines its edges with the knowledge
system's proposals and asks a further direction question when both directions
are suggested. Plausibility, association, temporality and a direct causal query
are separate prompt conditions. Their relative performance matters as much as
the strongest result. \cite{exec22_domain_lin}

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{p{0.48\linewidth}rr}
\hline
Reported configuration & F1 & Difference \\
\hline
Observational initial model & 0.396 & --- \\
Initial model plus LLM, plausibility & 0.636 & --- \\
Initial model plus ordinary retrieval, plausibility & 0.714 & --- \\
Initial model plus graph retrieval, plausibility & 0.745 & 0.031 over 0.714 \\
Graph retrieval alone after direction resolution & 0.737 & 0.008 below 0.745 \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

These are displayed scores against the single expert graph. The improvement
from 0.396 to 0.745 is 0.349, but the extra gain over ordinary retrieval is 0.031,
and the gain from adding observational discovery to the strongest graph-retrieval
configuration is 0.008. None is a paired confidence interval or a measured return
on engineering effort. Before direction resolution, graph retrieval's plausibility
F1 is 0.602, below the LLM-only value of 0.627. After resolution the values are
0.737 and 0.636. In the final combined systems, ordinary retrieval exceeds graph
retrieval for association by 0.060 and for temporality by 0.130. A blanket ranking
of retrieval architectures would conceal these reversals. \cite{exec22_domain_lin,exec22_domain_reference}

The strongest combined configuration still reports FDR 0.360, meaning disagreement
among its predicted directed edges against this reference under the paper's
definition. It is not a certified probability that a proposed bank causal claim
is false. Small differences also deserve care: subtracting the printed 0.396
from 0.636 gives 0.240, whereas Table 5 prints a change of 0.241. Rounding of
unreported underlying values can explain that discrepancy. It supplies a reason
to recover the original edge records, not a reason to invent corrected results.

\subsection{Direct edges, indirect effects and feedback need different objects}
\label{exec22:domain-semantics}

The chronic-pain plausibility and temporality questions explicitly allow a
relationship ``through one or more intermediate variables.'' Their answers
therefore need not describe direct adjacency among the measured variables.
For the chain
\begin{equation}
 A\longrightarrow M\longrightarrow Y,
 \qquad E=\{(A,M),(M,Y)\},
 \label{exec22:domain-chain}
\end{equation}
\(A\) is an ancestor of \(Y\) even though \((A,Y)\notin E\). A positive
indirect-effect answer cannot be inserted as a direct edge without changing the
graph and possibly its conditional independences. Conversely, when a variable
is unmeasured, a projected graph may legitimately have different edge semantics.
The interface must state which object it is constructing. The paper's source
text is sufficient to identify the mismatch that needs checking; it is not
sufficient to reconstruct every edge's intended semantics. \cite{exec22_domain_lin,exec22_domain_reference}

Taking a union of proposed edges also has no universal accuracy guarantee.
Starting from the correct two-edge set in equation~\eqref{exec22:domain-chain},
adding the false edge \(Y\to A\) produces two true positives, one false positive
and no false negatives. Thus
\begin{equation}
 F_1=\frac{2\,\mathrm{TP}}{2\,\mathrm{TP}+\mathrm{FP}+\mathrm{FN}}
     =\frac45<1.
 \label{exec22:domain-f1}
\end{equation}
It also creates a directed three-cycle without any reciprocal pair. Resolving
only two-way pairs would not remove it. This exact example does not assert that
the paper's code necessarily produces such a failure. It shows why the observed
nonnegative changes in its result table cannot be promoted to a theorem that
combining knowledge and data always improves the graph. \cite{exec22_domain_reference}

There is a further distinction in the observational comparison. Moralization
drops arrowheads and connects parents of a common child. For
\(A\to M\leftarrow B\), it adds the \(A\)--\(B\) link even though that link
is absent from the original skeleton. Consequently, the paper's moralized-graph
comparison is not simply a comparison of adjacencies after ignoring direction.
Good agreement on that object cannot identify a unique causal ordering. Similarly,
a cyclic expert reference and a DAG learner require an explicit account of the
representation mismatch before their distance is interpreted as scientific error.

A useful banking representation retains the proposition type, time horizon,
population, supporting span and evidence strength for each proposed relation.
It distinguishes a direct cause from an ancestor, an association, an ontological
relationship and a modeler's assumption. A type hierarchy or a semantic link in
a knowledge graph is not automatically a causal edge. Hard constraints can narrow
the graph search when justified by an information clock or design rule. Uncertain
literature claims should remain revisable evidence; treating them as inviolable
constraints can exclude the true graph. When sources conflict, returning the
alternatives preserves information that forced orientation destroys.

\subsection{Identical records can support opposite investment decisions}
\label{exec22:domain-value}

An exact illustration explains why better graph agreement alone is insufficient
for a product decision. Let \(A\) denote a centered, standardized servicing
intensity and \(L\) a centered loss index, where one loss unit is stipulated to
equal USD~100. Consider two authored Gaussian structural models. In the first,
all exogenous variables are independent and
\begin{equation}
 A=U_A,\qquad L=-\tfrac12 A+\varepsilon,
 \qquad \operatorname{Var}(U_A)=1,\quad
 \operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon)=\tfrac34.
 \label{exec22:domain-causal}
\end{equation}
In the second, \(U,\eta_A,\eta_L\) are mutually independent centered Gaussians,
each with variance \(1/2\), and
\begin{equation}
 A=U+\eta_A,\qquad L=-U+\eta_L.
 \label{exec22:domain-latent}
\end{equation}
Both models imply exactly the same centered bivariate Gaussian observed law:
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{Var}\!\begin{pmatrix}A\\L\end{pmatrix}=
 \begin{pmatrix}1&-1/2\\-1/2&1\end{pmatrix}.
 \label{exec22:domain-covariance}
\end{equation}
In the first model, replacing the action equation
by a one-unit higher intervention lowers expected loss by one half unit. In the
second, replacing the action equation leaves \(U\) and \(L\) unchanged, so the
effect is zero. The observed regression slope is \(-1/2\) in both. No amount
of replication of this observed joint law distinguishes the two intervention
effects. The Gaussian loss index is an illustrative local model, not a claim
that realized bank losses can have an unrestricted negative support.
\cite{exec22_domain_reference}

Suppose the higher action costs USD~20 per eligible customer over the declared
horizon, with no other monetized effects. Its modeled incremental margin is
\begin{equation}
 V=-100\{\mathbb E[L\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a+1)]
             -\mathbb E[L\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a)]\}-20,
 \label{exec22:domain-margin}
\end{equation}
which equals USD~30 in the first model and USD~\(-20\) in the second. Retaining
both models therefore retains the range \([-20,30]\). Under a separately declared
subjective weight \(w\) on the first model, expected margin is \(50w-20\),
positive only when \(w>2/5\). A language-model vote fraction, retrieval score or
graph F1 is not that probability. The practical task is to find evidence that
can distinguish the models: an admissible randomization, a justified additional
measurement, or an independently supported restriction. More fluent explanations
of the same observed correlation cannot do so. \cite{exec22_domain_reference}

\subsection{A public evaluation and a concrete integration decision}
\label{exec22:domain-validation}

The proposal should first test graph assistance on public documents and generated
cases with declared causal laws. The evaluation needs two distinct targets.
One is reconstruction of a specified expert account, for which alternative
adjudicators and documented disagreements are legitimate evidence. The other is
recovery of causal implications under a known data-generating law. Conflating
these targets would reward agreement with an expert even when the expert's graph
is incomplete. The Gaussian pair above provides an inexpensive refusal case:
a system given only the shared observed law should retain both effects unless
the task supplies additional identifying information.

Cases should also include indirect-only relations, long cycles, feedback requiring
time expansion, unmeasured common causes, contradictory papers and evidence that
is silent about direction. Keep the adjudication documents separate from the
retrieval corpus for the primary test; report same-corpus reconstruction as a
different condition. Hold out domains as well as individual documents. Match
source access, context allowance and reviewer effort across data-only,
expert-only, ontology-assisted, LLM-only, ordinary-retrieval, graph-retrieval and
combined systems. This tests whether constructing a knowledge graph is worth its
additional extraction, maintenance and review cost.

Measure source identity and span entailment, variable/time alignment, direct-edge
and ancestral accuracy, equivalence-class retention, abstention, valid
identification and decision consequences separately. Repeat prompts and seeds;
do not treat correlated edge votes from a shared corpus as independent experts.
Record graph-building tokens, query tokens, latency, correction effort and
maintenance alongside numerical scores. An 8,000-token context cap does not
equalize the cost of building the two retrieval systems. The public study should
predeclare thresholds for useful assistance and costs before inspecting the
held-out results. There is no measured financial benefit in the two clinical
papers that can set those thresholds for a bank.

For implementation planning, adopt the evidence-provenance pattern and the
separation of variable definition, relation proposal and graph validation.
Integrate retrieval behind a typed interface only after pinning the underlying
corpus, software, model and rights. Retain the ordinary-retrieval comparator;
the results do not justify porting an entire graph-retrieval stack in advance
of a matched benefit test. Reject unconditional union, compulsory orientation
and silent conversion of an indirect relation into a direct edge. The chronic-pain
appendix's Boolean answer schema and fallback to general knowledge lack an
explicit abstention channel; the proposed interface should supply one.
\cite{exec22_domain_lin}

The same reviewed request can pass through a library call, CLI or MCP tool. It
should carry the target, variable clocks, corpus identities, proposed relation
types and permitted operations, and return evidence-backed alternatives and
identification status. Retrieved prose is evidence to inspect, not an instruction
that authorizes another tool call. A cycle or unsupported edge should produce a
specific unresolved result that downstream estimation preserves. These are
proposed contracts, not demonstrated cross-repository integrations. Public
prototype merit must precede an expensive experiment with private bank data.
~~~
