\chapter{Language assistance, causal discovery and uncertainty}
\label{ch:la03-discovery}

This chapter follows a graph suggestion through the operations that could
make it useful for a decision. The opening comparison separates linguistic
knowledge from observations and interventions. The subsequent studies develop
information bounds, numerical alternatives, search failures, expert evidence
and executable graph contracts. Temporal and latent-variable examples then
show what those operations cannot determine from the supplied information.
The final identification study asks whether the resulting answer still
addresses the original population and action. These are successive obligations,
not interchangeable measures of discovery quality.

\section{The scientific object behind a graph proposal}

A banking analyst may begin with a list of columns and a request to explain why
balances move after a change in deposit pricing. A language model can recognize
the vocabulary, propose a market-rate variable, distinguish a customer offer
from a realized rate, and suggest that customer characteristics affect both
assignment and retention. These suggestions are useful because a statistical
algorithm does not recover the meaning of a column from its numerical values.
The scientific question nevertheless remains open. The proposed relation may
describe a mechanism in another population, a historical association, a direct
effect, an indirect path, or simply a familiar phrase. The role given to the
suggestion determines the claim the resulting graph can support.

The inspected literature offers several roles rather than one method called
``LLM causal discovery.'' Pairwise language judgments, breadth-first graph
construction, retrieval-assisted discovery, response-based independence
queries, statistical prompting, soft graph priors, multi-agent debate and
numerical experiment design alter different parts of an analysis
\citep{v12_la_2305_00050,v12_la_2402_01207,v12_la_2402_15301,
v12_la_2406_07378,v12_la_2402_01454,v12_la_2405_13551,
v12_la_2407_15073,v12_la_2608_09696}.
They should be compared by what information they consume, what object they
change, and what uncertainty survives that change.

Let $D$ denote numerical observations, $T$ the retrieved or supplied technical
text, and $M$ the language-model mechanism, including its version, prompts and
decoding policy. A proposal is then a function or random output of
$(D,T,M)$. It is not an additional independent sample from the banking process.
If the model proposes a graph $G$, the relevant questions are whether the
variables have the intended meaning, whether the graph restrictions are
scientifically warranted, whether the data support the inference procedure,
and whether the target effect is identified under those restrictions. These
questions remain distinct even when one conversational interface presents all
of them together.

The following analysis uses inspected primary methods and evaluations. Reported
benchmark gains are the authors' results; no external discovery package or
language-model endpoint is executed here. The finite examples and probability
calculations below are project constructions. Their role is to test the logic
of proposed interfaces and interpretations, not to claim bank validation.

\section{What language-only discovery measures}

The broad proof of concept of K{\i}c{\i}man and colleagues motivates language
support for several causal tasks, including the elicitation of background
knowledge and reasoning about causal relationships
\citep{v12_la_2305_00050}. A model can answer a question such as whether an
increase in a borrowing rate affects demand without receiving a numerical
sample. Such an answer may encode useful inherited knowledge. It cannot reveal
which of several observationally compatible assignment mechanisms generated a
particular bank's records unless the prompt or the model's knowledge provides
additional applicable information.

Feng and colleagues investigate relation occurrences in accessible OLMo and
BLOOM pretraining corpora and report that relation frequency is associated with
prediction success \citep{v12_la_2407_19638}. Their controlled additions of
synthetic relations and the effects of reversed or negated statements help
separate recall from a claim of general discovery. The scope matters: their
pretraining investigation concerns accessible models and predominantly
commonsense relationships. It is evidence for a contamination concern and a
test design, not proof that every model operates only by memorization.

A sensible banking evaluation therefore crosses two kinds of novelty. One can
change the variable names while holding the mechanism fixed, or change the
mechanism while retaining familiar labels. The first tests reliance on
surface vocabulary. The second asks whether a familiar story prevents the
system from responding to contrary evidence. Neither test should declare a
new label intrinsically uninformative: operational definitions often carry
real information about intervention feasibility and time order. Removing all
meaning from a variable name changes the task as well as its contamination risk.

Context must also be handled carefully. In the inspected reliability study,
positive and negative contexts alter affirmative response rates, with contexts
generated by a model and assessed by human annotators
\citep{v12_la_2407_19638}. Some contextual changes legitimately change a causal
claim. A policy that affects demand in one regulatory regime may have no effect
in another. A robustness test should either hold the target world fixed or
declare the changed world and its new truth. Scoring every changed answer as
instability would conflate semantic responsiveness with error.

Jiralerspong and colleagues use breadth-first organization to reduce graph
construction calls \citep{v12_la_2402_01207}. This offers an engineering
alternative to asking about every pair separately. Call complexity is not total
resource cost. A call that lists many nodes may have a growing prompt and
response, require retries, or depend on a long context. A complete comparison
must record input and output tokens, wall time, cache policy, model cost,
failure frequency and the review time needed to adjudicate proposals. Rejecting
a cycle is useful structural validation, but does not make the remaining
acyclic graph true.

\section{Response tests are not sampling-law independence tests}

Cohrs and colleagues investigate language-model judgments in a
constraint-based discovery workflow \citep{v12_la_2406_07378}. This is a
different mechanism from applying a conditional-independence test to observed
bank records. For example, the statement
$X\mathrel{\perp\!\!\!\perp}Y\mid Z$ is a claim about a distribution. A
model's frequency of saying ``YES'' to that statement is a property of a
prompted response process. Even a correctly estimated response probability
does not establish the distributional statement.

Static inspection of the pinned \texttt{causal\_GPT} source shows a further
issue that can be examined without making any model calls. Its response
aggregation counts YES and NO within the same response collection. The
inspected test forms proportions $\widehat p_N=N_N/n$ and
$\widehat p_Y=N_Y/n$, pools them as
$\widehat p=(N_N+N_Y)/(2n)$, and uses the denominator
\begin{equation}
 \widehat s_{\mathrm{ind}}=
 \sqrt{\frac{2\widehat p(1-\widehat p)}{n}}.
 \label{eq:la03-independent-denominator}
\end{equation}
The formula resembles an independent two-proportion standard error. Its
interpretation needs the actual sampling relationship between the counts.

Consider the deliberately simple project response model in which independent
draws take values NO, YES or OTHER, with probabilities $p_N,p_Y,p_O$. Let
$I_N$ and $I_Y$ be indicators for the first two categories in one draw. The
categories are mutually exclusive, so
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}(I_N,I_Y)=-p_Np_Y.
\]
Consequently the exact variance of the difference of the sample proportions is
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{Var}(\widehat p_N-\widehat p_Y)
 =\frac{p_N+p_Y-(p_N-p_Y)^2}{n}.
 \label{eq:la03-multinomial-variance}
\end{equation}
This elementary calculation is a project derivation under the stated
independent categorical law. It is not a claim that actual model calls are
independent or stationary.

Under the binary symmetric response null $p_N=p_Y=1/2$, the true variance is
$1/n$, whereas the square of
Equation~\eqref{eq:la03-independent-denominator} is $1/(2n)$. The denominator
is too small by a factor $\sqrt{2}$. For $n=100$ and a nominal one-sided
level of $0.01$, summing the exact binomial probabilities over the inspected
formula's rejection region gives approximately $0.044313$. The calculation
enumerates all counts with their rational binomial probabilities; it does not
simulate responses or execute the downloaded implementation.

Correcting this variance would address one response-model issue. It would not
convert language judgments into a bank conditional-independence test. Real
calls may share context, cached outputs, decoding artifacts or a changing
backend. The source also converts the response decision to a numerical zero
or one at the independence-test interface. Those values need a type that
exposes their meaning. Passing them through an API named ``pvalue'' cannot
confer sampling-law calibration.

In a funding example, repeated model agreement that customer risk is unrelated
to pricing conditional on branch does not validate the bank's assignment law.
The remedy is to separate a language-evidence object from a numerical test
object. The former can carry source anchors, answer frequencies and unresolved
scientific questions. The latter must identify its observations, null,
sampling assumptions and calibration. Neither object should silently replace
the other.

\section{Retrieval, constraints and soft priors}

Retrieval changes the information available to a model. It may supply an
operational definition or an expert restriction that the numerical data cannot
identify. It can also supply irrelevant or contradictory evidence. Zhang and
colleagues' retrieval-assisted method reports mixed results: in the inspected
ASIA setting, documents reduce skeleton F1 from 1 to 0.73, while other settings
benefit \citep{v12_la_2402_15301}. The result argues for keeping retrieval
conditions visible in a comparison, rather than labeling retrieval as a
uniform improvement.

The reported orientation accuracy in that work is evaluated on recovered
true-positive edges. Its denominator excludes missing or false edges. For a
reader deciding whether a graph is useful for intervention, skeleton error and
orientation error both matter. A system must report the metric and its
denominator before drawing a conclusion about the full graph. Downstream
effect behavior remains a separate outcome.

A retrieved statement may concern an ancestral path rather than direct
adjacency. Ban and colleagues elicit ancestral constraints and use soft
penalties alongside numerical scores \citep{v12_la_2306_16902}. In a chain
$A\to M\to Y$, $A$ is an ancestor of $Y$ even when no direct $A\to Y$
edge exists. If an adapter turns ``can affect'' into ``directly causes,'' it
changes the scientific input. Path, adjacency, temporal-order and exclusion
constraints therefore need different representations and conversion tests.

Hard constraints delete graphs. If a wrong constraint removes the true graph,
increasing the numerical sample does not restore it within the constrained
search. Darvariu and colleagues investigate soft language-derived priors that
retain support for possible graphs \citep{v12_la_2405_13551}. In schematic
form, one can write a search objective as
\begin{equation}
 \widehat G_\lambda\in\arg\max_G
 \{S(D,G)+\lambda L(T,M,G)\},
 \label{eq:la03-soft-score}
\end{equation}
where $S$ is a numerical score, $L$ a language-derived preference and
$\lambda$ a declared strength. This notation is a common project comparison
device; the actual score and statistical assumptions must be taken from the
chosen method.

Positive prior support prevents one particular failure: a graph is not
logically excluded solely because a model dislikes it. A large wrong
preference can still dominate weak numerical evidence. Subsequent pruning can
again remove the relevant graph. The inspected experiments include selected
combined gains and cases where standalone priors harm performance. A useful
evaluation fixes the prior rule, compares $\lambda=0$, varies evidence quality
and preserves every failed setting. Tuning $\lambda$ after viewing the final
test graphs invalidates a simple interpretation of the reported comparison.

Takayama and colleagues instead feed statistical discovery information into
language prompts, then convert response probabilities into forced, forbidden
or unknown constraints for particular algorithms
\citep{v12_la_2402_01454}. The conversion differs across PC, exact search and
DirectLiNGAM. Their inspected examples contain both gains and failures and
caution against treating the procedure as an opaque automatic solution.
A bootstrap frequency, a response frequency and a posterior model probability
are three different objects. A user interface should not place them under one
unqualified confidence label.

Statistical prompting also raises a data-reuse issue. If $D$ determines the
initial graph summary and that summary shapes the language restriction, the
restriction is a function of $D$. A later fit cannot casually treat it as
independent external evidence. This does not make every such procedure
invalid; it changes the procedure that must be justified or evaluated.
Tracking data hashes and the full adaptive rule makes the reuse visible.
Sample splitting may help a particular construction, but it neither proves the
restriction true nor automatically supplies valid downstream uncertainty.

\section{Debate, disagreement and scientific evidence}

The multi-agent discovery approach of Le and colleagues assigns different
roles to language agents and uses their interaction to construct a graph
\citep{v12_la_2407_15073}. This can organize critique and expose alternative
stories. Its inspected assumptions exclude hidden confounding and cycles, and
the reported canonical benchmark scale is limited. Those conditions should
remain attached to a banking interpretation.

Several agents need not provide several independent pieces of evidence. They
may use the same model family, encounter overlapping training material, or
retrieve the same article. A majority can therefore amplify a common error.
Disagreement is useful as a review signal, but agreement cannot be converted
to a causal confidence interval without a model of the information and
dependence involved.

For servicing, one agent may propose that a contact causes distress, another
that distress causes contact, and a critic may resolve the conflict by choosing
the more plausible story. A more defensible workflow keeps both candidates,
asks which timestamp and assignment evidence would distinguish them, and
identifies the effects under each. A later scientific owner may supply an
applicable restriction. The agent's role is to formulate the unresolved
question and retrieve the evidence, not to manufacture the answer.

Candidate remedies include comparing one-agent and multi-agent conditions,
using the same numerical evidence and total budget, and clustering evaluation
results by shared mechanism rather than counting paraphrased prompts as
independent cases. These are proposed tests. No multi-agent trial has been
executed here, and diversity of models alone does not verify assumptions.

\section{Graph ambiguity and the target effect}

A graph matters because it changes the interpretation of an intervention.
Suppose an observed distribution $P$ is compatible with a class
$\mathcal G$. For a target $Q$, let $\Theta_G(P,Q)$ contain the effects
allowed by the distribution and assumptions under $G$. The scientifically
relevant target set is
\begin{equation}
 \Theta_{\mathcal G}(P,Q)=\bigcup_{G\in\mathcal G}\Theta_G(P,Q).
 \label{eq:la03-effect-union}
\end{equation}
This is a definition, not a claim that the set has been computed or that a
learned class covers the truth. An unrestricted member can make the union
unrestricted. A point estimate from the most fluent graph narrative would
answer a different, more strongly conditioned question.

The project's two-variable example makes this concrete. Under model F,
$A\sim\mathrm{Bernoulli}(1/2)$ and $Y=A$ with probability $0.9$, with an
independent flip otherwise. Under model R the roles are reversed:
$Y\sim\mathrm{Bernoulli}(1/2)$ and $A=Y$ with probability $0.9$. Both
models yield
\[
 P(0,0)=P(1,1)=0.45,\qquad P(0,1)=P(1,0)=0.05.
\]
Replacing $A$'s equation by an intervention gives an average effect of $0.8$
under F and zero under R. In this deliberately finite class the target set is
$\{0,0.8\}$. Neither acyclicity nor observational fit selects the effect.
A sufficiently informative scientific time order or intervention could remove
an alternative, but the example intentionally assumes only a coarse shared
recording time.

The distinction between set identification and confidence in a learned set is
equally important. Let $G_\star$ be the true graph, $\widehat{\mathcal G}$ a
random retained class, and $C_G$ a random set for the target under $G$. Define
$C=\bigcup_{G\in\widehat{\mathcal G}}C_G$. If the actual joint procedure
satisfies
\[
 \Pr(G_\star\notin\widehat{\mathcal G})\le\alpha_G,
 \qquad
 \Pr(\theta_\star\notin C_{G_\star})\le\alpha_\theta,
\]

\begin{equation}
 \Pr(\theta_\star\notin C)\le\alpha_G+\alpha_\theta.
 \label{eq:la03-coverage-decomposition}
\end{equation}

declared alternatives while delegating full class recognition and
identification to a formal engine.

an expert's asserted exclusion from an algorithmic orientation and from a
model's suggestion. Changed restrictions create a new analysis identity;
they should not overwrite the prior result invisibly.

Failure recovery must preserve scientific meaning as well as computation. If a
job stops after producing a partial graph, replay must not publish it as a
complete answer. If a source or data hash changes, an earlier identification
claim cannot simply be reused. A report should expose a refused or unknown
effect when that is the formal outcome. The completed local operation contract
provides a bounded implementation surface; new discovery adapters still need
their own source, semantic and execution qualification.

\section{What would establish useful progress}

A meaningful comparison begins with a fixed question and information set.
The numerical baseline, language-only baseline, retrieval condition, hybrid
and agent-assisted workflow should receive explicitly matched information or
have their information advantage declared. Accuracy on familiar graphs is
only one outcome. The study also needs identification correctness, retention
of compatible alternatives, valid abstention, effect-set coverage where a
guarantee is claimed, interval or set width, decision loss and full cost.

Every request belongs in the denominator. Failed parsing, unavailable models,
timeouts, nonidentification and legitimate refusals have different meanings
and should be recorded separately. A graph metric conditional on successful
requests can be informative, but it must accompany the success probability
and the selection rule. A narrow accurate set emitted only in easy cases is
not the same product as one that delivers useful valid output reliably.

The proposed remedies are correspondingly bounded. Novel labels test one
shortcut; counterevidence tests retrieval dependence; correctly typed
constraints prevent a specific semantic conversion; fixed prompts and budgets
make an experiment reproducible; and preserved graph classes prevent one form
of overstatement. None of these repairs creates missing bank assignment
truth, resolves observational equivalence by itself, or proves arbitrary
dependent-sample calibration.

This opening comparison supports language assistance for explicit proposals
and reviewable workflow support, with each hybrid method qualified separately.
The following studies develop that position through information limits,
numerical alternatives, source-specific failures and decision consequences.
They distinguish the restricted results already available from the general
temporal graph and useful-precision questions that remain open. New scientific
information, justified assumptions or additional experiments may change the
answer; more fluent explanations of the same information cannot.

\chapter{Operating a study without changing its scientific meaning}
\label{in:operations}

Operating an analysis preserves more than its final number. The argument begins with execution identity and recovery, then develops the publication, retention and capacity boundaries that make a result usable. Discovery, funding, observation and servicing examples show how those boundaries interact with causal uncertainty and monetary consequences. Their exact interface screens and mathematical constructions answer different questions from the fitted studies elsewhere in the book; the comparison keeps those evidential roles explicit.

\section{An execution identity is larger than a request name}

A durable analysis must bind the canonical request, scientific context, input
bytes, code, schema, numerical environment, seed and budget. A repeated job
name alone cannot establish that a result is still valid. The inspected runtime binds the request and a selected source/schema/environment fingerprint and rejects key collisions when those recorded identities change. The fuller identity is a design obligation; the developed recovery argument below identifies dependencies that the selected fingerprint does not independently record.~\citep{v12_in_runtime}

Artifacts use the specified Python JSON encoding, content and descriptor hashes, opaque identities and bounded local reads. Calling that encoding canonical describes this implementation's byte rule; it does not establish cross-language canonicalization. Regular-file and nonsymlink checks reduce accidental
path redirection. A content hash establishes byte identity under the relevant
assumption about the hash function; it is not an authenticated endorsement of
the input's scientific accuracy. A local operator can still supply a false
declaration whose bytes remain perfectly stable.

The scientific request contains no arbitrary shell command, Python import or
network endpoint. Fixed worker entry points execute the supported operations.
This makes the scope of the local tool explicit and allows a review grant to
refer to actual operations. The current controller's trusted caller object is
not a substitute for an institutional identity and approval service.

\section{Budgets, durable jobs and cancellation}

Scientific workers have wall-time and address-space limits. The memory bound
applies to the worker, not to all memory used by the resident SDK and
coordinator. A complete operating measurement must include both. Small control
or error envelopes may exceed an extremely small requested output limit to
explain why the request cannot be fulfilled. These are disclosed boundaries of
the present implementation.~\citep{v12_in_runtime}

Report jobs retain a hashed prefix of completed work identities. The local
retry rule caps worker starts at three and accounts for remaining time against the original local wall-clock budget. That rule is not a hard end-to-end deadline guarantee. Individual publication files are atomic, while artifact content, metadata and terminal job state remain separate transitions. Replay checks request, artifact and checkpoint identities before continuation. The recorded restart fixture kills a report worker after its
first checkpoint and completes all one hundred distinct work identities once.
This is evidence for that local workflow, not a distributed exactly-once
guarantee for arbitrary external side effects.

Cancelling an in-flight protocol request and cancelling a durable application
job are different operations. The inspected specification also recognizes
cancellation/completion races.~\citep{v12_mcp_legacy_cancellation} If publication
has already completed, a cancellation response must report that terminal state.
It must not imply that a displayed result or an external action was undone.
The present service has no operation that changes a bank account or sends a
customer communication.

\section{Fault evidence and what remains unmeasured}

Nine recorded fault cases cover replay with conflicting budgets, wall timeout,
output limits, worker memory, kill/restart with checkpoint, cooperative
cancellation, changed artifact bytes, changed scientific context and changed
checkpoints.~\citep{v12_in_runtime} The tests distinguish preserving a result from
merely restarting a process. An interrupted computation that silently uses new
inputs is a different analysis even if it eventually finishes.

These fixtures do not measure institution-scale availability, multi-host
recovery, adversarial tenant isolation or a service-level commitment. They also
do not show that streaming always improves elapsed time. The earlier complete
local workload comparisons retain small or absent gains; engineering choices
must be justified by the intended workload rather than by the existence of a
streaming interface.

Operational qualification should measure the complete request: artifact import,
scientific work, uncertainty, serialization, reporting and recovery. A benchmark
of one reducer omits fitting and coordination costs. The comparison needs
matched inputs, numerical tolerance and an explicit accounting of unsuccessful
requests, just as a scientific comparison needs a common target.

\section{Compatibility is a maintained scientific obligation}

A new backend release can change defaults, graph encodings, estimator targets,
uncertainty or failure behavior. A compatible JSON schema alone does not prove
scientific compatibility. The proposed adapter register should bind a version,
accepted inputs, method identity, preserved result types and matched adverse
fixtures. A material semantic change requires a reviewed successor rather than
relabeling an old qualification.

Transport migration likewise needs real client/server tests. The current legacy
MCP choice is useful for its tested environment. Supporting a modern protocol
or both eras requires a new compatibility argument, discovery behavior and
failure tests. It should not be advertised by extending a version string while
keeping the old handshake.

Ownership must also remain explicit. The causal library owns its result
contract and adapters. Numerical providers own their implementations and
scientific domains. Consumers own their target interpretation and displayed
decision. The bank owns actual data authority, assignment records, operational
constraints and acceptance. A report can connect those responsibilities; it
cannot replace their evidence.

\section{What a recovery identity must preserve}

Consider a daily deposit report that aggregates customer-level evidence into
a 90-day funding decision. A restarted process must answer the same question
using the same admitted observations. Replacing a data extract with a later
vintage, changing a sign convention, or upgrading a numerical routine can
alter the scientific result even when the file name and command remain
unchanged. This is why recovery needs an analysis identity rather than only
a process identifier.

Write the intended identity as
\[
 J=\operatorname{Hash}(Q,A,S,E,\rho,B),
\]
where $Q$ is the scientific request, $A$ the input identities, $S$ the schema
and method semantics, $E$ the relevant execution environment, $\rho$ the
randomization state where applicable, and $B$ the declared budget. This is a
proposed completeness condition. The inspected runtime fingerprints a selected
list of source files and schemas, Python, and four named package versions.
Its request digest omits the display request identifier and idempotency key
while retaining the other request fields. It rejects reuse of a key with a
changed request or selected execution identity
\cite{exec13_ops_source}.

The selected fingerprint is useful but does not describe every numerical or
platform dependency. It does not, for example, independently record the
complete transitive dependency graph, numerical-library build, operating
system and hardware state. A future numerical adapter must identify which
of those properties can affect its result, then bind and test them. Extending
the fingerprint is an engineering obligation; it does not establish that the
underlying causal assumptions are true. Conversely, irrelevant display
metadata need not invalidate a deterministic result if the scientific and
execution identities remain unchanged.

Three compatibility questions follow. Byte replay asks whether the same
admitted computation returns the same canonical bytes. Numerical compatibility
allows a declared tolerance or stochastic comparison under an unchanged
mathematical target. Scientific compatibility asks whether the population,
treatment, horizon, units, assumptions and inferential meaning remain the
same. A backend upgrade can satisfy a numerical tolerance while changing
which observations are dropped or which population is weighted. Such an
upgrade needs a semantic review even if its output schema is unchanged.

For the funding report, sensible adverse fixtures include a changed date
cutoff, a currency-unit conversion, a negative monetary map, a missing
assignment field, an unbounded uncertainty set and a default that drops
customers without complete histories. The comparison must preserve valid
refusals and ambiguous results. Substituting a point estimate for an
unbounded set is not a compatibility repair.

\section{Checkpoint invariants and the scope of idempotence}

Suppose a report combines deterministic contributions $s_i$ for a frozen
ordered list of work identities $(a_1,\ldots,a_m)$. A useful checkpoint is
\[
 C_k=(J,(a_1,\ldots,a_k),(s_1,\ldots,s_k),h_k),
\]
where $h_k$ binds the preceding contents. The required invariant is that the
completed identifiers form a prefix of the frozen request, each identifier
has one committed contribution, and the public result is a function of those
committed contributions. Recomputing an uncommitted contribution after a
crash may waste work; committing it twice changes the answer.

An exact project construction makes the distinction visible. Three intended
contributions are $100,-40,70$, so the total is $130$. A crash and retry can
produce the calculation trace $100,-40,-40,70$. Naively appending every
returned value gives $90$. A map from work identity to its immutable
contribution still gives $130$, provided a repeated identity cannot carry
changed contents. These are finite arithmetic results, not measurements of
a distributed service~\citep{exec13_ops_exact}.

The inspected local report worker verifies its completed prefix and digest,
skips already committed identities, and updates summaries and completed
identities together in the job state. Its preserved restart trial completed
100 distinct work identities, with 100 unique entries, after two worker
starts. The more recent preserved fault replay also reports the nine declared
cases passing; that replay was not a fresh MCP client/server trial
\cite{exec13_ops_source,exec13_ops_faults}. This evidence supports the named
local report path. It does not establish recovery for arbitrary estimators,
multi-host execution or transactions at a bank.

The atomicity boundary is also specific. The artifact store publishes its
content and metadata as individually atomic files, checks any already
present bytes, and can complete a repeated deterministic publication. The
report's result reference and terminal job state are then published in the
job record. These are several transitions, not one transaction spanning
arbitrary external systems. A crash can leave an unreferenced artifact even
when no incorrect public result is exposed. Retention and garbage collection
therefore need a separate rule that preserves artifacts referenced by admitted
jobs and evidence. Hash verification alone cannot establish that cleanup is
safe.

A customer communication illustrates the stronger problem. If an external
system sends an offer and the acknowledgement is lost, a retrying client may
not know whether the offer was sent. Recording the local calculation once
does not resolve that ambiguity. An eventual external-action adapter would
need a cooperating transaction or deduplication contract, reconciliation and
a named owner for unresolved outcomes. The present service performs no such
bank action. Its proposal should retain report generation as a distinct,
read-oriented capability rather than infer action safety from a successful
restart.

\section{Retries purchase attempts, not independent chances of success}

Let $K$ be a maximum number of attempts and $q$ the probability of a transient
failure on each attempt. If failures are independent and identically
distributed, the probability of obtaining a result is $1-q^K$ and the
expected number of attempts is
\[
 \mathbb E N_K=\sum_{j=0}^{K-1}q^j.
\]
For the stipulated values $q=1/5$ and $K=3$, these are $124/125=0.992$
and $31/25=1.24$. The numbers express an assumed failure law. Nine passing
fault fixtures do not estimate $q$, and a retry cap alone cannot establish
the 99.2\% success probability~\citep{exec13_ops_exact}.

Persistent failures change the calculation. Suppose one tenth of requests
cannot succeed under the supplied environment, while the remaining nine
tenths have independent per-attempt failure probability one tenth. Three
attempts then succeed with probability
\[
 \frac9{10}\left(1-\frac1{10^3}\right)=0.8991,
\]
and require $0.1(3)+0.9(1+0.1+0.01)=1.299$ attempts on average.
The marginal first-attempt failure probability is $0.19$. Treating that
marginal value as independent across retries would predict
$1-0.19^3=0.993141$, substantially overstating success. The retry has not
changed an unavailable dependency, an unsupported method or contradictory
input declarations. Operational classification should distinguish those
persistent causes from a recoverable interruption.

A bounded retry policy also retains its original time account. In the
inspected report path, remaining time is computed from the job creation
timestamp and original wall budget, and the worker-start count is capped at
three. Restarting does not intentionally grant three new full deadlines.
The implementation uses local wall-clock timestamps and operating-system
timers; this is not a distributed clock or a hard real-time guarantee.
Launch overhead, host suspension, clock adjustment and recovery of a failed
machine require a target-environment study before making a service-level
claim~\citep{exec13_ops_source}.

Statistical retries need an additional distinction. Replaying an interrupted
calculation with preserved random state is different from drawing new
randomness until a desired conclusion appears. If three independent valid
null $p$-values are generated and the smallest is selected, the probability
of at least one value below $0.05$ is
\[
 1-(1-0.05)^3=0.142625.
\]
This exact counterexample assumes independent uniform null $p$-values;
it does not allege that the runtime performs such selection. It shows why
the proposed adapter must separate mechanical recovery from a new statistical
replicate and preserve all requested analyses. The same issue arises when
timeouts depend on difficult data and only easy completed fits enter a
coverage report~\citep{exec13_ops_exact}.

\section{Resource budgets and cancellation at the right boundary}

The local worker sets an address-space limit and a wall-time timer. The
coordinator starts a fixed worker entry point, collects its output and
validates the canonical response against the requested output size. This
supports a bounded set of local operations. It does not impose one aggregate
memory bound on the worker, coordinator, SDK and all clients, and the output
check is applied after collection rather than as an incremental bound on an
arbitrary producer's stream~\citep{exec13_ops_source}.

For a proposed third-party numerical adapter, admission should therefore
include peak resident memory of the whole workflow, temporary disk use,
serialization and parent-process buffers. A limit that is safe for a short
report may be inappropriate for an estimator returning a large covariance
matrix. If a result exceeds the public response size, the design can publish
a separately bounded artifact with explicit custody and expose a small
reference. It must retain the scientific object's meaning and cannot silently
truncate interval components or omit unsuccessful fits to meet a size limit.

Cancellation is a race between a request and the computation's next state
transition. For pure report generation, a useful rule is that an accepted
cancellation recorded before the publication transition prevents a new public
result; cancellation after
publication returns the actual completed state. The inspected implementation
checks a cancellation flag around report work and before publication. That
cooperative behavior does not guarantee that every numerical kernel can be
interrupted at an arbitrary instruction. A later adapter may need worker
termination and a rule for discarding uncommitted artifacts.

A timeout should be recorded as an execution outcome. A scientifically
unidentified effect can instead be a completed result with an explicit
scientific limitation. Converting both into one generic failure statistic
obscures the remedy: the first may need resource or implementation work, while
the second may need a different target, new information or abstention. A
successful process exit likewise says nothing by itself about whether the
effect is precise enough to support a decision.

\section{Ownership and a reversible adoption path}

Operational ownership follows the claim being made. A method maintainer owns
the supported algorithm and numerical domain. The common-library owner owns
the request/result contract, method-version binding and admitted conversions.
The consumer owns the displayed target, units and business action. A later
bank study additionally needs a data owner for the actual observation and
assignment processes and a decision owner for losses and feasible actions.
These are proposed responsibilities, not names or approvals that have already
been supplied.

For example, a deposit report may use a valid backend estimate while a
consumer interprets the coefficient as currency rather than thousands of
currency units. The remedy belongs partly in the shared unit contract and
partly in the consuming application's acceptance examples. A central
numerical team cannot certify a silently altered presentation. Conversely,
an application owner cannot declare a confidence procedure valid merely
because the resulting interval is displayed correctly.

The proposal should make an adoption decision reversible at its natural
boundaries. Retain the incumbent expert workflow and its artifacts while a
new adapter is evaluated on matched public/generated requests. Publish both
methods' complete outputs with their own identities; compare discrepancies
before replacing the default. A schema migration should have a declared
mapping and refusal cases for information it cannot preserve. Where a new
method changes the estimand, the migration is a new scientific analysis,
not a formatting conversion. A rollback retains access to the previously
admitted version and evidence without rewriting its result as if produced
by the new version.

The same approach applies to workspace consumers. Read-only inspection of a
repository can reveal candidate objects and interfaces. It cannot establish
that its owner accepts the proposed contract, that its launch environment is
compatible, or that an integration saves work. A local mock consumer can test
the proposed request and response boundary now. Actual consumer execution,
deployment ownership and institutional operation remain distinct later
claims, with their own narrowly defined studies.

\section{The economic denominator is every attempted request}

Let $R$ denote whether a request returns a usable result and $D$ its incremental
decision value relative to the incumbent workflow, including the specified
fallback when $R=0$. Let $C$ include all request-specific compute, review,
retry and recovery costs. The per-request economic target is
\[
 \mathbb E[D-C],
\]
plus a consistent allocation of fixed construction and shared operating
costs. Reporting $\mathbb E[D\mid R=1]$ with a nominal successful-run cost
answers a different question. Reliability and economic comparisons require
both the success probability and what happens on the unsuccessful branch.

In an exact stipulated example, 70\% of requests are easy, complete and add
USD~10 of gross value. Another 15\% complete but add USD~$-30$. The remaining
15\% fail and revert to the baseline action, adding zero gross value but
requiring USD~20 of recovery work. Every attempt costs USD~2 in tools and
computation. The completed-only calculation reports
\[
 \frac{0.70(10)+0.15(-30)}{0.85}-2
 =\frac{16}{17}\simeq0.941
\]
USD per completed request. The all-attempt account instead gives
\[
 0.70(10)+0.15(-30)-2-0.15(20)=-2.5
\]
USD per attempted request. The apparent gain changes sign when the
unsuccessful work and correct denominator enter the account. These numbers
are generated planning assumptions, not workflow prices or measured bank
returns~\citep{exec13_ops_exact}.

Measurement should therefore retain attempted task identity, terminal
execution state, scientific disposition, usable-result status, fallback
action and disjoint cost categories. Repeated attempts are costs within a
request, not new independent banking opportunities. Correlated requests from
one institution, calendar or scientific task family also cannot be treated
as independent evidence merely because their request identifiers differ.
The analysis unit should follow the source of independent information.

A prototype can measure machine resources and trace whether required fields
survive recovery. It cannot price saved analyst time without observing a
matched workflow, nor infer business value from seconds saved. The next
inexpensive operational study should compare complete local workflows under
declared faults and budgets, preserve adverse results, and report source and
environment identities. Only a subsequent justified platform or bank study
can supply institution-specific availability, ownership, labor, and
decision-value evidence. Their absence limits those claims while leaving
the public/generated proposal work executable.

\section{The next complete qualification}

The remaining engineering route is concrete: choose source-audited packages
and permitted integration forms, implement representative bridges, and run
matched consumer workflows across all three surfaces. The trial must include
unsupported methods, late observations, graph ambiguity, weak or disconnected
effect sets, interruption and changed-input rejection. Passing results should
name the actual supported environments and domains.

This work will close an engineering gap only in those domains. Negative
persistent-map, latent-graph and dependent-learner studies remain scientific
obligations. Independent review, authentic bank validation and measured
economics remain additional gates. A coherent runtime makes their required
inputs and outputs reviewable; it does not turn missing information into an
accepted causal answer.

\label{exec13:operations-end}

local report path. It does not establish recovery for arbitrary estimators,

The atomicity boundary is also specific. The artifact store publishes its
content and metadata as individually atomic files, checks any already
present bytes, and can complete a repeated deterministic publication. The
report's result reference and terminal job state are then published in the
job record. These are several transitions, not one transaction spanning
arbitrary external systems. A crash can leave an unreferenced artifact even
when no incorrect public result is exposed. Retention and garbage collection
therefore need a separate rule that preserves artifacts referenced by admitted
jobs and evidence. Hash verification alone cannot establish that cleanup is
safe.

A customer communication illustrates the stronger problem. If an external
system sends an offer and the acknowledgement is lost, a retrying client may
not know whether the offer was sent. Recording the local calculation once
does not resolve that ambiguity. An eventual external-action adapter would
need a cooperating transaction or deduplication contract, reconciliation and
a named owner for unresolved outcomes. The present service performs no such
bank action. Its proposal should retain report generation as a distinct,
read-oriented capability rather than infer action safety from a successful
restart.

\section{Retries purchase attempts, not independent chances of success}

Let $K$ be a maximum number of attempts and $q$ the probability of a transient
failure on each attempt. If failures are independent and identically
distributed, the probability of obtaining a result is $1-q^K$ and the
expected number of attempts is
\[
 \mathbb E N_K=\sum_{j=0}^{K-1}q^j.
\]
For the stipulated values $q=1/5$ and $K=3$, these are $124/125=0.992$
and $31/25=1.24$. The numbers express an assumed failure law. Nine passing
fault fixtures do not estimate $q$, and a retry cap alone cannot establish
the 99.2\% success probability~\citep{exec13_ops_exact}.

Persistent failures change the calculation. Suppose one tenth of requests
cannot succeed under the supplied environment, while the remaining nine
tenths have independent per-attempt failure probability one tenth. Three
attempts then succeed with probability
\[
 \frac9{10}\left(1-\frac1{10^3}\right)=0.8991,
\]
and require $0.1(3)+0.9(1+0.1+0.01)=1.299$ attempts on average.
The marginal first-attempt failure probability is $0.19$. Treating that
marginal value as independent across retries would predict
$1-0.19^3=0.993141$, substantially overstating success. The retry has not
changed an unavailable dependency, an unsupported method or contradictory
input declarations. Operational classification should distinguish those
persistent causes from a recoverable interruption.

A bounded retry policy also retains its original time account. In the
inspected report path, remaining time is computed from the job creation
timestamp and original wall budget, and the worker-start count is capped at
three. Restarting does not intentionally grant three new full deadlines.
The implementation uses local wall-clock timestamps and operating-system
timers; this is not a distributed clock or a hard real-time guarantee.
Launch overhead, host suspension, clock adjustment and recovery of a failed
machine require a target-environment study before making a service-level
claim~\citep{exec13_ops_source}.

Statistical retries need an additional distinction. Replaying an interrupted
calculation with preserved random state is different from drawing new
randomness until a desired conclusion appears. If three independent valid
null $p$-values are generated and the smallest is selected, the probability
of at least one value below $0.05$ is
\[
 1-(1-0.05)^3=0.142625.
\]
This exact counterexample assumes independent uniform null $p$-values;
it does not allege that the runtime performs such selection. It shows why
the proposed adapter must separate mechanical recovery from a new statistical
replicate and preserve all requested analyses. The same issue arises when
timeouts depend on difficult data and only easy completed fits enter a
coverage report~\citep{exec13_ops_exact}.

\section{Resource budgets and cancellation at the right boundary}

The local worker sets an address-space limit and a wall-time timer. The
coordinator starts a fixed worker entry point, collects its output and
validates the canonical response against the requested output size. This
supports a bounded set of local operations. It does not impose one aggregate
memory bound on the worker, coordinator, SDK and all clients, and the output
check is applied after collection rather than as an incremental bound on an
arbitrary producer's stream~\citep{exec13_ops_source}.

For a proposed third-party numerical adapter, admission should therefore
include peak resident memory of the whole workflow, temporary disk use,
serialization and parent-process buffers. A limit that is safe for a short
report may be inappropriate for an estimator returning a large covariance
matrix. If a result exceeds the public response size, the design can publish
a separately bounded artifact with explicit custody and expose a small
reference. It must retain the scientific object's meaning and cannot silently
truncate interval components or omit unsuccessful fits to meet a size limit.

Cancellation is a race between a request and the computation's next state
transition. For pure report generation, a useful rule is that an accepted
cancellation recorded before the publication transition prevents a new public
result; cancellation after
publication returns the actual completed state. The inspected implementation
checks a cancellation flag around report work and before publication. That
cooperative behavior does not guarantee that every numerical kernel can be
interrupted at an arbitrary instruction. A later adapter may need worker
termination and a rule for discarding uncommitted artifacts.

A timeout should be recorded as an execution outcome. A scientifically
unidentified effect can instead be a completed result with an explicit
scientific limitation. Converting both into one generic failure statistic
obscures the remedy: the first may need resource or implementation work, while
the second may need a different target, new information or abstention. A
successful process exit likewise says nothing by itself about whether the
effect is precise enough to support a decision.

\section{Ownership and a reversible adoption path}

Operational ownership follows the claim being made. A method maintainer owns
the supported algorithm and numerical domain. The common-library owner owns
the request/result contract, method-version binding and admitted conversions.
The consumer owns the displayed target, units and business action. A later
bank study additionally needs a data owner for the actual observation and
assignment processes and a decision owner for losses and feasible actions.
These are proposed responsibilities, not names or approvals that have already
been supplied.

For example, a deposit report may use a valid backend estimate while a
consumer interprets the coefficient as currency rather than thousands of
currency units. The remedy belongs partly in the shared unit contract and
partly in the consuming application's acceptance examples. A central
numerical team cannot certify a silently altered presentation. Conversely,
an application owner cannot declare a confidence procedure valid merely
because the resulting interval is displayed correctly.

The proposal should make an adoption decision reversible at its natural
boundaries. Retain the incumbent expert workflow and its artifacts while a
new adapter is evaluated on matched public/generated requests. Publish both
methods' complete outputs with their own identities; compare discrepancies
before replacing the default. A schema migration should have a declared
mapping and refusal cases for information it cannot preserve. Where a new
method changes the estimand, the migration is a new scientific analysis,
not a formatting conversion. A rollback retains access to the previously
admitted version and evidence without rewriting its result as if produced
by the new version.

The same approach applies to workspace consumers. Read-only inspection of a
repository can reveal candidate objects and interfaces. It cannot establish
that its owner accepts the proposed contract, that its launch environment is
compatible, or that an integration saves work. A local mock consumer can test
the proposed request and response boundary now. Actual consumer execution,
deployment ownership and institutional operation remain distinct later
claims, with their own narrowly defined studies.

\section{The economic denominator is every attempted request}

Let $R$ denote whether a request returns a usable result and $D$ its incremental
decision value relative to the incumbent workflow, including the specified
fallback when $R=0$. Let $C$ include all request-specific compute, review,
retry and recovery costs. The per-request economic target is
\[
 \mathbb E[D-C],
\]
plus a consistent allocation of fixed construction and shared operating
costs. Reporting $\mathbb E[D\mid R=1]$ with a nominal successful-run cost
answers a different question. Reliability and economic comparisons require
both the success probability and what happens on the unsuccessful branch.

In an exact stipulated example, 70\% of requests are easy, complete and add
USD~10 of gross value. Another 15\% complete but add USD~$-30$. The remaining
15\% fail and revert to the baseline action, adding zero gross value but
requiring USD~20 of recovery work. Every attempt costs USD~2 in tools and
computation. The completed-only calculation reports
\[
 \frac{0.70(10)+0.15(-30)}{0.85}-2
 =\frac{16}{17}\simeq0.941
\]
USD per completed request. The all-attempt account instead gives
\[
 0.70(10)+0.15(-30)-2-0.15(20)=-2.5
\]
USD per attempted request. The apparent gain changes sign when the
unsuccessful work and correct denominator enter the account. These numbers
are generated planning assumptions, not workflow prices or measured bank
returns~\citep{exec13_ops_exact}.

Measurement should therefore retain attempted task identity, terminal
execution state, scientific disposition, usable-result status, fallback
action and disjoint cost categories. Repeated attempts are costs within a
request, not new independent banking opportunities. Correlated requests from
one institution, calendar or scientific task family also cannot be treated
as independent evidence merely because their request identifiers differ.
The analysis unit should follow the source of independent information.

A prototype can measure machine resources and trace whether required fields
survive recovery. It cannot price saved analyst time without observing a
matched workflow, nor infer business value from seconds saved. The next
inexpensive operational study should compare complete local workflows under
declared faults and budgets, preserve adverse results, and report source and
environment identities. Only a subsequent justified platform or bank study
can supply institution-specific availability, ownership, labor, and
decision-value evidence. Their absence limits those claims while leaving
the public/generated proposal work executable.

\section{The next complete qualification}

The remaining engineering route is concrete: choose source-audited packages
and permitted integration forms, implement representative bridges, and run
matched consumer workflows across all three surfaces. The trial must include
unsupported methods, late observations, graph ambiguity, weak or disconnected
effect sets, interruption and changed-input rejection. Passing results should
name the actual supported environments and domains.

This work will close an engineering gap only in those domains. Negative
persistent-map, latent-graph and dependent-learner studies remain scientific
obligations. Independent review, authentic bank validation and measured
economics remain additional gates. A coherent runtime makes their required
inputs and outputs reviewable; it does not turn missing information into an
accepted causal answer.

\label{exec13:operations-end}

\section{SAS: preserve the boundary between statistical procedures and services}
\label{sec:exec24-sas-reuse}

A universal bank's SAS estate may contain statistical procedures, historical
econometric models, a Viya platform and open clients that call particular
services. These are related components with different scientific and operating
contracts. The proposal retains the documented workflows as references and
defines conditional integration at the procedure and service level. A Python
client's availability cannot establish that a bank owns the required server
component, that a supplied structural model is identified, or that an
asynchronous job returned a usable causal result
\cite{exec13_latent_sas_calis,exec23_workflow_sasctl,
exec23_workflow_delegates_sasctl,exec24_sas_choice}.

\subsection{Edition and component identity constrain the comparison}
The retained scientific evidence includes explicitly archived SAS/STAT 14.1
and SAS/ETS 14.1 pages. The latter are adjacent econometric comparisons,
not a declaration that every SAS/STAT or Viya entitlement includes them.
The selected spatial-regression guide declares 2023.10 and carries an
August 2024 document date. These identities remain separate from a current
installation, supported server release and exact original bytes at the
7 October 2026 cutoff. Selected HTML equations are image-based; inspected
prose supports the vendor claims, while the finite equations below are
independently authored
\cite{exec13_ct_sas_causal,exec13_ivrd_sas,
exec20_network_sas_latest_spatial,exec24_sas_choice}.

The open sasctl client is inspected at the retained 26 August 2026 revision.
Its README documents Python-module and command-line use. Its own root notice
declares Apache License 2.0; this is not an entitlement to SAS/STAT, SAS Viya
or every server API. The separate REST sample repository is explicitly
described as a preview. Its Job Execution example's document version and
historical update date are not a supported server compatibility matrix
\cite{exec23_workflow_sasctl,exec24_workflow_contracts_sas}.

\subsection{A fitted structural model preserves its supplied assumptions}
The CALIS overview documents observed and latent structural models,
measurement error, path specifications, constraints and reciprocal relations.
It distinguishes normal-theory maximum likelihood, Satorra--Bentler adjusted
inference, and an outlier-downweighting option that the procedure calls
robust. Those alternatives should not be collapsed into one flag. The
documented full-information missing-data route assumes missing at random;
a successful optimizer does not verify that assumption
\cite{exec13_latent_sas_calis}.

An authored Gaussian example shows why covariance fit does not settle an
intervention direction. For independent standard-normal disturbances, one
model is
\[
 X=U,\qquad Y=\tfrac12X+\sqrt{3/4}\,V.
\]
A second model reverses the direction:
\[
 Y=U',\qquad X=\tfrac12Y+\sqrt{3/4}\,V'.
\]
Both have zero means, unit variances and covariance one half. Setting $X=x$
in the first model changes the mean of $Y$ at rate one half; setting it in
the second changes that mean at rate zero. This is an exact model witness,
not an executed CALIS comparison. A generated path diagram must retain the
business mechanism and identifying restrictions that distinguish the two
models, rather than accepting whichever orientation gives a convenient
story \cite{exec24_sas_choice}.

The SYSLIN documentation similarly treats instruments as specified inputs:
the listed variables enter first-stage regressions for the relevant
estimators. Declaring those variables does not prove exclusion or their
relationship to omitted disturbances. The VARMAX CAUSAL statement tests
specified Granger restrictions; its label does not automatically identify
a bank intervention. The dynamic simultaneous-equations representation is
another declared model representation, not evidence that an unrestricted
shock interpretation has been learned
\cite{exec13_ivrd_sas,exec13_ct_sas_causal,exec13_ct_sas_structural}.

\subsection{Event histories require the information available at each time}
The PHREG overview provides a concrete strength relative to a generic
single-record treatment interface: time-dependent explanatory variables,
counting-process input, recurrent events and left truncation are explicitly
discussed. It also discusses clustered failure times and different methods
for tied times. The adapter should preserve entry and exit times, event
types, subject and cluster identity, time units and the selected method
\cite{exec14_survival_sas}.

Support for a changing covariate does not establish that the covariate was
known when the bank acted, or that conditioning on it identifies a dynamic
treatment strategy. In an authored four-account example, let the eventual
event indicators be zero, zero, one and one. Copying those future outcomes
into an alleged baseline covariate gives perfect prediction by construction.
It provides no feasible baseline decision rule. A public fixture should
reject this timestamp violation even when its numerical fit is excellent.
With treatment-dependent intermediate variables, the proposed scientific
contract must additionally specify the longitudinal intervention and the
assumptions supporting its estimator
\cite{exec24_sas_choice}.

The selected spatial-regression documentation adds a further target
distinction. Dependence through a supplied spatial matrix, direct and
indirect effects, and the banking action that changes a network exposure
need separate definitions. The existing spatial comparison retains those
conditions. No product-wide permission to infer causality follows from
having both a survival procedure and a spatial procedure available
\cite{exec20_network_sas_latest_spatial,exec24_sas_choice}.

\subsection{Missing outcomes remain a scientific sensitivity question}
The MI and MIANALYZE manuals distinguish imputation, completed-data analysis
and pooling of estimates with their uncertainty. The assumptions pages
state missing at random and distinguish the data-model parameters from
the missingness-model parameters. The sensitivity discussion treats
pattern-mixture and selection-model factorizations separately; the
inspected edition implements the described pattern-mixture route and
explicitly says its MI procedure does not provide the selection-model
approach discussed there. These are scoped edition-specific statements
\cite{exec21_transport_sas_mi_intro,exec21_transport_sas_mianalyze_intro,
exec21_transport_sas_assumptions,exec21_transport_sas_sensitivity}.

For an authored bounded outcome, suppose exactly half the population is
observed, its observed mean is $1/5$, and every outcome lies between zero
and one. If the missing half has mean $m$, the population mean is
\[
 \mu=\tfrac12\cdot\tfrac15+\tfrac12m,
 \qquad 0\leq m\leq1.
\]
The observed information permits means from $1/10$ to $3/5$. For a
hypothetical 10,000 accounts and 1,000 USD per unit outcome, the associated
expected loss ranges from 1,000,000 to 6,000,000 USD. Imputing one value
selects a restriction; it does not learn the missing population from the
observations alone. Public sensitivity tests can reproduce these endpoints,
while actual bank missingness needs further information or justified
restrictions \cite{exec24_sas_choice}.

The pooled covariance and transformation scale must also survive export.
The retained combining-inferences discussion belongs to the uncertainty
contract, not to an optional presentation layer. An agent should record
which imputation model, analysis model, assumptions, overrides and failed
fits contributed to a result before narrating a business recommendation
\cite{exec21_transport_sas_combining,exec21_transport_sas_mianalyze_intro,
exec24_sas_choice}.

\subsection{Terminal jobs and bounded polling are different guarantees}
The inspected sasctl generic job monitor treats completed and failed as
terminal states. Returning a terminal job therefore does not by itself
mean success. Its refresh limit counts requests and its loop sleeps half
a second per refresh; the selected request delegate separately accepts a
timeout argument whose default is None. This source inspection does not
prove that every service uses this helper, nor does it establish actual
server behavior \cite{exec23_workflow_delegates_sasctl}.

An authored timing model makes the required contract explicit. Sixty
polls with a half-second sleep and one-second request duration take
90 seconds; with sixty-second request duration they take 3,630 seconds.
A bound on poll count alone cannot bound wall time without a request-time
bound. A proposed worker therefore needs an end-to-end deadline, explicit
request limits and a typed unresolved state after local expiry. Cancellation
and recovery of the remote job require separately qualified semantics
\cite{exec24_sas_choice}.

The selected score-polling method has a different loop and return contract;
its timeout branch appears inside the loop, without an explicit return
after loop exit. The workflow class carries an experimental warning about
its partial implementation and historical documentation status. That
warning is preserved as a claim about the inspected source, not recast as
a verified statement about every present-day API. The request delegate's
token-refresh retry and its tests' mocked HTTP operations likewise require
public fault and recovery fixtures before native qualification
\cite{exec23_workflow_sasctl,exec23_workflow_delegates_sasctl}.

The historical Job Execution sample separates definitions, execution jobs,
states, errors, results and cleanup. Its result map is provider-specific.
Visual Investigator's BPMN case-management workflow is a different context;
it must not be substituted for a generic analytical workflow merely because
both use the word workflow. A CLI or MCP response must retain the server
profile, request identity, provider, terminal state and result schema
\cite{exec24_workflow_contracts_sas}.

\subsection{Pagination and complete costs matter to scientific results}
The inspected client pagination uses offsets and limits derived from links,
and its item count is documented as approximate. This does not establish
a snapshot-consistent analysis population. In an authored example, the
first page of the ordered list $(a,b,c,d)$ is $(a,b)$. Inserting $x$ at the
front before fetching offset two produces the second page $(b,c)$. Four
returned records contain three unique original accounts and omit $d$.
This conditional witness is not a native SAS failure; it specifies a
test for immutable extraction, stable identities and changing populations
\cite{exec23_workflow_delegates_sasctl,exec24_sas_choice}.

The reference route is retained for the named statistical and operational
contracts. Conditional integration requires a supported entitled procedure
or service plus public fixtures. Direct adoption as the complete causal
product is deferred. Open-client reuse or porting needs the actual selected
component's notices and dependencies; proprietary statistical implementations
cannot be ported on the basis of an open wrapper's license. Unsupported
causal, timing and success claims are rejected without rejecting every
bounded use of the components \cite{exec24_sas_choice}.

Scientific owners must specify targets, assumptions and loss; statistical
owners must specify event and missing-data laws; adapter owners must retain
model, time and extraction semantics; platform owners must establish exact
service support, rights and failure recovery. Hypothetical expenditure of
36,000 USD over 1,200 submitted, 900 completed and 600 qualified requests
gives 30, 40 and 60 USD respectively. Actual prices and economic value
remain unmeasured. Remaining treatment, panel, discovery and service scopes
need exact primary evidence; the present selection is not an exhaustive
inventory. Package execution and independent validation remain to be performed \cite{exec24_sas_choice}.

\subsection{Pagination and complete costs matter to scientific results}
The inspected client pagination uses offsets and limits derived from links,
and its item count is documented as approximate. This does not establish
a snapshot-consistent analysis population. In an authored example, the
first page of the ordered list $(a,b,c,d)$ is $(a,b)$. Inserting $x$ at the
front before fetching offset two produces the second page $(b,c)$. Four
returned records contain three unique original accounts and omit $d$.
This conditional witness is not a native SAS failure; it specifies a
test for immutable extraction, stable identities and changing populations
\citep{exec23_workflow_delegates_sasctl,exec24_sas_choice}.

The reference route is retained for the named statistical and operational
contracts. Conditional integration requires a supported entitled procedure
or service plus public fixtures. Direct adoption as the complete causal
product is deferred. Open-client reuse or porting needs the actual selected
component's notices and dependencies; proprietary statistical implementations
cannot be ported on the basis of an open wrapper's license. Unsupported
causal, timing and success claims are rejected without rejecting every
bounded use of the components \citep{exec24_sas_choice}.

Scientific owners must specify targets, assumptions and loss; statistical
owners must specify event and missing-data laws; adapter owners must retain
model, time and extraction semantics; platform owners must establish exact
service support, rights and failure recovery. Hypothetical expenditure of
36,000 USD over 1,200 submitted, 900 completed and 600 qualified requests
gives 30, 40 and 60 USD respectively. Actual prices and economic value
remain unmeasured. Remaining treatment, panel, discovery and service scopes
need exact primary evidence; the present selection is not an exhaustive
inventory. Package execution and independent validation remain to be performed \citep{exec24_sas_choice}.

\section{Data and code agents: a fail-closed banking boundary}
\label{exec13:data-code-agents}

An agent that prepares data or code can save analyst time while silently changing a causal question. The proposed boundary starts with a typed decision contract and uses the agent for retrieval, clarification, code drafting and criticism around fixed operations. It does not execute arbitrary notebook or shell text, download mutable ontologies, or convert malformed output into an empty successful analysis. This is a proposal architecture supported by inspected papers, package source and local adverse fixtures; it is not a live-model performance result.

Suppose a bank asks whether an early arrears review should be offered to eligible accounts. The unit is the account at its first qualifying arrears date. The action $A$ is an offer made using data available immediately before that date, and $Y$ is discounted net recovery over 180 days. The target is $\tau_P=E_P[Y(1)-Y(0)]$ for the declared eligible population $P$, with the offer cost either inside $Y$ or subtracted once in the decision rule. A field's event date and its database availability date are separate: a hardship flag entered on day $11$ cannot be a day-$10$ covariate. The agent may list candidate fields and ask an analyst to resolve ownership, timing, interference and missingness; it cannot infer those facts from column names.

The non-agent baseline is a structured analyst interview, a versioned data dictionary and manually reviewed code. The agent-assisted path adds a typed specification, source-to-claim links, a graph candidate set, fixed operation requests and deterministic report rendering. Both paths receive the same information and the same numerical fixtures. The comparison should score target preservation, clock errors, unsupported certainty, unresolved questions, artifact completeness and analyst time. A shorter answer is not better if it changes $P$, $A$, $Y$ or the horizon.

\subsection{What the inspected frontier contributes}

CausalAgent describes processing, structure-learning and reporting agents routed through MCP tools and demonstrates a Sachs protein-signalling workflow. Its paper lists quantitative effect estimation and counterfactual modules as future work. It therefore supplies an interaction and routing idea, not evidence that a bank servicing effect was estimated. The inspected pinned server declares PC and OLC tools, but its OLC call is not imported or defined in the selected module. Its JSON helper extracts text between the first and last braces and returns an empty dictionary on decoding failure. The proposal retains a typed refusal or malformed-result state instead of accepting that empty object as success. \cite{exec13_data_causalagent,exec13_data_causalagent_code}

The human-augmenting OCI workflow is closer to this target. It places a human principal over specifications, templated notebooks, actor/critic review and overlap diagnostics, and reports public ACIC and LaLonde evaluations. Those are source-reported evaluations, not a live run here. Its pinned notebook labels a uniform AIPW mean after propensity trimming as ATO. With two equally frequent strata, propensities $0.2,0.5$ and effects $0,10$, the retained-population mean is $5$, while conventional overlap weighting gives $6.09756$. The label cannot change the estimand. Our adapter would retain retained indices, weights, target and trimming rule. \cite{exec13_data_oci,exec13_data_oci_code}

CausalDS is useful as a benchmark design because it separates scenes, observations, identification decisions, private structural ground truth and scoring artifacts. Its scorer treats abstention as correct only when the task is explicitly abstainable and the model intentionally returns a null-equivalent answer. It separately records interval width, coverage and interval score, with both uncapped and capped normalized scores. The source also has nullable identification states and branches where missing metadata can default toward an identifiable interpretation. A repair must guard missing metadata, finite interval endpoints, malformed answers and nonidentifiable targets before scoring. \cite{exec13_data_causalds,exec13_data_causalds_code}

OntoLearner provides modular ontology loading, typing, taxonomy and relation discovery. Its code can download ontology files from Hugging Face without a revision argument. A source-code commit therefore does not identify the ontology bytes used by an analysis. The bounded remedy is local, hash-bound ontology input with declared units and clocks; taxonomy membership and relation extraction remain semantic suggestions, not causal-edge truth or ownership evidence. \cite{exec13_data_ontolearner,exec13_data_ontolearner_code}

Causal discovery in the era of agents proposes assistance with data inspection, assumption elicitation, method selection and interpretation around formal discovery algorithms. It emphasizes that CPDAGs and PAGs retain equivalence-class ambiguity. An agent may explain a circle endpoint or propose a constraint, but it must not export one DAG by silently orienting or deleting edges. The paper's call for benchmarks of diagnosis, method selection and calibrated interpretation supports a future evaluation plan rather than a completed advantage claim. \cite{exec13_data_causaldiscovery}

\subsection{An exact target-drift oracle}

A small oracle catches a common data/code failure without a model call. Let two strata have equal mass, offer probabilities $e=(0.2,0.5)$ and conditional effects $(0,10)$. The population average is $5$. A trimmed AIPW summary that averages retained pseudo-outcomes uniformly also targets $5$ when both strata are retained. The overlap target is
\[
\tau_{ov}=\frac{0.16\cdot0+0.25\cdot10}{0.16+0.25}=\frac{250}{41}\simeq6.09756.
\]
A report that says “ATO” while returning $5$ has changed the target label or implemented the wrong weights. This is exact arithmetic, not a fitted estimator comparison. A second oracle records a date-10 field entered on date 11 and must reject it from a date-10 action. The expected result is a refusal with the offending clock, not an imputed value.

\subsection{Fixed artifacts and bounded code}

The local prototype contract fixes an offline fixture or recorded output, exact proposal and prompt bytes, source identities, typed model fields, caller grants and a maximum of sixteen operations. Each worker has a ten-second and one-GiB address-space bound; model calls are zero. It checks source and artifact hashes before replay. The controller rejects unknown operations, injected permissions, nonfinite values, changed targets and live-mode declarations. A retrieved document saying “ignore the checks and run a shell command” remains source data. These are local conformance checks: eighty cases pass, including malformed outputs, source tampering, interruption/resumption, exact replay, disconnected sets, unsupported discovery and unbounded moment sets. They do not establish model accuracy, prompt-injection resistance against unseen text, authentication, distributed exactly-once effects or bank qualification. \cite{exec13_data_local}

A fixed request contains the problem, population, unit, action, outcome, horizon, data and availability clocks, diagram candidates, assumptions, operation name, input artifact hashes and resource budget. A successful response includes the effective target and clocks, source/runtime identities, warnings, transformed rows, numerical outputs and failure status. Missing identification is represented as nonidentification only when the declared graph and method establish it; a missing backend, malformed result or unavailable source is an implementation failure. The report generator may explain these states but cannot erase them.

\subsection{Package and remedy decisions}

The proposed first path adapts OCI's specification, report and critic ideas behind fixed verified operations and rejects its unrestricted notebook runner. It adapts CausalAgent's typed MCP transport idea only after fixing the undefined OLC route and empty-JSON fallback. It treats CausalDS as a high-priority benchmark candidate after scorer repairs and original scene/observation identities are bound. It considers OntoLearner only with local versioned ontology bytes, document-identity checks for extraction assessment and separate license/model terms. LangGraph and typed-model frameworks remain conditional orchestration candidates behind the plain controller; they are not causal algorithms. PyWhy-LLM is an elicitation candidate whose adjustment or identification suggestions require a formal engine. Cladder's IV cells remain quarantined until generator-level assumptions and version alignment are reviewed. Unlicensed or source-paper/code-misaligned leads remain deferred.

The next experiment is an offline public or generated task set with a frozen brief, deterministic structured-interview baseline, fixed prompts and split, target/clock/diagram rubrics, malformed and refusal cases, resource budget and stopping rule. It should measure semantic preservation and adverse-case handling before any live backend call. A later live-model comparison needs a named provider, custody, price and independent adjudication; none is claimed here. Authentic bank truth, production reliability and customer economics remain later conditional evidence.
