Before:
~~~text
\section{Choosing an agent framework without changing the causal question}
\label{sec:exec24-framework-census}

An agent framework can help a bank turn a loosely specified business request
into a sequence of inspectable analytical tasks. It can retain a conversation,
route work, call a causal engine and recover an interrupted calculation. The
scientific question remains separate: what intervention is proposed, for whom,
at what information time, under which assumptions, and with what uncertainty?
The useful comparison is therefore between concrete execution contracts and
their ability to preserve that question. A returned sentence, a completed
workflow and a qualified causal recommendation are distinct outcomes
\cite{exec24_framework_contracts}.

Consider a request to increase retention among accounts at risk of leaving.
An assistant can elicit whether the action is a fee waiver, a contact policy
or a credit-limit change; identify the decision date; retrieve a data
dictionary; propose competing graphs; and submit an explicit intervention
query. Every step can be useful before a production product exists. Public
fixtures can test whether the assistant preserves treatment versions,
account histories, unresolved confounding and refusal messages. A later
bank experiment is justified only after these cheaper checks demonstrate
that the proposed chain addresses the relevant scientific problem
\cite{exec24_framework_contracts}.

\subsection{Source profiles and dependencies are part of the comparison}
The inspected LangChain repository contains distinct declarations for
modern LangChain 1.4.3, core 1.6.7 and classic 1.0.8. The modern package
declares a LangGraph range, rather than implementing every execution layer
itself. The separately retained LangGraph source declares 1.2.14.
Comparing the packages as independent causal engines would double-count
the shared orchestration dependency and misstate what either provides
\cite{exec24_framework_langchain,v12_la04_langgraph}.

The other inspected profiles are Semantic Kernel's Python 1.45.0,
DSPy 3.4.0, LlamaIndex core 0.14.25 and a Haystack source declaration of
3.4.0-rc0. A release-candidate label must survive the comparison; it is
not silently promoted to a stable distribution. LlamaIndex's workflow
modules re-export another package. The traced repository resolves to
\texttt{run-llama/llama-agents}, where the selected package declares
\texttt{llama-index-workflows} 2.25.0. This declaration fits core's
specified range, but no solved environment or native compatibility test
has been performed
\cite{exec24_framework_semantic_kernel,exec24_framework_dspy,
exec24_framework_llama_index,exec24_framework_haystack,
exec24_framework_workflows}.

These are authenticated source revisions with commit dates no later than
7 October 2026, inspected from retained original bytes. They are not
claims about the latest release, a bank's installed version, or all
permitted dependency combinations. Root notices for the selected
LangChain, Semantic Kernel, DSPy, LlamaIndex and workflow sources are MIT;
Haystack's selected root notice is Apache License 2.0. AutoGen's earlier
review keeps its AgentChat code notice separate from its documentation
notice. Complete dependency, model-weight, connector and hosted-service
rights remain component-specific inputs
\cite{exec24_framework_langchain,exec24_framework_semantic_kernel,
exec24_framework_dspy,exec24_framework_llama_index,
exec24_framework_haystack,exec24_framework_workflows,v12_la04_autogen}.

\subsection{LangChain and LangGraph: graph recovery is not side-effect recovery}
The modern LangChain factory constructs a state graph and passes a
checkpointer, store and interrupt boundaries into compilation. This is
a concrete route for retaining the business brief, candidate graphs,
assumption decisions and tool results. The factory's configured recursion
limit is a graph-execution control; it is not a token budget, monetary
budget or end-to-end service deadline
\cite{exec24_framework_langchain}.

The retained LangGraph interrupt documentation states that resumption
restarts the node and re-executes its logic. A checkpointer is required
for the documented interrupt route. These properties support recoverable
analysis, but preceding external actions need their own replay contract.
If a node creates a paid external job before the interrupt, restored graph
state does not by itself prove that the job can safely be created again
\cite{v12_la04_langgraph,exec24_framework_contracts}.

The inspected modern retry middleware makes a useful further distinction.
It counts the initial attempt plus the configured retries, propagates
graph control-flow exceptions, and treats nonmatching exceptions separately.
After exhaustion, the tool middleware can return a tool message explicitly
marked as an error; the model middleware can return an assistant message
containing failure information. Both also permit an error-raising route.
A wrapper that tests only whether a message exists would erase the
difference between recovered output and reported failure
\cite{exec24_framework_langchain}.

An authored banking example specifies the resulting public test. Suppose
an external service accepts a 500 USD action, but its acknowledgement is
lost. Three submissions without a shared deduplication key can represent
1,500 USD of actions. Under an explicitly stipulated service contract
that deduplicates the same key, they represent 500 USD. The 1,000 USD
difference is not an observed framework defect; it is the consequence
of different external contracts. The proposed adapter must preserve the
logical action key, attempt identity, acknowledgement state and recovery
query. Retrying an unidentified causal request also does not repair its
scientific assumptions \cite{exec24_framework_contracts}.

LangChain and LangGraph are retained as reference orchestration choices,
with conditional integration through typed causal-engine tools. Direct
adoption as the scientific product is deferred. Porting a small source
mechanism is an alternative only when its dependency and notice obligations
are understood and its semantics can be maintained. A custom controller
may be simpler for a narrowly bounded workflow; the comparison should
measure that alternative on the same recovery and refusal fixtures
\cite{exec24_framework_contracts}.

\subsection{AutoGen: conversational state and scientific state are different}
The retained AutoGen AgentChat 0.7.5 source says that its assistant retains
state across calls and should receive new messages rather than the whole
conversation again. It warns against concurrent calls on the same agent
instance. The documented tool behavior can involve concurrent tool calls
and an additional model call for reflection. Its save/load methods retain
model context; they do not establish transactional recovery of arbitrary
external side effects
\cite{v12_la04_autogen}.

For the retention example, separate conversational roles can propose
assumptions, challenge them and explain results. Agreement among those
roles is not independent scientific evidence if they share the same
model, data, prompt history or mistaken business premise. Their graph
proposals should enter a comparison set with provenance, not become
accepted orientations because a conversation reached consensus. Scientific
state must include the graph object, query, assumptions, identification
result and uncertainty object independently of the natural-language history
\cite{exec24_framework_contracts}.

The pinned README declares maintenance mode and recommends a successor.
That declaration informs a maintenance decision; the successor's advertised
properties are not established here by repeating the README. Reference
use and an existing-installation adapter remain possible, while a new
deployment decision needs an independently reviewed migration target and
matched fixtures. The proposal therefore defers unconditional adoption,
retains a conditional integration route, and records maintenance and
component-specific rights as explicit revisit conditions
\cite{v12_la04_autogen,exec24_framework_contracts}.

\subsection{Semantic Kernel: function filters do not verify scientific claims}
The inspected Python function-choice behavior exposes included/excluded
plugins and functions, and a maximum automatic-invocation setting. Its
kernel checks required and unexpected argument names, constructs an
invocation-filter stack, and can return a termination context. These are
useful controls for exposing only the intended causal tools at a given
stage. They do not verify the truth of a proposed exclusion restriction
or the adequacy of an adjustment set
\cite{exec24_framework_semantic_kernel}.

The selected automatic-invocation handler catches ordinary function
exceptions and places error text in a function result. A separate guard
is therefore needed before a later assistant message is accepted as a
qualified answer. The proposed protocol distinguishes an invalid request,
an unavailable service, a scientific refusal, a partial numerical result
and a successful calculation with stated assumptions. Argument-schema
validity is one condition among these, not their replacement
\cite{exec24_framework_semantic_kernel,exec24_framework_contracts}.

This review covers the selected Python profile. It does not transfer its
behavior to .NET, Java or every provider connector. Conditional integration
would expose a narrow tool set, retain scientific output objects and
test filters, failure results and termination using public fixtures.
Reference use is retained; broad cross-language parity and direct adoption
as the causal library are deferred. Porting requires separately inspecting
the actual component and maintaining its conversion contract
\cite{exec24_framework_contracts}.

\subsection{DSPy: optimizing a program requires a defensible evaluator}
The inspected ReAct implementation builds a trajectory, calls selected
tools and records execution exceptions as observations. It may leave the
tool loop after an invalid selection or context-window problem and then
run an extraction step. This is a useful mechanism for explaining partial
work, but the extraction step is not proof that the requested causal
calculation succeeded. The result must retain whether identification,
estimation and uncertainty checks actually completed
\cite{exec24_framework_dspy}.

The evaluation implementation supplies a particularly relevant positive
contract: after a returned evaluation run, missing per-example results
receive the configured failure score, and the aggregate denominator is
the full supplied development set. That guards against silently reporting
only successful examples in that code path. If the executor raises at
its error threshold, however, no completed aggregate should be invented.
The task definition, scorer, allowed failure score and failure threshold
must accompany every reported benchmark
\cite{exec24_framework_dspy}.

In an authored example, 1,000 requests produce 800 returned answers and
600 scientifically qualified answers. The qualified fraction among
returns is $600/800=3/4$, while the fraction among all requests is
$600/1000=3/5$. These answer different questions. Neither fraction alone
measures causal calibration, utility or the severity of unqualified
answers. A public experiment should report the complete request ledger,
refusals, errors, qualified answers and the prespecified loss assigned to
each outcome \cite{exec24_framework_contracts}.

The inspected parallel executor also deserves careful source-level
qualification. It can resubmit stragglers and stores completed outcomes
by input index, while a resubmission set is keyed by Future objects.
The nearby comment describing one resubmission per item is therefore not
by itself a proved per-item invariant: distinct Future identities can
refer to the same input. No native liveness or duplicate-work failure is
asserted here. A public test must trace the input key and every submission,
including work that continues after a useful result has been collected
\cite{exec24_framework_dspy,exec24_framework_contracts}.

DSPy is retained as a reference for program construction and evaluation,
with conditional integration around a fixed causal-task scorer. The
scorer must distinguish graph prediction, identification, numerical
estimation, uncertainty and business loss. Optimizing on the same examples
later used to claim performance would change the evaluation question.
Adoption as a causal oracle is rejected; bounded program optimization and
selective source reuse remain testable alternatives
\cite{exec24_framework_contracts}.

\subsection{LlamaIndex: stopping, structured output and runtime delegation}
The selected LlamaIndex base agent keeps iteration counts in context.
At its limit, the inspected path either raises or performs a final model
generation, depending on the chosen early-stopping method. A generated
summary after exhausting the budget is useful communication, but its
scientific status must remain partial or unresolved when necessary.
The selected function-agent code also distinguishes ordinary tool output
from a return-direct route and from handoff behavior
\cite{exec24_framework_llama_index}.

The separate workflows package makes the time contract especially clear.
Its selected constructor documents timeout in known-alive seconds accrued
through processed journal ticks; downtime during resumption and some
pre-crash time do not count. This is a different clock from an external
bank service deadline. In an authored example, two 20-second active
periods separated by a one-hour outage total 40 active seconds but
3,640 elapsed seconds. A caller needing a 60-second wall deadline cannot
infer it from the active-time limit
\cite{exec24_framework_workflows,exec24_framework_contracts}.

The inspected cancellation method signals the runtime and waits for the
result, while catching timeout, cancellation and other exceptions. Its
return therefore does not independently prove that every remote side
effect has stopped. The retry-policy source separately defines retry
predicates, delays and stopping conditions. These concrete distinctions
support an adapter design with external job reconciliation, explicit
deadline clocks and durable attempt identifiers. They do not establish
that the complete distributed runtime has been qualified
\cite{exec24_framework_workflows,exec24_framework_contracts}.

Conditional integration is attractive when document retrieval and a
workflow context are needed together, provided retrieved statements stay
traceable to inspected source material. Reference use is retained and
direct adoption as the scientific layer is deferred. The actual delegated
runtime, serializer, persistence backend and model connector need their
own fixture results. A source-level range match is only the start of

the current public state. A tool-based exit checks error information;
the selected logic does not treat an errored exit-condition tool as a
successful exit. These are valuable details to preserve when comparing
returned results
\cite{exec24_framework_haystack}.

an after-run hook can alter the final state. These facilities can reduce

adapter must therefore define and validate the causal result itself
~~~

~~~text
\section{Choosing an agent framework without changing the causal question}
\label{sec:exec24-framework-census}

An agent framework can help a bank turn a loosely specified business request
into a sequence of inspectable analytical tasks. It can retain a conversation,
route work, call a causal engine and recover an interrupted calculation. The
scientific question remains separate: what intervention is proposed, for whom,
at what information time, under which assumptions, and with what uncertainty?
The useful comparison is therefore between concrete execution contracts and
their ability to preserve that question. A returned sentence, a completed
workflow and a qualified causal recommendation are distinct outcomes
\citep{exec24_framework_contracts}.

Consider a request to increase retention among accounts at risk of leaving.
An assistant can elicit whether the action is a fee waiver, a contact policy
or a credit-limit change; identify the decision date; retrieve a data
dictionary; propose competing graphs; and submit an explicit intervention
query. Every step can be useful before a production product exists. Public
fixtures can test whether the assistant preserves treatment versions,
account histories, unresolved confounding and refusal messages. A later
bank experiment is justified only after these cheaper checks demonstrate
that the proposed chain addresses the relevant scientific problem
\citep{exec24_framework_contracts}.

\subsection{Source profiles and dependencies are part of the comparison}
The inspected LangChain repository contains distinct declarations for
modern LangChain 1.4.3, core 1.6.7 and classic 1.0.8. The modern package
declares a LangGraph range, rather than implementing every execution layer
itself. The separately retained LangGraph source declares 1.2.14.
Comparing the packages as independent causal engines would double-count
the shared orchestration dependency and misstate what either provides
\citep{exec24_framework_langchain,v12_la04_langgraph}.

The other inspected profiles are Semantic Kernel's Python 1.45.0,
DSPy 3.4.0, LlamaIndex core 0.14.25 and a Haystack source declaration of
3.4.0-rc0. A release-candidate label must survive the comparison; it is
not silently promoted to a stable distribution. LlamaIndex's workflow
modules re-export another package. The traced repository resolves to
\texttt{run-llama/llama-agents}, where the selected package declares
\texttt{llama-index-workflows} 2.25.0. This declaration fits core's
specified range, but no solved environment or native compatibility test
has been performed
\citep{exec24_framework_semantic_kernel,exec24_framework_dspy,
exec24_framework_llama_index,exec24_framework_haystack,
exec24_framework_workflows}.

These are authenticated source revisions with commit dates no later than
7 October 2026, inspected from retained original bytes. They are not
claims about the latest release, a bank's installed version, or all
permitted dependency combinations. Root notices for the selected
LangChain, Semantic Kernel, DSPy, LlamaIndex and workflow sources are MIT;

review keeps its AgentChat code notice separate from its documentation
notice. Complete dependency, model-weight, connector and hosted-service
rights remain component-specific inputs
\citep{exec24_framework_langchain,exec24_framework_semantic_kernel,
exec24_framework_dspy,exec24_framework_llama_index,
exec24_framework_haystack,exec24_framework_workflows,v12_la04_autogen}.

\subsection{LangChain and LangGraph: graph recovery is not side-effect recovery}
The modern LangChain factory constructs a state graph and passes a
checkpointer, store and interrupt boundaries into compilation. This is
a concrete route for retaining the business brief, candidate graphs,
assumption decisions and tool results. The factory's configured recursion
limit is a graph-execution control; it is not a token budget, monetary
budget or end-to-end service deadline
\citep{exec24_framework_langchain}.

The retained LangGraph interrupt documentation states that resumption
restarts the node and re-executes its logic. A checkpointer is required
for the documented interrupt route. These properties support recoverable
analysis, but preceding external actions need their own replay contract.
If a node creates a paid external job before the interrupt, restored graph
state does not by itself prove that the job can safely be created again
\citep{v12_la04_langgraph,exec24_framework_contracts}.

The inspected modern retry middleware makes a useful further distinction.
It counts the initial attempt plus the configured retries, propagates
graph control-flow exceptions, and treats nonmatching exceptions separately.
After exhaustion, the tool middleware can return a tool message explicitly
marked as an error; the model middleware can return an assistant message
containing failure information. Both also permit an error-raising route.
A wrapper that tests only whether a message exists would erase the
difference between recovered output and reported failure
\citep{exec24_framework_langchain}.

An authored banking example specifies the resulting public test. Suppose
an external service accepts a 500 USD action, but its acknowledgement is
lost. Three submissions without a shared deduplication key can represent
1,500 USD of actions. Under an explicitly stipulated service contract
that deduplicates the same key, they represent 500 USD. The 1,000 USD
difference is not an observed framework defect; it is the consequence
of different external contracts. The proposed adapter must preserve the
logical action key, attempt identity, acknowledgement state and recovery
query. Retrying an unidentified causal request also does not repair its
scientific assumptions \citep{exec24_framework_contracts}.

LangChain and LangGraph are retained as reference orchestration choices,
with conditional integration through typed causal-engine tools. Direct
adoption as the scientific product is deferred. Porting a small source
mechanism is an alternative only when its dependency and notice obligations
are understood and its semantics can be maintained. A custom controller
may be simpler for a narrowly bounded workflow; the comparison should
measure that alternative on the same recovery and refusal fixtures
\citep{exec24_framework_contracts}.

\subsection{AutoGen: conversational state and scientific state are different}

state across calls and should receive new messages rather than the whole
conversation again. It warns against concurrent calls on the same agent
instance. The documented tool behavior can involve concurrent tool calls
and an additional model call for reflection. Its save/load methods retain
model context; they do not establish transactional recovery of arbitrary
external side effects
\citep{v12_la04_autogen}.

For the retention example, separate conversational roles can propose
assumptions, challenge them and explain results. Agreement among those
roles is not independent scientific evidence if they share the same
model, data, prompt history or mistaken business premise. Their graph
proposals should enter a comparison set with provenance, not become
accepted orientations because a conversation reached consensus. Scientific
state must include the graph object, query, assumptions, identification
result and uncertainty object independently of the natural-language history
\citep{exec24_framework_contracts}.

The pinned README declares maintenance mode and recommends a successor.
That declaration informs a maintenance decision; the successor's advertised
properties are not established here by repeating the README. Reference
use and an existing-installation adapter remain possible, while a new
deployment decision needs an independently reviewed migration target and
matched fixtures. The proposal therefore defers unconditional adoption,
retains a conditional integration route, and records maintenance and
component-specific rights as explicit revisit conditions
\citep{v12_la04_autogen,exec24_framework_contracts}.

The inspected Python function-choice behavior exposes included/excluded
plugins and functions, and a maximum automatic-invocation setting. Its

\citep{exec24_framework_semantic_kernel}.

The selected automatic-invocation handler catches ordinary function

validity is one condition among these, not their replacement

Reference use is retained; broad cross-language parity and direct adoption

\citep{exec24_framework_contracts}.

\subsection{DSPy: optimizing a program requires a defensible evaluator}
The inspected ReAct implementation builds a trajectory, calls selected
tools and records execution exceptions as observations. It may leave the
tool loop after an invalid selection or context-window problem and then
run an extraction step. This is a useful mechanism for explaining partial
work, but the extraction step is not proof that the requested causal
calculation succeeded. The result must retain whether identification,
estimation and uncertainty checks actually completed
\citep{exec24_framework_dspy}.

The evaluation implementation supplies a particularly relevant positive
contract: after a returned evaluation run, missing per-example results
receive the configured failure score, and the aggregate denominator is
the full supplied development set. That guards against silently reporting
only successful examples in that code path. If the executor raises at
its error threshold, however, no completed aggregate should be invented.
The task definition, scorer, allowed failure score and failure threshold
must accompany every reported benchmark
\citep{exec24_framework_dspy}.

In an authored example, 1,000 requests produce 800 returned answers and
600 scientifically qualified answers. The qualified fraction among
returns is $600/800=3/4$, while the fraction among all requests is
$600/1000=3/5$. These answer different questions. Neither fraction alone
measures causal calibration, utility or the severity of unqualified
answers. A public experiment should report the complete request ledger,
refusals, errors, qualified answers and the prespecified loss assigned to
each outcome \citep{exec24_framework_contracts}.

The inspected parallel executor also deserves careful source-level
qualification. It can resubmit stragglers and stores completed outcomes
by input index, while a resubmission set is keyed by Future objects.
The nearby comment describing one resubmission per item is therefore not
by itself a proved per-item invariant: distinct Future identities can
refer to the same input. No native liveness or duplicate-work failure is
asserted here. A public test must trace the input key and every submission,
including work that continues after a useful result has been collected
\citep{exec24_framework_dspy,exec24_framework_contracts}.

DSPy is retained as a reference for program construction and evaluation,
with conditional integration around a fixed causal-task scorer. The
scorer must distinguish graph prediction, identification, numerical
estimation, uncertainty and business loss. Optimizing on the same examples
later used to claim performance would change the evaluation question.
Adoption as a causal oracle is rejected; bounded program optimization and
selective source reuse remain testable alternatives
\citep{exec24_framework_contracts}.

\subsection{LlamaIndex: stopping, structured output and runtime delegation}
The selected LlamaIndex base agent keeps iteration counts in context.
At its limit, the inspected path either raises or performs a final model
generation, depending on the chosen early-stopping method. A generated
summary after exhausting the budget is useful communication, but its

from a return-direct route and from handoff behavior
\citep{exec24_framework_llama_index}.

infer it from the active-time limit
~~~

~~~text
\section{NumPyro: preserving the experiment through handlers and compiled inference}
\label{sec:exec23-numpyro-worker}

NumPyro is a plausible Python worker when a bank can state a probabilistic model and wants to explore a JAX-based computational route. Its role begins with that supplied model. It does not determine whether a servicing action is manipulable, whether an unrecorded customer state confounds treatment, or whether a financial reporting field was available when the decision was made. These scientific choices must enter the model contract before a sampler can answer the intended question. The pinned source examined here declares version 0.22.0 at revision \texttt{033f7e2e57bd0396fba8493ae246debe52f2c973}, committed on 5 October 2026. This is a source declaration at a revision within the literature cutoff, rather than an assertion that an independently acquired release artifact has identical contents. The root license is Apache-2.0, the Python requirement is at least 3.11, and the direct numerical requirements include JAX and jaxlib at least 0.7.0. Device-specific extras and the additional Funsor inference route require their own artifact and rights review. \cite{exec23_numpyro_sources}

The comparison with PyMC is therefore a comparison of proposed worker contracts. PyMC's inspected route transforms a graph and controls predictive freezing and regeneration; NumPyro's inspected route applies handlers to executions of a stochastic function and passes arrays through compiled inference. Neither representation supplies missing assignment information. Both need the same banking estimand, information clock, outcome units and refusal semantics. Their different defaults make a transparent adapter more useful than a wrapper that merely gives identically named commands. \cite{exec23_pymc_sources,exec23_numpyro_sources}

\subsection{Conditioning, intervention and the meaning of an execution trace}

In the inspected handler implementation, \texttt{condition} sets a matched sample value and marks the site observed. \texttt{substitute} can replace several kinds of primitive, including deterministic values, without making the same observation declaration. \texttt{replay} takes matched sampled values from an execution trace, checks the sampled-versus-observed role and leaves already observed target sites alone. Thus matching a site name is a mechanism for moving values; it is not evidence that two models describe the same financial experiment. An adapter must bind the model, data and site roles as well as their array shapes. \cite{exec23_numpyro_sources}

The \texttt{do} handler makes an especially consequential distinction. It creates a fresh sample site with the original name whose value does not propagate to descendants, then sends the supplied intervention value down the original computation. A returned treatment value and a recorded sample under the original treatment name can consequently differ by design. The upstream counterfactual tests explicitly distinguish the model's returned values from the trace values, including when observation and intervention are composed. Those tests describe intended behavior; they have not been executed in this proposal. A converter that extracts the original-name trace entry and calls it the administered action could misreport the experiment even when the handler follows its own contract. Multiple intervention handlers at the same site also require attention to the inspected warning and handler order. \cite{exec23_numpyro_sources}

The causal distinction can be checked without a numerical backend. Let an unobserved binary type $U$ have probability $1/2$, let a binary action $A$ agree with $U$ with probability $3/4$, and set the response to $Y=2A+4U$. Enumeration gives
\begin{equation}
 \mathrm{E}(Y\mid A=0)=1,\qquad
 \mathrm{E}(Y\mid A=1)=5,\qquad
 \mathrm{E}\{Y\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a)\}=2a+2.
\end{equation}
The association is four response units and the intervention contrast is two. This is the same deliberately confounded law used in the PyMC comparison, recalculated by an independently authored finite enumeration here. It supplies a common semantic oracle: conditioning an action and cutting its assignment mechanism have different answers. Neither backend acquires identification simply by returning one of these numbers. \cite{exec23_pymc_reference,exec23_numpyro_reference}

Composing handlers also does not make every customer-specific counterfactual identified. To see the extra requirement, let $Y^0$ and $Y^1$ denote binary responses under two actions. One structural model has $(Y^0,Y^1)=(U,U)$ for $U\sim\mathrm{Bernoulli}(1/2)$; another has $(Y^0,Y^1)=(U,1-U)$. Both have
\begin{equation}
 \Pr(Y^0=1)=\Pr(Y^1=1)=\tfrac12,
\end{equation}
but $\Pr(Y^1=1\mid Y^0=1)$ is one in the first model and zero in the second. Equal single-world intervention marginals leave this cross-world quantity undetermined. A shared-noise construction or another justified restriction can define a model-specific answer, and sensitivity across these constructions can expose the ambiguity. A model proposed by an LLM must state that construction explicitly; handler composition cannot verify it. This example is an authored identification witness, not an upstream software failure. \cite{exec23_numpyro_reference}

\subsection{Prediction must preserve which latent variables are regenerated}

The inspected \texttt{Predictive} implementation substitutes supplied posterior values, then executes the model. By default it ignores stored deterministic values during substitution and recomputes them from their parents. Setting \texttt{condition\_deterministic=True} instead permits those stored values to be substituted. Output selection through \texttt{return\_sites} has a separate role. As a simple arithmetic check, equal-weight parent values $(1,2)$ give a stored-square mean of $5/2$ and a recomputed-cube mean of $9/2$. Keeping the old deterministic values after changing the expression answers a different question from recomputation. NumPyro's default and PyMC's inspected predictive controls should therefore be represented by explicit regeneration choices in a common interface. One cannot infer equivalence from matching output names. \cite{exec23_numpyro_sources,exec23_pymc_sources,exec23_numpyro_reference}

Posterior substitution also fixes supplied stochastic sites. Including such a site among requested outputs does not ask the model to redraw it. Conversely, an absent latent site is not automatically inferred from an observed response during ordinary forward execution. The inspected \texttt{infer\_discrete} path invokes additional enumeration and posterior-sampling machinery; ordinary prediction uses a different masking and execution path. The documentation further requires clearing an observed response to generate a new realization of that response. Leaving an old observation attached can preserve that value rather than create a new future outcome. A bank worker must distinguish parameter draws learned from historical data, historical customer states, states to infer from new evidence and genuinely new outcomes. \cite{exec23_numpyro_sources}

A servicing example shows why this is an economic distinction. Suppose a hidden type $U=1$ has prior probability $1/3$, and an alert $S=1$ has probabilities $3/4$ under type one and $1/4$ under type zero. The alert probability and posterior type probability are
\begin{equation}
 \Pr(S=1)=\tfrac{5}{12},\qquad
 \Pr(U=1\mid S=1)=
 \frac{(1/3)(3/4)}{(1/3)(3/4)+(2/3)(1/4)}=\tfrac35.
\end{equation}
Let an additional action have stipulated net payoffs USD 100 for type one and USD $-200$ for type zero; taking no additional action pays zero. Averaging over the posterior gives
\begin{equation}
 V(1\mid S=1)=\tfrac35(100)+\tfrac25(-200)=-20.
\end{equation}
Replacing the type distribution by its most probable state instead reports USD 100 and selects the action, with an actual expected loss of USD 20 under the specified posterior law. Ignoring the alert and drawing the type from its prior gives yet another action value, USD $-100$. Posterior averaging, MAP substitution and unconditioned regeneration are three different procedures. These exact, stipulated amounts motivate the adapter's uncertainty contract; they are not measured returns from a bank or observed package behavior. \cite{exec23_numpyro_reference}

\subsection{Discrete inference and continuous sampling have separate contracts}

For enumerable latent sites, the inspected model utilities prepare parallel enumeration, with plate dimensions controlling the tensor arrangement. The Funsor contribution is an additional dependency and is labelled experimental by its import path. The inspected discrete handler accepts temperature one for posterior sampling and temperature zero for MAP-style decoding; other temperatures are rejected. Its source also warns that inferred-trace log probabilities are not meaningful. A downstream likelihood audit must not reuse those trace log probabilities as an ordinary fitted likelihood. Likewise, a MAP path is not a collection of posterior paths and cannot propagate hidden-state uncertainty in the servicing example. The scan boundary needs more careful qualification: the handler documentation says the scan primitive is unsupported, whereas the selected tests include scan hidden-Markov examples of lengths one and two and mark length ten as expected to fail because of a Markov sum-product adjoint limitation. This documentation/test tension justifies a registered length- and construction-specific trial, not a blanket assertion of support or a reproduced failure. None of those upstream tests has been run here. \cite{exec23_numpyro_sources}

NumPyro also exposes composable Gibbs and HMC-within-Gibbs routes. The inspected discrete selector distinguishes enumerable sites being updated from sites already marked for marginalization. The proposal must record that choice, support sizes, block structure and proposal settings. The inspected composition rejects some configurations, including subsample plates and value-dependent supports across blocks; the HMC-within-Gibbs entry rejects a bare potential-function model. These restrictions do not establish that a different kernel can repair the case. Native qualification should compare a small hidden-state model against complete enumeration and retain separate acceptance for marginal likelihood, posterior state probabilities and policy value. A state decoder agreeing with one selected path cannot satisfy all three. \cite{exec23_numpyro_sources}

MCMC splits a single key for multiple chains; it also accepts a supplied batch of keys. An adapter should preserve how chains and prediction tasks receive keys and check the intended independence or deliberate coupling. Their names do not establish identity with another package's diagnostic implementation. The proposed worker must distinguish an unavailable diagnostic, a nonfinite value, an adverse diagnostic and a satisfactory result under predeclared criteria. None of these outcomes certifies assignment truth, graph identification or repeated-sampling calibration of a causal policy interval. \cite{exec23_numpyro_sources}

For continuation, \texttt{last\_state} and \texttt{post\_warmup\_state} expose more information than saved posterior draws. The documented continuation route reuses the final state and its random key; warmup behavior changes when a post-warmup state is supplied. This is a useful interface for a future recovery design, but not evidence of durable serialization, crash consistency or compatibility across changed models. A restart contract must bind the complete sampler state, model/data identities, transformations, adaptation, random-key lineage, numerical environment and publication boundary. Local fault injection must then show whether uninterrupted and interrupted executions meet the registered comparison rule. Timing must also account for JAX's asynchronous dispatch, which the MCMC documentation expressly notes; elapsed Python submission time alone is not complete computational cost. \cite{exec23_numpyro_sources}

\subsection{A concrete reuse decision and a bounded qualification route}

The appropriate disposition is to retain NumPyro as a source-qualified reference for a future native Python worker. Direct use would preserve its handler, enumeration and numerical semantics within a pinned environment. A general R, Java or C++ port would duplicate those semantics and the compiler boundary without demonstrated benefit; a process interface is the more defensible candidate until conversion costs are measured. PyMC remains a substantive alternative for graph transformation and posterior prediction, while exact finite and conjugate calculations remain independent semantic references. No hardware performance ranking follows from the source review. \cite{exec23_numpyro_sources,exec23_pymc_sources,exec23_numpyro_reference}

Library, CLI and MCP entrypoints should preserve one model and experiment identity: observation versus intervention, factual versus cross-world target, fixed versus regenerated sites, posterior averaging versus MAP decoding, units and clock, chain layout, precision and diagnostic availability. \section{NumPyro: preserving the experiment through handlers and compiled inference}
~~~
~~~text
\label{sec:exec23-numpyro-worker}

NumPyro is a plausible Python worker when a bank can state a probabilistic model and wants to explore a JAX-based computational route. Its role begins with that supplied model. It does not determine whether a servicing action is manipulable, whether an unrecorded customer state confounds treatment, or whether a financial reporting field was available when the decision was made. These scientific choices must enter the model contract before a sampler can answer the intended question. The pinned source examined here declares version 0.22.0 at revision \texttt{033f7e2e57bd0396fba8493ae246debe52f2c973}, committed on 5 October 2026. This is a source declaration at a revision within the literature cutoff, rather than an assertion that an independently acquired release artifact has identical contents. The root license is Apache-2.0, the Python requirement is at least 3.11, and the direct numerical requirements include JAX and jaxlib at least 0.7.0. Device-specific extras and the additional Funsor inference route require their own artifact and rights review. \citep{exec23_numpyro_sources}

The comparison with PyMC is therefore a comparison of proposed worker contracts. PyMC's inspected route transforms a graph and controls predictive freezing and regeneration; NumPyro's inspected route applies handlers to executions of a stochastic function and passes arrays through compiled inference. Neither representation supplies missing assignment information. Both need the same banking estimand, information clock, outcome units and refusal semantics. Their different defaults make a transparent adapter more useful than a wrapper that merely gives identically named commands. \citep{exec23_pymc_sources,exec23_numpyro_sources}

\subsection{Conditioning, intervention and the meaning of an execution trace}

In the inspected handler implementation, \texttt{condition} sets a matched sample value and marks the site observed. \texttt{substitute} can replace several kinds of primitive, including deterministic values, without making the same observation declaration. \texttt{replay} takes matched sampled values from an execution trace, checks the sampled-versus-observed role and leaves already observed target sites alone. Thus matching a site name is a mechanism for moving values; it is not evidence that two models describe the same financial experiment. An adapter must bind the model, data and site roles as well as their array shapes. \citep{exec23_numpyro_sources}

The \texttt{do} handler makes an especially consequential distinction. It creates a fresh sample site with the original name whose value does not propagate to descendants, then sends the supplied intervention value down the original computation. A returned treatment value and a recorded sample under the original treatment name can consequently differ by design. The upstream counterfactual tests explicitly distinguish the model's returned values from the trace values, including when observation and intervention are composed. Those tests describe intended behavior; they have not been executed in this proposal. A converter that extracts the original-name trace entry and calls it the administered action could misreport the experiment even when the handler follows its own contract. Multiple intervention handlers at the same site also require attention to the inspected warning and handler order. \citep{exec23_numpyro_sources}

The causal distinction can be checked without a numerical backend. Let an unobserved binary type $U$ have probability $1/2$, let a binary action $A$ agree with $U$ with probability $3/4$, and set the response to $Y=2A+4U$. Enumeration gives
\begin{equation}
 \mathrm{E}(Y\mid A=0)=1,\qquad
 \mathrm{E}(Y\mid A=1)=5,\qquad
 \mathrm{E}\{Y\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a)\}=2a+2.
\end{equation}
The association is four response units and the intervention contrast is two. This is the same deliberately confounded law used in the PyMC comparison, recalculated by an independently authored finite enumeration here. It supplies a common semantic oracle: conditioning an action and cutting its assignment mechanism have different answers. Neither backend acquires identification simply by returning one of these numbers. \citep{exec23_pymc_reference,exec23_numpyro_reference}

Composing handlers also does not make every customer-specific counterfactual identified. To see the extra requirement, let $Y^0$ and $Y^1$ denote binary responses under two actions. One structural model has $(Y^0,Y^1)=(U,U)$ for $U\sim\mathrm{Bernoulli}(1/2)$; another has $(Y^0,Y^1)=(U,1-U)$. Both have
\begin{equation}
 \Pr(Y^0=1)=\Pr(Y^1=1)=\tfrac12,
\end{equation}
but $\Pr(Y^1=1\mid Y^0=1)$ is one in the first model and zero in the second. Equal single-world intervention marginals leave this cross-world quantity undetermined. A shared-noise construction or another justified restriction can define a model-specific answer, and sensitivity across these constructions can expose the ambiguity. A model proposed by an LLM must state that construction explicitly; handler composition cannot verify it. This example is an authored identification witness, not an upstream software failure. \citep{exec23_numpyro_reference}

\subsection{Prediction must preserve which latent variables are regenerated}

The inspected \texttt{Predictive} implementation substitutes supplied posterior values, then executes the model. By default it ignores stored deterministic values during substitution and recomputes them from their parents. Setting \texttt{condition\_deterministic=True} instead permits those stored values to be substituted. Output selection through \texttt{return\_sites} has a separate role. As a simple arithmetic check, equal-weight parent values $(1,2)$ give a stored-square mean of $5/2$ and a recomputed-cube mean of $9/2$. Keeping the old deterministic values after changing the expression answers a different question from recomputation. NumPyro's default and PyMC's inspected predictive controls should therefore be represented by explicit regeneration choices in a common interface. One cannot infer equivalence from matching output names. \citep{exec23_numpyro_sources,exec23_pymc_sources,exec23_numpyro_reference}

Posterior substitution also fixes supplied stochastic sites. Including such a site among requested outputs does not ask the model to redraw it. Conversely, an absent latent site is not automatically inferred from an observed response during ordinary forward execution. The inspected \texttt{infer\_discrete} path invokes additional enumeration and posterior-sampling machinery; ordinary prediction uses a different masking and execution path. The documentation further requires clearing an observed response to generate a new realization of that response. Leaving an old observation attached can preserve that value rather than create a new future outcome. A bank worker must distinguish parameter draws learned from historical data, historical customer states, states to infer from new evidence and genuinely new outcomes. \citep{exec23_numpyro_sources}

A servicing example shows why this is an economic distinction. Suppose a hidden type $U=1$ has prior probability $1/3$, and an alert $S=1$ has probabilities $3/4$ under type one and $1/4$ under type zero. The alert probability and posterior type probability are
\begin{equation}
 \Pr(S=1)=\tfrac{5}{12},\qquad
 \Pr(U=1\mid S=1)=
 \frac{(1/3)(3/4)}{(1/3)(3/4)+(2/3)(1/4)}=\tfrac35.
\end{equation}
Let an additional action have stipulated net payoffs USD 100 for type one and USD $-200$ for type zero; taking no additional action pays zero. Averaging over the posterior gives
\begin{equation}
 V(1\mid S=1)=\tfrac35(100)+\tfrac25(-200)=-20.
\end{equation}
Replacing the type distribution by its most probable state instead reports USD 100 and selects the action, with an actual expected loss of USD 20 under the specified posterior law. Ignoring the alert and drawing the type from its prior gives yet another action value, USD $-100$. Posterior averaging, MAP substitution and unconditioned regeneration are three different procedures. \chapter{Funding value when customer identity is uncertain}
~~~
~~~text
\label{integrated:weak_audit_projection}


\begin{quote}\small
The regular funding interval cannot support inference when a representative identity
audit cannot distinguish two candidate portfolio assignments. An alternative reporting design uses simultaneous bands for the four observable
candidate monetary responses, exact binomial audit intervals, and projection
through the assignment inverse without dividing by a nearly zero estimated
rank. In 3,000 fresh paired synthetic requests, the resulting set has high
all-request coverage but markedly worse financial precision. At the near-rank
design, 546 of 600 sets equal the whole real line. Exact audit inversion does
not make the response bands finite-sample exact, verify causal exogeneity, or
provide a bank decision threshold. These findings concern constructed funding studies; their usefulness for a
bank depends on the validity of the assumptions and the precision it needs.
\end{quote}

\section{The bank's target and the rank-one obstruction}

The target remains the value of a one-month 10-basis-point price intervention
over a fixed balance-stock response horizon $H=6$, summed across 48 branches:
\begin{equation}\label{integrated:weak_audit_projection:eq:target}
 V=\sum_{h=0}^{H}w_h\beta\rho^h-C.
\end{equation}
The monetary weights $w_h$ include branch scale, margin, discounting and the
first-month repricing interaction; $C$ is the direct repricing cost. The
intervention, weights and horizon were fixed before this experiment. A funding
desk needs both an interval/set that covers under defensible assumptions and
a width small enough to distinguish a worthwhile price change. These are
separate requirements.

For identity-audit stratum $s\in\{0,1\}$, let $\theta_s$ be the focal
portfolio's weighted response before $C$, $\delta_s$ the companion's weighted
response, and $p_s$ the probability that the first candidate is correctly
assigned. Noninformative whole-horizon swaps give observable candidate
responses
\begin{equation}\label{integrated:weak_audit_projection:eq:mixture}
 \mu_{s1}=p_s\theta_s+(1-p_s)\delta_s,\qquad
 \mu_{s2}=(1-p_s)\theta_s+p_s\delta_s.
\end{equation}
For $p_s\ne 1/2$, inversion yields
\begin{equation}\label{integrated:weak_audit_projection:eq:inverse}
 \theta_s=\frac{p_s\mu_{s1}-(1-p_s)\mu_{s2}}{2p_s-1},\qquad
 V=\tfrac12(\theta_0+\theta_1)-C.
\end{equation}
At $p_s=1/2$, the two observable responses both equal
$(\theta_s+\delta_s)/2$. If the companion response is unrestricted,
$\theta_s$ is then unrestricted. A finite interval obtained by substituting
$\widehat p_s\approx1/2$ would conceal this identification failure. The regular procedure in Section~\ref{v10:execution}
uses a Wilson rank guard and returns
``unavailable'' when its audit interval crosses $1/2$. The new design reports
the full set of values compatible with primitive response and audit bands.

\section{Primitive inference before inversion}

The nuisance pilot is independent of evaluation and has $M=4T$ dates. It
retains the fixed six-column dictionary, chronological half-split ridge
selection and full-pilot refit described in Section~\ref{v10:pilot}. Dependence within the pilot is allowed;
independence from evaluation and a stable relevant law are required. For each
evaluation date, let $v_t$ be the residualized action and $u_{tj}$ the
residualized, financially weighted candidate outcome for $j=1,2$. Write
\begin{equation}
 Q_s=\sum_t1\{S_t=s\}v_t^2,\qquad
 \widehat\mu_{sj}=Q_s^{-1}\sum_t1\{S_t=s\}v_tu_{tj}.
\end{equation}
Crucially, these are \emph{observable mixed-candidate} responses. Neither
an estimated audit probability nor the unstable inverse enters their score.
The scalar influence estimate is
\begin{equation}\label{integrated:weak_audit_projection:eq:score}
 \widehat\phi_{tsj}=\frac{T1\{S_t=s\}v_t
 (u_{tj}-v_t\widehat\mu_{sj})}{Q_s}.
\end{equation}
For each of four coordinates separately, center the score over all $T$ dates
and sum lag products through the prespecified response horizon $H$. The
variance of the sample mean is
\begin{equation}\label{integrated:weak_audit_projection:eq:hac}
 \widehat V_{sj}=T^{-2}\left\{\sum_t\widetilde\phi_{tsj}^2+
 2\sum_{k=1}^{H}\sum_{t=k+1}^{T}
 \widetilde\phi_{tsj}\widetilde\phi_{t-k,sj}\right\}.
\end{equation}
Only positive finite estimates qualify. This untapered fixed-horizon formula
uses the innovation-filtration argument in Section~\ref{v9:covariance}
under correct action-mean and exogeneity premises. Newey and West's positive-semidefinite Bartlett
construction is a distinct inherited alternative, not a proof that
\eqref{integrated:weak_audit_projection:eq:hac} is finite-sample positive or correctly calibrated under a
different law \cite{newey1986}. The orthogonal partialling-out score and
nuisance-product logic trace to the inspected primary DML text
\cite{dml2018}; its iid theorem does not supply this dependent-calendar
inference. The fixed-dictionary $M=4T$ centering rate is a project derivation
in Section~\ref{v9:pilot}.

Allocate $\alpha_R=.025$ among four two-sided normal response bands:
\begin{equation}
 B_{sj}=\left[\widehat\mu_{sj}\pm
 z_{1-\alpha_R/8}\sqrt{\widehat V_{sj}}\right].
\end{equation}
For independent representative binomial audits $(K_s,n_s)$, allocate
$\alpha_A=.025$ among two exact equal-tail binomial inversions $P_s$. Each
audit interval has error allocation $\alpha_A/2=.0125$ and tails of .00625.
The implementation computes beta-quantile endpoints rounded outwards; exact
binomial coverage was enumerated for sizes 1--15 on a probability grid and
compared to the existing inversion. This exact statement concerns only the
audit component. The response bands are normal/dependent-calendar
approximations, not exact finite-sample intervals.

Let $f(B_{s1},B_{s2},P_s)$ be the exact image of the rectangle under
\eqref{integrated:weak_audit_projection:eq:inverse}, retaining disconnected and infinite components. The
reported financial set is the Minkowski sum
\begin{equation}\label{integrated:weak_audit_projection:eq:set}
 \mathcal V=\tfrac12 f(B_{01},B_{02},P_0)
 +\tfrac12 f(B_{11},B_{12},P_1)-C.
\end{equation}
The projection can be computed without a grid over audit probabilities.
For one stratum, write $u=\mu_{s1}$, $v=\mu_{s2}$ and $r=2p_s-1$.
The inverse becomes
\begin{equation}\label{rel80:projection-corners}
 \theta_s=\frac{u+v}{2}+\frac{u-v}{2r},\qquad
 \frac{\partial\theta_s}{\partial r}=-\frac{u-v}{2r^2}.
\end{equation}
Here the denominator parameter is the mixing matrix's determinant; zero
determinant means matrix rank one. At any nonzero determinant, the inverse
is linear in the candidate responses, so its extrema occur at rectangle
corners. Each corner's derivative has a fixed sign on either side of zero;
its extrema therefore occur at branch endpoints or one-sided zero limits.
Continuity on each connected branch gives an interval image, although the
union can be disconnected. Combine stratum images by all pairwise interval
sums and merge overlaps; taking a convex hull would fill unsupported gaps.

If the audit interval contains one half and the candidate bands overlap,
equal observed responses are compatible with a rank-one matrix. Any focal
response is then possible: the unrestricted companion adjusts to preserve
their sum. The projection is the whole line. Nonoverlapping bands exclude
that singular case and can produce two unbounded components, one from each
side of the singularity. If the audit region consists only of one half,
nonoverlapping bands give an empty image. Substituting a large finite
interval would change both the set and its financial meaning.

On the event that all six primitive intervals cover their truths, $V\in
\mathcal V$ regardless of the rank of the audit matrix. For each fixed law
under the stated nuisance rate and response-score central limit theorem,
Bonferroni therefore gives $\Pr(V\in\mathcal V)\geq .95-o(1)$.
No uniform near-rank, false-law or finite-sample response guarantee is
claimed. At exact rank one, a compatible primitive region may project to the
whole real line; that is honest identification uncertainty, not a precise
answer. An empty projection is recorded as noncoverage, not replaced by an
unbounded set.

\section{Registered comparison and independent numerical challenge}

The design and author challenge were recorded before new draws. Five selected
stress cases each use 600 fresh paired requests: the 1,200-date baseline,
small audit, near-rank audit, persistent response and false exogeneity. The
same evaluation histories, fourfold pilot and audit counts feed both the
inherited regular pilot interval and the new projection. Pilot/evaluation/audit
seeds are disjoint from the precision comparison in Chapter~\ref{ch:precision-streaming}. The final journal records every request and
reconstructs all five summaries exactly. At 600 repetitions, the ordinary
Monte Carlo half-width near .95 is about .0174; the worst-case value is about
.0400. Exact-binomial Monte Carlo intervals and a five-cell Bonferroni family
are retained in the machine result. They describe these fixed synthetic laws,
not bank-population coverage.

Before the final draws, eight numerical challenges passed: small-count audit
coverage enumeration and comparison with the inherited inversion; whole-line
and disconnected rank-one sets; dense candidate-slope and horizon-covariance
arithmetic for baseline and near-rank fixtures; and rejection of invalid
counts, declarations, dimensions and nonfinite histories. These are author
checks, not independent scientific review. The streaming implementation keeps
fixed-dimensional pilot factors and four scalar lag accumulators, without
storing all evaluation scores.

571/600 versus 600/600, with median widths USD 499,000 and USD 1.406 million.
The selected persistent design had 555/600 versus 600/600, at approximately

selected-law sets, not evidence that a bank would accept their precision.

Near rank, the regular procedure returned a finite interval in only 132/600
requests and covered on 130/600 all requests. The projection produced 546/600
whole-line sets; only 54 were finite. Their conditional median finite width
was about USD 63.7 million, versus USD 1.91 million among the regular
procedure's 132 available intervals. All 600 projected sets covered, mainly
because most contained every real value. Reporting only ``100\% coverage''
would invert the practical conclusion.

In the false-exogeneity design, regular coverage was 122/600 and projection
coverage was 591/600. The latter had median width about USD 1.367 million,
roughly 2.4 times the regular width. This high selected-law coverage does not
validate the false declaration. The method has no causal guarantee there;
a different violation magnitude or economic threshold can expose the bias.
No method was chosen after observing this cell, and no universal correction
is established.

\section{Financial interpretation and the information still needed}

Projection can trade noncoverage or refusal for width. That trade is not
automatically useful. A funding decision based on the sign of $V$ would need
the entire defensible set on one side of the bank's specified decision
threshold. A whole-line set can never meet that rule. Even the baseline median
set width exceeds the synthetic target value (about USD 375,000) by more than
a factor of three. The exercise does not provide a bank threshold, the price
of representative audit labels, or the cost and availability of independent
pilot history. Width conditional on a finite set cannot substitute for
all-request coverage and finite-set availability.

The inherited regular inverse is tighter in selected cases but can refuse
near rank and undercovers under some finite designs. A sharper transformed
average/difference confidence region or candidate-specific covariance
inversion is a substantive alternative; it would need its own simultaneous
dependent-score argument and numerical qualification. More representative
audit labels can shrink $P_s$ but cannot cure a false origin-swap or
exogeneity premise. New outcome-linked information may identify targets that
counts and candidate responses cannot. These alternatives require separate evaluation.

Chapter~\ref{integrated:weak_audit_sharpening} develops the transformed average/difference alternative and evaluates it on fresh paired requests, including weak audits, persistence and false exogeneity. That comparison addresses precision under the same target; it does not acquire the new causal information required to rule out confounding. Bank use would also require
credible histories and audit labels, an economically meaningful precision
threshold, measured costs and operating evidence. The local experiment
establishes neither an adopted service nor institutional savings.

findings are project work. The cited sources support the specific technical
steps identified in the text; neither is presented as proving the new
construction. The study specification, code and complete results are retained
with the research materials. The literature cutoff is 7 October 2026.
~~~

~~~text
\chapter{Funding value when customer identity is uncertain}
\label{integrated:weak_audit_projection}


\begin{quote}\small
The regular funding interval cannot support inference when a representative identity
audit cannot distinguish two candidate portfolio assignments. An alternative reporting design uses simultaneous bands for the four observable
candidate monetary responses, exact binomial audit intervals, and projection
through the assignment inverse without dividing by a nearly zero estimated
rank. In 3,000 fresh paired synthetic requests, the resulting set has high
all-request coverage but markedly worse financial precision. At the near-rank
design, 546 of 600 sets equal the whole real line. Exact audit inversion does
not make the response bands finite-sample exact, verify causal exogeneity, or
provide a bank decision threshold. These findings concern constructed funding studies; their usefulness for a
bank depends on the validity of the assumptions and the precision it needs.
\end{quote}

\section{The bank's target and the rank-one obstruction}

The target remains the value of a one-month 10-basis-point price intervention
over a fixed balance-stock response horizon $H=6$, summed across 48 branches:
\begin{equation}\label{integrated:weak_audit_projection:eq:target}
 V=\sum_{h=0}^{H}w_h\beta\rho^h-C.
\end{equation}
The monetary weights $w_h$ include branch scale, margin, discounting and the
first-month repricing interaction; $C$ is the direct repricing cost. The
intervention, weights and horizon were fixed before this experiment. A funding
desk needs both an interval/set that covers under defensible assumptions and
a width small enough to distinguish a worthwhile price change. These are
separate requirements.

For identity-audit stratum $s\in\{0,1\}$, let $\theta_s$ be the focal
portfolio's weighted response before $C$, $\delta_s$ the companion's weighted
response, and $p_s$ the probability that the first candidate is correctly
assigned. Noninformative whole-horizon swaps give observable candidate
responses
\begin{equation}\label{integrated:weak_audit_projection:eq:mixture}
 \mu_{s1}=p_s\theta_s+(1-p_s)\delta_s,\qquad
 \mu_{s2}=(1-p_s)\theta_s+p_s\delta_s.
\end{equation}
For $p_s\ne 1/2$, inversion yields
\begin{equation}\label{integrated:weak_audit_projection:eq:inverse}
 \theta_s=\frac{p_s\mu_{s1}-(1-p_s)\mu_{s2}}{2p_s-1},\qquad
 V=\tfrac12(\theta_0+\theta_1)-C.
\end{equation}
At $p_s=1/2$, the two observable responses both equal
$(\theta_s+\delta_s)/2$. If the companion response is unrestricted,
$\theta_s$ is then unrestricted. A finite interval obtained by substituting
$\widehat p_s\approx1/2$ would conceal this identification failure. The regular procedure in Section~\ref{v10:execution}
uses a Wilson rank guard and returns
``unavailable'' when its audit interval crosses $1/2$. The new design reports
the full set of values compatible with primitive response and audit bands.

\section{Primitive inference before inversion}

The nuisance pilot is independent of evaluation and has $M=4T$ dates. It
retains the fixed six-column dictionary, chronological half-split ridge
selection and full-pilot refit described in Section~\ref{v10:pilot}. Dependence within the pilot is allowed;
independence from evaluation and a stable relevant law are required. For each
evaluation date, let $v_t$ be the residualized action and $u_{tj}$ the
residualized, financially weighted candidate outcome for $j=1,2$. Write
\begin{equation}
 Q_s=\sum_t1\{S_t=s\}v_t^2,\qquad
 \widehat\mu_{sj}=Q_s^{-1}\sum_t1\{S_t=s\}v_tu_{tj}.
\end{equation}
Crucially, these are \emph{observable mixed-candidate} responses. Neither
an estimated audit probability nor the unstable inverse enters their score.
The scalar influence estimate is
\begin{equation}\label{integrated:weak_audit_projection:eq:score}
 \widehat\phi_{tsj}=\frac{T1\{S_t=s\}v_t
 (u_{tj}-v_t\widehat\mu_{sj})}{Q_s}.
\end{equation}
For each of four coordinates separately, center the score over all $T$ dates
and sum lag products through the prespecified response horizon $H$. The
variance of the sample mean is
\begin{equation}\label{integrated:weak_audit_projection:eq:hac}
 \widehat V_{sj}=T^{-2}\left\{\sum_t\widetilde\phi_{tsj}^2+
 2\sum_{k=1}^{H}\sum_{t=k+1}^{T}
 \widetilde\phi_{tsj}\widetilde\phi_{t-k,sj}\right\}.
\end{equation}
Only positive finite estimates qualify. This untapered fixed-horizon formula
uses the innovation-filtration argument in Section~\ref{v9:covariance}
under correct action-mean and exogeneity premises. Newey and West's positive-semidefinite Bartlett
construction is a distinct inherited alternative, not a proof that
\eqref{integrated:weak_audit_projection:eq:hac} is finite-sample positive or correctly calibrated under a
different law \citep{newey1986}. The orthogonal partialling-out score and
nuisance-product logic trace to the inspected primary DML text
\citep{dml2018}; its iid theorem does not supply this dependent-calendar
inference. The fixed-dictionary $M=4T$ centering rate is a project derivation
in Section~\ref{v9:pilot}.

Allocate $\alpha_R=.025$ among four two-sided normal response bands:
\begin{equation}
 B_{sj}=\left[\widehat\mu_{sj}\pm
 z_{1-\alpha_R/8}\sqrt{\widehat V_{sj}}\right].
\end{equation}
For independent representative binomial audits $(K_s,n_s)$, allocate
$\alpha_A=.025$ among two exact equal-tail binomial inversions $P_s$. Each
audit interval has error allocation $\alpha_A/2=.0125$ and tails of .00625.
The implementation computes beta-quantile endpoints rounded outwards; exact
binomial coverage was enumerated for sizes 1--15 on a probability grid and
compared to the existing inversion. This exact statement concerns only the
audit component. The response bands are normal/dependent-calendar
approximations, not exact finite-sample intervals.

Let $f(B_{s1},B_{s2},P_s)$ be the exact image of the rectangle under
\eqref{integrated:weak_audit_projection:eq:inverse}, retaining disconnected and infinite components. The
reported financial set is the Minkowski sum
\begin{equation}\label{integrated:weak_audit_projection:eq:set}
 \mathcal V=\tfrac12 f(B_{01},B_{02},P_0)
 +\tfrac12 f(B_{11},B_{12},P_1)-C.
\end{equation}
The projection can be computed without a grid over audit probabilities.
For one stratum, write $u=\mu_{s1}$, $v=\mu_{s2}$ and $r=2p_s-1$.
The inverse becomes
\begin{equation}\label{rel80:projection-corners}
 \theta_s=\frac{u+v}{2}+\frac{u-v}{2r},\qquad
 \frac{\partial\theta_s}{\partial r}=-\frac{u-v}{2r^2}.
\end{equation}
Here the denominator parameter is the mixing matrix's determinant; zero
determinant means matrix rank one. At any nonzero determinant, the inverse
is linear in the candidate responses, so its extrema occur at rectangle
corners. Each corner's derivative has a fixed sign on either side of zero;
its extrema therefore occur at branch endpoints or one-sided zero limits.
Continuity on each connected branch gives an interval image, although the
union can be disconnected. Combine stratum images by all pairwise interval
sums and merge overlaps; taking a convex hull would fill unsupported gaps.

If the audit interval contains one half and the candidate bands overlap,
equal observed responses are compatible with a rank-one matrix. Any focal
response is then possible: the unrestricted companion adjusts to preserve
their sum. The projection is the whole line. Nonoverlapping bands exclude
that singular case and can produce two unbounded components, one from each
side of the singularity. If the audit region consists only of one half,
nonoverlapping bands give an empty image. Substituting a large finite
interval would change both the set and its financial meaning.

On the event that all six primitive intervals cover their truths, $V\in
\mathcal V$ regardless of the rank of the audit matrix. For each fixed law
under the stated nuisance rate and response-score central limit theorem,
Bonferroni therefore gives $\Pr(V\in\mathcal V)\geq .95-o(1)$.
No uniform near-rank, false-law or finite-sample response guarantee is
claimed. At exact rank one, a compatible primitive region may project to the
whole real line; that is honest identification uncertainty, not a precise
answer. An empty projection is recorded as noncoverage, not replaced by an
unbounded set.

\section{Registered comparison and independent numerical challenge}

The design and author challenge were recorded before new draws. Five selected
stress cases each use 600 fresh paired requests: the 1,200-date baseline,
small audit, near-rank audit, persistent response and false exogeneity. The
same evaluation histories, fourfold pilot and audit counts feed both the
inherited regular pilot interval and the new projection. Pilot/evaluation/audit
seeds are disjoint from the precision comparison in Chapter~\ref{ch:precision-streaming}. The final journal records every request and
reconstructs all five summaries exactly. At 600 repetitions, the ordinary
Monte Carlo half-width near .95 is about .0174; the worst-case value is about
.0400. Exact-binomial Monte Carlo intervals and a five-cell Bonferroni family
are retained in the machine result. They describe these fixed synthetic laws,
not bank-population coverage.

Before the final draws, eight numerical challenges passed: small-count audit
coverage enumeration and comparison with the inherited inversion; whole-line
and disconnected rank-one sets; dense candidate-slope and horizon-covariance
arithmetic for baseline and near-rank fixtures; and rejection of invalid
counts, declarations, dimensions and nonfinite histories. These are author
checks, not independent scientific review. The streaming implementation keeps
fixed-dimensional pilot factors and four scalar lag accumulators, without
storing all evaluation scores.
~~~

~~~text
\hypertarget{text-measurement-must-preserve-the-causal-question}{%
\subsection{Text measurement must preserve the causal
question}\label{text-measurement-must-preserve-the-causal-question}}

\label{exec13:census-measurement}

A servicing analyst may ask an assistant to extract financial distress
from call notes and then adjust for the extracted score when comparing
repayment plans. This can be useful work. It also combines three
different claims: that the score measures distress, that the note was
available before the plan decision, and that conditioning on the score
removes the relevant confounding. An accurate summary of the note
establishes none of the latter two claims. A later note may describe a
reaction to the plan; a note written only after a complaint may select
on both treatment and outcome. The proposed formulation interface must
attach a time and a measurement interpretation to each extracted
variable before adding it to an adjustment set.

Keith, Jensen and O'Connor review text used to measure otherwise
unobserved confounders. Their discussion explicitly distinguishes
confounders, colliders and mediators and asks whether one document can
encode several of these at once. It also identifies error in measured
confounders as an unresolved problem. A richer language representation
can improve measurement, but the review provides no guarantee that a
representation eliminates confounding. The appropriate comparison
therefore includes simple dictionaries, supervised extractors,
human-coded measurements and a language model, with the same permitted
document dates and the same effect target.
\cite{exec13_census_text_review_arxiv}

\hypertarget{a-reproducible-example-of-residual-confounding}{%
\subsubsection{A reproducible example of residual
confounding}\label{a-reproducible-example-of-residual-confounding}}

Consider the following project-generated population model. The
intervention intensity \(A\) and later loss \(Y\) are standardized
continuous quantities; these are illustrative units, not calibrated bank
measurements. True predecision distress is \(U\), while \(W\) is an
imperfect score extracted from a predecision note:

\[
 A=U+\varepsilon_A,\qquad
 W=U+\varepsilon_W,\qquad
 Y=\tau A+U+\varepsilon_Y.
\]

All four disturbances are mutually independent and centered Gaussian.
The variances of \(U,\varepsilon_A,\varepsilon_Y\) are one, while
\(\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_W)=s\geq0\). The true effect of
increasing \(A\) by one is \(\tau\). Conditional on \(W\), the residual
variance of \(U\) is \(v=s/(1+s)\). Residualizing both \(A\) and \(Y\)
on \(W\) therefore gives the population regression coefficient

\[
 \beta_{A\mid W}
 =\tau+\frac{v}{1+v}
 =\tau+\frac{s}{1+2s}.
\]

The second term persists with an infinite sample. It is not estimation
noise that a larger language model, an accurate propensity fit to \(W\),
or a narrower regression interval automatically removes. With the
stipulated \(\tau=-1/5\), exact covariance calculations give the
following values.

\begin{longtable}[]{@{}lll@{}}
\toprule
Text-score noise variance \(s\) & True effect & Adjusted population
coefficient\tabularnewline
\midrule
\endhead
\(0\) & \(-1/5\) & \(-1/5\)\tabularnewline
\(1/4\) & \(-1/5\) & \(-1/30\)\tabularnewline
\(1\) & \(-1/5\) & \(2/15\)\tabularnewline
\(4\) & \(-1/5\) & \(11/45\)\tabularnewline
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}

The score with \(s=1\) leaves enough confounding to reverse the sign.
This example is independently reproduced by solving the population
covariance normal equations and by residual variance decomposition. It
demonstrates a specific failure mechanism under a stated law, not a
claim that all text adjustment fails. A successful extraction study must
measure the relevant error and evaluate how it affects the causal
target. If a proxy-correction method is proposed, its additional
measurement assumptions and available validation information must be
stated rather than inferred from predictive accuracy.

\hypertarget{freeze-the-measurement-rule-before-evaluating-its-effects}{%
\subsubsection{Freeze the measurement rule before evaluating its
effects}\label{freeze-the-measurement-rule-before-evaluating-its-effects}}

Egami and colleagues make the measurement rule itself explicit. Let
\(g\) map a document into a category or vector. For a textual outcome,
\(E[g(Y(1))-g(Y(0))]\) is a target defined by that particular rule.
Searching over rules using the same treatment assignments and documents
later used for effect estimation can induce dependence and select
apparent effects. Their proposed separation of codebook discovery from
effect estimation addresses that problem, while their text-as-treatment
discussion imposes a further sufficiency restriction on the
representation. \cite{exec13_census_texts}

For a language-based measurement pipeline, the rule includes the model
version, prompt, retrieval corpus, preprocessing, extraction schema and
response aggregation. Freezing only a classifier filename while changing
the prompt after reading the effect estimates does not freeze \(g\). The
prototype should develop the rule on a designated development set,
record its identity, and evaluate it on held-out units. If several calls
concern one customer or conversation, those calls should remain together
in the split. This is a proposed implementation of the separation
principle, not a claim that sample splitting alone ensures valid
inference for dependent histories.

The held-out review asks whether the labels retain their intended
meaning, whether extraction errors differ by treatment and outcome, and
whether missing documents have a defensible observation model. It must
preserve negative findings. Rewriting the measurement rule to rescue a
disappointing effect requires a new evaluation set or an explicitly
exploratory analysis. Neither a fixed rule nor a held-out set supplies
unmeasured assignment information or repairs a post-treatment adjustment
error.

\hypertarget{formulate-competing-explanations-before-selecting-a-diagram}{%
\subsubsection{Formulate competing explanations before selecting a
diagram}\label{formulate-competing-explanations-before-selecting-a-diagram}}

Geraldo Bastías proposes building diagrams from the assumptions actually
used in a study, preserving several models where the assumptions do not
determine one. His workflow checks identification within each model,
derives observable implications, and distinguishes missing relationships
from missing variables. This is a methodological contribution to diagram
review, not an implemented LLM discovery algorithm. It supports an
assistant that makes assumptions inspectable rather than treating a
familiar design label as sufficient. \cite{exec13_census_credible}

For the servicing example, a short initial brief can leave open whether
distress caused the plan assignment, whether a later complaint caused a
note to be recorded, and whether the proposed outcome is arrears, loss
or customer welfare. The assistant should construct separate compatible
diagrams and show how each changes adjustment or identification. It can
check timing contradictions and derive conditional-independence
implications. Passing those checks does not establish that an omitted
common cause is absent. Where the diagrams imply different effects, the
useful output is the unresolved choice and the evidence that could
distinguish it.

These requirements permit immediate public and generated evaluation. A
public document corpus can supply realistic language, while a declared
generator supplies assignment, document timing, measurement error and
outcome truth. Simple extraction and fixed numerical workflows provide
baselines. The evaluation must vary mechanisms that are difficult for
the chosen extractor, including selective note availability and notes
written after treatment. Keith and colleagues specifically caution that
authors can choose semi-synthetic confounders their own method can
easily recover. Freezing adverse mechanisms and separating their
construction from final method selection addresses that concern more
directly than adding familiar domain vocabulary to a favorable
simulation. \cite{exec13_census_text_review_arxiv}

\label{exec13:census-measurement-end}
~~~

~~~text
Egami and colleagues make the measurement rule itself explicit. Let
~~~
