\section{A native forest boundary that preserves the banking question}
\label{exec13:grf-adapter}

A servicing analyst asks whether making a specified offer changes
twelve-month net receipts for eligible customers. The proposed treatment
is the offer, coded one, against no offer, coded zero. The outcome
includes the offer's cost and is measured in dollars per customer over
the stated horizon. A heterogeneous-effect forest can help estimate this
contrast under a declared identification model. Its C++ implementation
cannot decide whether the recorded offer was randomized, whether all
confounders were measured, or whether the analyst actually wants the
mean over customers, branches, or treated customers. Those choices must
precede engine dispatch and survive it.

The proposed first grf integration uses its maintained R interface in a
pinned local process, which in turn invokes the native C++ core. Direct
native embedding is a separate alternative. Inspection covers commit
\texttt{5bee99b51471}, dated 30 April 2026, whose package description
declares version 2.6.1. The snapshot therefore precedes the literature
cutoff; its October acquisition date is separately retained. The design
is not an installed adapter. The executed examples below are
project-owned arithmetic references; they neither train grf nor measure
its statistical performance
\citep{exec13_grf_runtime,exec13_grf_design,exec13_grf_oracle}.

\subsection{From an offer question to a local moment}

Let \(X\) contain information available before the offer,
\(W\in\{0,1\}\) denote assignment, and \(Y(w)\) denote the potential
twelve-month net receipt. With consistency, no interference, conditional
exchangeability and positivity, the target is \[
 \tau(x)=E[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid X=x],\qquad
 \theta=E[\tau(X)].
\] The outer expectation defines the customer population. An observed
treated subpopulation or an overlap-weighted population gives a
different target. The initial proposed profile accepts complete
observations from independent customers, a binary treatment, one fixed
outcome and a fixed horizon. It excludes repeated decision histories,
unmeasured confounding, interference, survey weighting and latent-graph
ambiguity that has not been resolved for this estimand. These are
restrictions of the proposed profile, not assertions that the package
has no other functionality.

Write \(m(x)=E[Y\mid X=x]\) and \(e(x)=E[W\mid X=x]\). The inspected R
wrapper either obtains nuisance predictions or uses supplied
predictions, then passes \(Y-\widehat m(X)\) and \(W-\widehat e(X)\) to
the native training boundary. A direct call that passes the original
vectors does not replicate that boundary. The causal binding selects the
instrumental trainer and sets the instrument coordinate to the treatment
coordinate. Consequently the inspected native prediction is a ratio of
locally weighted covariances, with the treatment variance in its
denominator \citep{exec13_grf_rpath,exec13_grf_native}.

For normalized nonnegative forest weights \(a_i(x)\), let
\(\widetilde Y_i\) and \(\widetilde W_i\) denote the residualized
values. The local calculation has the form \[
 \widehat\tau(x)=
 \frac{\sum_i a_i(x)(\widetilde Y_i-\overline Y_a)
                         (\widetilde W_i-\overline W_a)}
      {\sum_i a_i(x)(\widetilde W_i-\overline W_a)^2},
 \quad
 \overline Y_a=\sum_i a_i(x)\widetilde Y_i,
 \quad \overline W_a=\sum_i a_i(x)\widetilde W_i.
\] In the exact reference, equal weights on residual outcomes
\((-2,-1,1,2)\) and residual treatments \((-1/2,-1/2,1/2,1/2)\) give
slope three. Constant residual treatment gives zero denominator and the
reference refuses the calculation. Its numerical threshold is an
explicit arithmetic rule, not evidence that positivity holds in a bank
population. The native source divides by its local first-stage quantity;
the adapter must inspect finite outputs and retain weak-support
diagnostics instead of silently replacing a failed division with zero.

Honest tree splitting and out-of-bag prediction address particular reuse
of observations. They do not establish the causal premises or turn
customer rows from a common branch shock into independent samples.
Generalized forest theory also imposes regularity, subsampling, smooth
local identification and variance conditions; a named package and a
successful fit do not verify them \citep{grf2018}. The proposed first
profile retains the R nuisance path and its out-of-bag predictions.
Supplying an independently estimated nuisance vector requires a later
profile with explicit training identities, alignment and sampling-unit
split rules. A known randomized propensity may be supplied only with the
corresponding assignment declaration; it is never inferred from a
convenient constant.

\subsection{Why the average effect needs its own calculation}

The average of fitted conditional effects is not interchangeable with
the package's default augmented average-effect estimator. In the
inspected binary path, write \(\widehat\tau_i\) for the out-of-bag
conditional prediction. Its score is \[
 \Gamma_i=\widehat\tau_i+
 \frac{W_i-\widehat e_i}{\widehat e_i(1-\widehat e_i)}
 \{Y_i-\widehat m_i-\widehat\tau_i(W_i-\widehat e_i)\}.
\] This equals the familiar two-outcome-regression expression after
setting \(\widehat\mu_{0i}=\widehat m_i-\widehat e_i\widehat\tau_i\) and
\(\widehat\mu_{1i}=\widehat m_i+(1-\widehat e_i)\widehat\tau_i\). The
equality is algebraic. Consistency and uncertainty still require
appropriate nuisance estimation, overlap and sampling assumptions
\citep{exec13_grf_rpath}.

The reference uses four tuples
\((Y,W,\widehat m,\widehat e,\widehat\tau)\): \((0,0,1,1/4,2)\),
\((1,0,1,1/2,2)\), \((3,1,2,1/2,2)\), and \((5,1,2,3/4,2)\). Their
scores are \(8/3,0,2,16/3\). The mean score is \(5/2\), whereas the mean
conditional prediction is two. The C++ residual-score calculation and an
independent rational Python calculation using the two-regression formula
agree. This is an exact conversion check with deliberately supplied
numbers, not fitted evidence for double robustness or coverage
\citep{exec13_grf_oracle}.

For target weights \(q_i\), the corresponding estimator is
\(\widehat\theta=\sum_iq_i\Gamma_i/\sum_iq_i\). Choosing \(q_i=1\)
targets a customer-weighted population; choosing inverse branch sizes
gives each observed branch equal total weight. A branch with two
customer scores of ten dollars and a branch with four scores of forty
dollars produce a customer mean of thirty dollars and an equal-branch
mean of twenty-five dollars. A planning cohort of ten thousand customers
turns the five-dollar difference into fifty thousand dollars in a naive
projection. That calculation exposes the target change; it does not
justify applying an equal-branch mean to an arbitrary customer
portfolio.

The R interface documents that equal cluster weighting changes both
training sampling and average-effect weights, and disallows user sample
weights in that mode. Replacing the final mean alone cannot reproduce
training under that option. A native port would have to preserve both
mechanisms. The initial independent-customer profile therefore rejects
cluster and weight options; the independent-cluster extension is
specified for later qualification and must name whether customers or
clusters define its target \citep{exec13_grf_rpath}.

\subsection{Sampling uncertainty is not a numerical decoration}

For independent clusters indexed by \(g\), define
\(S_g=\sum_{i\in g}q_i(\Gamma_i-\widehat\theta)\), \(Q=\sum_iq_i\), and
let \(G\) count positive-weight clusters. The inspected all-sample
augmented average-effect path computes the variance expression \[
 \widehat V_{\rm cl}=\frac{G}{G-1}\frac{\sum_g S_g^2}{Q^2}.
\] This specifies a computation. Asymptotic validity needs an
appropriate independent-cluster experiment, sufficient effective
clusters and nuisance conditions; no fixed small cluster count
guarantees it. Dependence shared across branches through a calendar
factor lies outside that law.

For the six scores above, treating all rows as independent gives
variance forty dollars squared. Preserving two branch clusters while
retaining the customer target gives \(1600/9\) dollars squared. Giving
the two branches equal total weight gives variance 225 dollars squared
around the changed target of twenty-five dollars. The standard errors
are approximately 6.325, 13.333 and 15 dollars. Two clusters make a
useful arithmetic counterexample and supply no empirical
confidence-coverage qualification. A single positive-weight cluster is
refused. Zero total weight is separately refused
\citep{exec13_grf_oracle,exec13_grf_rpath}.

Conditional prediction variance is another quantity. The native
prediction strategy estimates it using grouped trees and a
variance-debiasing calculation; the binding copies the variance values
into \texttt{variance.estimates}. The R average-effect operation instead
returns \texttt{std.err}, already square-rooted. Squaring the wrong
field or taking its square root twice changes the units. The proposed
adapter keeps the raw field identity, method and units, then creates any
reported interval only under a declared inference profile. Pointwise
conditional intervals cannot become a simultaneous customer band or an
interval for their average through serialization. Likewise
\texttt{excess.error}, a finite-forest error diagnostic, is not a
substitute for sampling uncertainty
\citep{exec13_grf_native,exec13_grf_rpath}.

\subsection{Memory ownership, coordinates and model persistence}

The inspected \texttt{Data} class is a read-only view of a borrowed
contiguous column-major buffer. Element \((r,c)\) is read at offset
\(cn+r\), where \(n\) is the number of rows. Constructing the view from
a temporary vector does not transfer ownership. The host must keep the
allocation alive until all training or prediction threads have finished;
it must validate shape, index ranges and multiplication overflow before
the call. A three-row, two-column example has columns \((1,2,3)\) and
\((10,20,30)\). Correct layout reads twenty at zero-based coordinate
\((1,1)\); passing row-major bytes to the same index formula reads
three. Neither value is a memory error, so a mere successful call cannot
detect the scientific corruption
\citep{exec13_grf_memory,exec13_grf_oracle}.

Role coordinates must remain separate from predictor coordinates. The
native setters mark outcome, treatment, instrument and weight columns as
disallowed split variables. The host records the ordered covariate
dictionary, row identifiers, role indices and training/query
distinction. It cannot infer those roles from whichever columns happen
to be numeric. Missing values in covariates are supported by inspected
package paths, but are excluded by the initial profile so that an
undocumented imputation or missingness assumption is not introduced.
Conversion to double precision must preserve identifier strings
separately and refuse nonfinite numerical values rather than silently
dropping affected customers.

Model serialization also has ownership semantics. The inspected Rcpp
helper iterates by moving the unique pointer to each native tree into
its serialized representation. The header explicitly says the original
forest cannot be used after that operation. A direct embedding that
serializes and then predicts on the consumed forest is therefore
invalid. Either serialize an explicitly supported copy, or deserialize
the saved representation into a new object. Retain the engine commit,
ordered feature map, original training-data identity, nuisance vectors,
options and format version beside the forest. The selected source does
not establish a stable C++ ABI or a portable standalone model format.
These are admission questions for a native route, not problems solved by
choosing a file extension \citep{exec13_grf_memory}.

\subsection{A concrete request and result contract}

The operation is \texttt{estimate.effect}. Its generic parameter schema
accepts an engine identifier and estimator identifier, so the proposed
profile uses \texttt{grf-r-native-2.6.1} and
\texttt{binary-iid-aipw-all-v1} there. Detailed settings reside in an
immutable configuration artifact, carried through the existing artifact
list. That artifact binds the exact source commit, treatment contrast,
outcome/horizon, row and column roles, seed, thread count, tree options
and target. The adapter validates its own profile before dispatch;
generic JSON acceptance alone does not validate these scientific
restrictions \citep{exec13_grf_design}.

Library, CLI and MCP surfaces must resolve identical authorized data and
configuration identities. The context digest retains the estimand,
population, units, information clock, assumptions, sampling declaration
and graph. The full request identity additionally binds data bytes,
configuration, engine environment and numerical settings. Changing the
target population or turning branch weighting on produces a different
request; transport names cannot cause reuse of a previous result. Graph
endpoint marks and unresolved sets remain intact. A forest is not a
graph-identification service: if a retained model class gives different
effects and the query has no accepted identification argument, this
profile cannot silently select a graph.

Before runtime admission, discovery of this engine returns unavailable.
A recognized but unsupported sampling regime, continuous treatment,
dynamic policy request or unresolved graph requirement returns
unsupported with an actionable explanation. Nonfinite output, failed
subprocess execution or an invalid model artifact is a failure; no
finite effect accompanies it. A reviewed identification failure can
return not-identified with its evidence, but the adapter's inability to
analyze a model is not an impossibility proof. An overlap alarm produces
a refusal under the declared profile. Trimming or switching to an
overlap population requires a newly reviewed target and request.

After engineering admission, a computed scalar estimate keeps its dollar
unit, signed offer-minus-no-offer contrast and target identifier. A
diagnostic conditional-prediction artifact retains query-row coordinates
and explicitly denotes conditional means, not individual counterfactual
differences. The initial engineering result carries execution-only
qualification and no confidence claim. Conditional inference needs its
own reviewed uncertainty construction and evidence. A mathematically
unbounded or disconnected result from another method must be returned
with its topology; this forest profile does not approximate it by a
large finite interval.

\subsection{Deployment choices and the next informative comparison}

The package description requires R at least 3.5.0, C++17 and GNU make,
links Rcpp and RcppEigen, and imports additional packages including
Matrix, DiceKriging, lmtest and sandwich. These declarations are
minimum/source requirements, not a tested environment lock. The proposed
R process must record the installed R and dependency versions, source
and binary hashes, compiler and flags, thread settings and runtime
options. The inspected native CMake file collects both source and test
files into an executable; its presence does not supply a ready
production shared library or a reviewed installed ABI. Package metadata
declares GPL-3 and the inspected source headers state GPL version 3 or
later. Preserve file and dependency terms and review distribution
obligations before shipping; a subprocess boundary alone settles neither
licensing compatibility nor distribution duties
\citep{exec13_grf_runtime}.

The parent process bounds wall time, memory and output size and
publishes only a complete validated result atomically. Standard output
is the protocol channel; diagnostics have a bounded separate log. A
crash or timeout leaves a typed failure and its input identities. No
mid-tree recovery is promised. Replaying an immutable request starts
from its recorded seed and environment; bitwise equality across
different compilers or thread settings remains a measured property. One
worker per isolated R process is the conservative initial choice because
the inspected binding also writes global runtime context. Concurrency
inside a shared embedding requires its own review.

The proposal recommends the R/native route first because it retains the
inspected nuisance, score and aggregation paths. Direct native embedding
may later reduce interface overhead or fit a host's deployment
constraints, but would transfer those statistical and ownership
responsibilities to the host. A full algorithm port has the greatest
maintenance and conformance burden. Reject direct embedding for the
initial profile until it reproduces the R path; this is a scoped
engineering choice, not a claim that native integration is impossible.

The next comparison should freeze one environment and the complete
workload: data conversion, nuisance estimation, forest training,
average-effect scoring, serialization, output validation and failure
handling. Compare the maintained R route with a direct-native candidate
only under identical inputs, target, options and estimator formulas.
Exact fixtures first check coordinates, residualization, score
aggregation and refusal behavior. A separately registered generated-data
study can then examine coverage, availability, heterogeneity recovery
and resources, retaining weak-overlap and dependent cases in its
denominator. Pure arithmetic agreement cannot replace that study, and
local runtime cannot establish bank workflow savings. The useful
investment question is whether a native route improves the complete
workload enough to justify owning the additional statistical and
deployment machinery. \label{exec13:grf-adapter-end}

\section{A common interface preserves differences that matter}

The adapter comparison supports a common request and result vocabulary with deliberately different admitted operations. The Python route returns a symbolic functional under a supplied graph and explicit conditional-path restrictions. The Java route proposes a graph class under a specified discovery model and must retain failed tests before publication. The R/native route estimates a defined customer effect while preserving nuisance adjustment, aggregation and uncertainty conventions. A single effect field cannot stand in for these three services.

The local trials show why preservation extends beyond the estimator. A coordinate permutation, rounding at an integer boundary, a changed context, corrupt replay or incomplete publication can alter or conceal the scientific result. The observed refusals and successful recoveries establish particular behavior; the descriptor, input-access and error-classification findings identify repairs still needed for those versions. The next service design must carry both kinds of evidence forward. Its value is that a caller can tell what was computed, under which assumptions, what remains uncertain and which next action could resolve the limitation.

\section{Factual support in a causal assistant}
\label{exec22:fact-scope}

A retrieved explanation of a lending policy can be well supported by its cited
document and still leave the causal question unanswered. The document may
describe association, concern a different customer population, or rely on an
unverified assignment assumption. Wang and colleagues' survey of factuality
organizes evaluation and improvement around knowledge, retrieval and domain
specificity \cite{exec22_factuality_wang}. Its selected arXiv edition is useful
background for designing evidence assistance. Its taxonomy and surveyed
examples should not be read as independent validations of each underlying
method or as a theorem about causal diagrams.

The survey scopes factuality around determinable, undisputed facts. A causal
proposal frequently includes a different type of claim: whether a servicing
offer would change default, whether selection creates a spurious association,
or whether a time-indexed edge is needed. These questions can remain disputed
even when dates, document quotations and variable definitions are correct.
The assistant therefore needs an explicit distinction between what a source
says, whether that statement is warranted outside the source, and whether it
supports the proposed causal role for the population and time in question.

\subsection{Match the evaluation to the claim}

The survey distinguishes rule-based, neural, human and language-model
evaluation. Lexical overlap and semantic similarity can help locate likely
support, but neither is sufficient for entailment. ``The offer causes
repayment'' and ``the offer does not cause repayment'' share most words while
disagreeing on the decision-relevant proposition. Even a citation that
accurately supports the first sentence may describe a randomized intervention
in another setting or an author's unsupported interpretation of a regression.
Checking attribution and checking causal identification answer different
questions.

Atomic claim checking offers a useful design discipline: split the output into
claims whose support can be examined. For example, an assistant might assert
that treatment preceded the outcome, an instrument predicts treatment, its
exclusion restriction holds, and the estimated effect exceeds cost. The first
two may have direct documentation or statistical evidence. Exclusion usually
requires a structural argument; an effect-above-cost claim additionally needs
the target population, units, uncertainty and cost assumptions. One global
``factual'' score cannot make these evidence types interchangeable.

A proposed evidence record should therefore retain the exact source span,
edition, scope and claim role; distinguish quotation from project inference;
and preserve a conflict or unsupported status. Human reviewers can assess
scientific assumptions, but the survey also discusses subjectivity and
inconsistency in human evaluation. Model judges introduce their own bias and
domain limitations. Agreement among judges that share the same document,
training exposure or prompting pattern is not an independent scientific
replication. Calibrating a judge for citation entailment would still leave
causal identification and monetary decision quality to be assessed separately.

\subsection{Retrieval and structured knowledge help under stated conditions}

The survey identifies failure routes involving missing or conflicting
information, misleading evidence, distraction and misinterpretation. This
suggests concrete proposal requirements. Evidence search should preserve
contradictory passages and their populations, intervention definitions and
dates. Retrieval should allow ``insufficient evidence'' rather than making
general knowledge completion an obligatory final step. An assistant should
explain when a source settles a definition, offers a mechanism hypothesis or
reports an identified effect under assumptions. Increasing retrieved volume
does not by itself resolve disagreement among those roles.

Structured knowledge can improve entity and query mapping. For banking, this
could distinguish an application score from a post-decision monitoring score,
or connect two names for the same branch. A knowledge-graph relation such as
``associated with'', ``measured after'' or ``mentioned together'' is still not
a direct causal edge. An indirect mechanism should not silently become a
direct edge among observed variables. Temporal feedback requires explicit
time indexing or an appropriate cyclic model, rather than an acyclic drawing
that hides the feedback. The assistant's contribution is to expose candidate
interpretations and supporting evidence so that graph assumptions can be
reviewed.

The survey discusses debate and interactive retrieval as strategies described
in the literature. Those accounts motivate candidate workflows, not verified
superiority of a multi-agent implementation in this proposal. Several agents
repeating an unsupported premise may amplify confidence without adding
information. A useful design would require an independently sourced challenge,
record the unresolved disagreement and retain an abstention route. Its merit
must be measured against simpler retrieval and human-assisted baselines at
matched evidence and review budgets.

The survey's financial examples mainly concern language tasks. In that context
``causal language model'' can denote autoregressive next-token modeling.
That architectural term does not identify an intervention effect. Financial
text accuracy, sentiment prediction and financial question answering may help
prepare evidence, while a causal bank decision still requires an intervention,
target population, information clock, identification argument and uncertainty.
Domain fluency is useful only when those roles remain visible.

\subsection{An evaluation that can justify a prototype}

Public evaluation can test these distinctions before private bank experiments.
Freeze known-law causal cases and separate documentary corpora, including
negated statements, obsolete policies, contradictory populations, indirect
relations and observationally equivalent causal explanations. Compare simple
retrieval, structured retrieval and proposed agent workflows with matched
documents and budgets. Hold out documents and domains, and give adjudicators
the actual claim definitions rather than asking for an undifferentiated
plausibility score. These are proposed studies, not completed live-model
evaluations.

Report evidence retrieval and entailment, entity/time mapping, graph-role
errors, identification/refusal, target-weight preservation and decision loss
separately. Known-law cases establish ground truth by construction; public
observational data can test reproducibility and practical relevance but need
their own identifying assumptions. Neither should be labeled authentic bank
qualification. Include adversarial cases where every quoted sentence is
accurate but the causal conclusion or target population is wrong. Count corpus
curation, retrieval, repeated model calls, adjudication and maintenance when
comparing costs.

In the proposed CLI and MCP workflow, evidence status should accompany the
claim into the causal analysis request. Retrieved text supplies evidence, not
tool authorization. The result should distinguish supported premises,
unverified assumptions, identified or unidentified effects and the population
to which an interval refers. This would allow the assistant to explain why a
proposal needs more information or a narrower claim. The survey supports the
need to examine these evidence failures; actual reliability and economic merit
remain empirical questions for the bounded public prototype.

\subsection{Evaluate the claim behind the benchmark
score}\label{evaluate-the-claim-behind-the-benchmark-score}}

\label{exec13:census-evaluation}

CausalEval places diverse language tasks in one comparative survey,
including commonsense cause selection, correlation-to-causation
questions, graph-based inference and judgments about described events.
This is useful navigation, but the common label ``causal reasoning''
does not make their outcomes interchangeable. Correctly classifying a
relation mentioned in a sentence, recovering a graph from observations
and identifying a policy value test different information and
assumptions. \cite{exec13_census_causaleval}

\hypertarget{relation-extraction-is-a-serious-baseline-with-a-narrower-claim}{%
\subsubsection{Relation extraction is a serious baseline, with a
narrower
claim}\label{relation-extraction-is-a-serious-baseline-with-a-narrower-claim}}

Susanti and Holsmoelle compare prompting with fine-tuned models on four
relation datasets. On DDI, Table 1 reports F1 of 67.4 for Single-Prompt
C and 87.9 for PubMedBERT: a 20.5-point difference. The paper reports
five-fold averages and explicitly limits its evaluation to binary
pairwise causality assessment. It neither demonstrates joint graph
verification nor establishes a universal advantage for fine-tuning under
equal annotation costs. The comparison does establish that a supervised
smaller model deserves consideration when the proposed task is
extraction from a stable document domain.
\cite{exec13_census_graph_validation}

For banking notes, evaluate the extraction role on held-out documents
with independently specified labels and timestamps. Track abstention and
the treatment of ambiguous or contradictory passages. Then separately
evaluate whether extracted statements are admissible graph evidence. A
sentence that says ``the waiver caused repayment'' is evidence of what
the author claimed; it is not, by itself, evidence that assignment was
unconfounded. A useful agent should retain the quotation, its source and
the alternative causal interpretations.

Sng and colleagues illustrate why agreement is a separate target. Their
retrieval experiment supplies a mocked true causal graph, and their
conclusion explicitly says that reducing inconsistent ratings does not
imply accurate causal prediction. A comparison in which one arm receives
such a graph evaluates its use of supplied information. It does not
measure whether retrieval can discover the graph in a bank setting.
Registering both correct and misleading retrieved evidence is necessary
to expose that distinction. \cite{exec13_hallucination}

\hypertarget{task-specific-gains-should-remain-task-specific}{%
\subsubsection{Task-specific gains should remain
task-specific}\label{task-specific-gains-should-remain-task-specific}}

In CausalEval's Table 3, GPT-4o scores 69 on CLADDER with ordinary
chain-of-thought and 76 with FunctionCall, but its e-CARE scores are 90
and 73, respectively. These are author-reported pass@1 results for the
named versions and samples. The gains and losses should remain visible
rather than being replaced by the claim that tools always improve causal
reasoning. The table is also preferable to silently repeating
inconsistent numerical values in the paper's surrounding discussion.
\cite{exec13_census_causaleval}

The study repeats each question five times with greedy decoding.
Repeated calls can reveal response variation, but five calls to the same
question are not five independent causal problems. For illustration,
suppose there are \(N\) independent mechanisms, \(m\) calls per
mechanism, equal marginal score variance \(\sigma^2\), and common
within-mechanism correlation \(\rho\). Then

\[
 \operatorname{Var}(\bar S)
 =\frac{\sigma^2}{Nm}\{1+(m-1)\rho\}.
\]

At \(N=100,m=5,\rho=1\), the effective independent count is 100, not
500. This is a project-derived sampling illustration, not an estimate of
the paper's unreported correlation. The appropriate prototype analysis
clusters calls and paraphrases by underlying mechanism, reports the
number of distinct mechanisms, and uses paired comparisons when methods
see the same cases.

CausalEval also evaluates some expensive models on 100 cases rather than
the usual 500. Its human row combines scores from original benchmark
papers with a study of three graduate students on 100 questions for
remaining datasets. A combined human/model gap therefore is not one
uniform matched experiment. Any investment argument should state the
comparison actually performed, the cost and failure accounting, and the
uncertainty that remains.

\hypertarget{an-affordable-falsifiable-evaluation-sequence}{%
\subsubsection{An affordable, falsifiable evaluation
sequence}\label{an-affordable-falsifiable-evaluation-sequence}}

The proposed sequence starts with fixed causal mechanisms, explicit
public document provenance and deterministic numerical answers. It then
tests formulation, variable timing, graph uncertainty, identification,
execution and reporting separately, followed by their composition.
Baselines receive the same data, permitted documentation and tools.
Model-only reasoning, retrieval, a typed numerical workflow, and a
supervised extractor answer different engineering questions and should
be included where relevant.

The primary denominator includes every attempted case, with scientific
refusals distinguished from crashes and wrong answers. Numerical
accuracy conditional on successful execution is a secondary outcome.
Cost includes failed calls, retrieval, annotation, retries and human
review. Deliberately adverse cases include an accurate quotation
supporting a false causal claim, a timestamp that makes a proposed
control post-treatment, alternative graphs with different effects, a
misleading retrieved graph, and an unsupported edit policy.

Public and generated data can establish that these failure cases are
handled as specified and can compare methods under a known law. They do
not establish the frequency of those failures in a target bank or the
value of changing its real decisions. The next expensive experiment
should address a remaining uncertainty that could change the build or
adoption decision. Until such evidence exists, the proposal can
recommend a bounded prototype and a testable research direction while
preserving uncertainty about live-model performance, source completeness
and bank transport.

\label{exec13:census-evaluation-end}

\section{Choosing an agent architecture for a servicing decision}
\label{exec13:agent-architecture}

A bank considering assisted causal analysis faces an architectural choice
before it faces a model leaderboard. It can give a language model a broad
notebook environment, surround a fixed statistical pipeline with conversational
assistance, or ask several specialist agents to negotiate an analysis. Each
choice changes which mistakes are easy to detect, what must be reviewed by a
person, and how much an apparently completed answer costs. The useful comparison
is therefore between complete analytical paths with declared scientific
obligations. Counting agent roles or successful tool calls gives little guidance
about whether a servicing decision has been answered.

Consider a manager asking: ``Should we offer an early restructuring review to
customers entering arrears?'' Let the unit be an eligible account at its first
qualifying arrears date, $X$ the information available immediately before the
offer, $A\in\{0,1\}$ the offer, and $Y$ the discounted net cash recovery over a
fixed following horizon. The offer is distinct from acceptance and from the
eventual restructuring terms. For a specified eligible population $P$, an
initial target is
\begin{equation}
 \tau_P=E_P\{Y(1)-Y(0)\}.
 \label{exec13:architecture-target}
\end{equation}
If $Y$ excludes the incremental cost $c$ of making the offer, an expected-value
decision compares $\tau_P$ with $c$. If costs are already inside $Y$, subtracting
them again is wrong. An agent should make this definition explicit before
requesting an estimator. Neither an offer-acceptance prediction nor the effect
among customers who accepted is automatically an answer to this question.

The information clock is equally consequential. A field can carry an event
date before the offer but be entered into the database after it. The admissible
record is the version available at the decision time, with the extraction and
revision rule specified. A distress assessment obtained during the offer call
cannot silently become a pretreatment covariate. Multiple accounts held by one
customer, branch policies and shared collection teams require an explicit
sampling and interference analysis; calling each row an independent customer
does not settle these issues. The simple point-treatment example below assumes
one eligible unit, no interference and a declared independent-unit law. The
longitudinal construction earlier in this chapter is needed when subsequent
contacts and evolving distress become part of the intervention.

\subsection{What the competing architectures actually contribute}

The primary literature supports several distinct proposals. Zhu and colleagues'
CausalAgent routes processing, structure learning and reporting through agents
and MCP tools. Its four-page demonstration uses the Sachs dataset; quantitative
effect estimation and counterfactual modules remain among its stated future
directions. Its conversational interface is evidence of an interaction design,
not a demonstrated solution to the servicing target in
\eqref{exec13:architecture-target}. Han and colleagues' separately authored
Causal Agent instead illustrates named graph objects in tool memory and a
generated question benchmark. Keeping these two systems distinct prevents a
result from one from being attributed to the other's implementation
\cite{v12_la_2602_11527,exec13_census_causal_agent}.

The actor/critic design of oci-agent addresses a closer statistical problem:
point-in-time observational effects under supplied unconfoundedness. It exposes
specifications, notebooks and diagnostics to a human principal. This can reduce
the effort of reproducing an analysis or finding a failed overlap diagnostic.
The critical question is whether a proposed revision preserves the target.
Removing unsupported parts of the population may make an estimate more stable
while answering a different banking question. That is a substantive decision
which an attractive report must not hide. The paper's benchmark results remain
reported source findings, and are not reproduced live-model results of this
proposal \cite{v12_la_2607_22443}.

The causal-learn+ position takes a stricter approach. Agents assist data
inspection, method explanation and interpretation around a protected discovery
core. Their proposed edges, orientations or constraints do not automatically
become scientific evidence. This reduces one path by which language-model
beliefs enter a graph, but leaves assumption elicitation, variable construction
and statistical method choice as important tasks. Its call for future
benchmarks is consistent with treating the architecture as a candidate for
evaluation rather than an established performance advantage
\cite{v12_la_2606_23608}.

ORCA emphasizes shared relational state: joins, variable roles, graphs and
estimation configurations. This is especially relevant when banking data are
spread over account, customer, contact and transaction tables. However, the
paper's conversion of a consensus PAG into an actionable DAG introduces
orientation, reversal or deletion decisions. An analysis conducted on that DAG
inherits these extra choices. The architecture should expose them as additions
to the assumptions, and preserve the original uncertain graph. The numerical
comparison is also narrower than its headline suggests: the inspected table
reports completion rates of $.83$ and $.75$, whereas the abstract claims a
42-percentage-point gain. Completion is defined as producing an ATE regardless
of its accuracy. These are reasons to preserve the source discrepancy and to
design a better denominator, not to invent a corrected experiment
\cite{exec13_census_orca}.

Two further architectures broaden the comparison. CausalSmith makes a formal
statement, proof dependencies and compiler results explicit; its own limitations
separate proof checking from unvalidated model judgments about statement
faithfulness and research quality. Model Discovery Agent proposes executable
mechanisms, then uses numerical fitting and experiment design to compare them.
The latter's model-disagreement criterion approximates information gain within
a changing candidate set. Its reported predictive tests do not establish
causal identification, and its illustrated experiments use open-loop policies.
Neither formal proof search nor mechanism proposal alone replaces the
observational assumptions needed for the servicing target
\cite{exec13_census_causalsmith,v12_la_2608_09696}.

\begin{longtable}{@{}P{.19\textwidth}P{.35\textwidth}P{.39\textwidth}@{}}
\caption{Architecture choices for a bounded servicing prototype. These are
proposal decisions based on inspected sources.}\label{exec13:architecture-choices}\\
\toprule
Design & Useful intermediate object & Proposed reuse boundary\\\midrule
\endfirsthead
\toprule Design & Useful intermediate object & Proposed reuse boundary\\\midrule
\endhead
Conversational causal tools & Named variables, graph objects and explicit
tool arguments & Adapt interaction ideas; independently check graph encoding,
tool scope and malformed-result handling.\\
Actor/critic notebooks & Analysis specification, code, diagnostics and
criticism & Adapt review artifacts; restrict execution to a frozen supported
analysis and require a new target declaration after trimming.\\
Protected discovery core & Distinct suggestions, decisions, parameters and
graph outputs & Prefer for an initial discovery assistant; retain graph
ambiguity and test the advice surrounding the core.\\
Shared relational state & Joins, populations, candidate graphs and estimators
& Adopt the concept of typed intermediate state; keep every consequential
join and orientation inside the scientific review.\\
Formal proof workflow & Exact statement, definitions, imports and proof
& Use for selected derivations; review semantic fidelity and satisfiability
separately from compilation.\\
Mechanism proposal loop & Executable mechanisms, fitted weights and experiment
candidates & Consider for a later controlled simulator; inspect model support,
action coverage and approximation error before causal interpretation.\\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}

These alternatives suggest a restrained first prototype: one application-owned
controller, a bounded set of numerical and graph operations, and optional
language-model assistance for drafting and criticism. Multiple personas can be
an experimental arm. Their added value should be measured against the same
tools, information and total repair budget available to a simpler workflow.
This choice concerns the proposed product; it does not claim that the reviewed
external frameworks have been installed or integrated.

\subsection{A target can drift while every tool succeeds}

Suppose consistency, conditional exchangeability
$(Y(0),Y(1))\perp A\mid X$, positivity and the stated sampling law hold.
Write $e(x)=P(A=1\mid X=x)$ and $m_a(x)=E(Y\mid A=a,X=x)$.
The familiar augmented inverse-probability score is
\begin{align}
 \phi(O;m,e)={}&m_1(X)-m_0(X)
   +\frac{A\{Y-m_1(X)\}}{e(X)}\nonumber\\
 &-\frac{(1-A)\{Y-m_0(X)\}}{1-e(X)}.
 \label{exec13:architecture-score}
\end{align}
At the true nuisance functions, conditioning on $X$ removes both residual
terms, leaving $E\{\phi\mid X\}=E\{Y(1)-Y(0)\mid X\}$.
Consequently, averaging over $P$ gives $\tau_P$. Estimated nuisance functions,
cross-fitting, dependence and uncertainty require the additional arguments
developed elsewhere in this monograph. Calling this score does not establish
exchangeability or those rate conditions \cite{hernan2020}.

Now let an overlap diagnostic cause the workflow to keep only
$K=\{x:.1\leq e(x)\leq .9\}$. A uniform average of the score among retained
units targets
\begin{equation}
 \tau_K=\frac{E[1_K(X)\{m_1(X)-m_0(X)\}]}{P(X\in K)}.
 \label{exec13:architecture-trim}
\end{equation}
By contrast, define the overlap-weighted target explicitly as
\begin{equation}
 \tau_{\mathrm{ov}}=
 \frac{E[e(X)\{1-e(X)\}\{m_1(X)-m_0(X)\}]}
      {E[e(X)\{1-e(X)\}]}.
 \label{exec13:architecture-overlap}
\end{equation}
Equations \eqref{exec13:architecture-trim} and
\eqref{exec13:architecture-overlap} integrate against different measures.
They coincide only under additional restrictions, such as a constant
conditional effect; their labels cannot make them equal. If $K$ is estimated
from the same data, uncertainty about the selection rule is another issue.
The present calculation uses known propensities and a fixed rule so that this
additional difficulty does not obscure the target distinction.

In the inspected oci-agent notebook, the branch labeled ATO calls a propensity
trimming function and then applies a uniform AIPW summary to the retained
pseudo-outcomes. The serialization retains this label and exports retained
indices separately. This source path supports a trimmed-population
interpretation under the relevant assumptions; it does not implement the
weighting in \eqref{exec13:architecture-overlap}. The appropriate adaptation
therefore reads the implemented weights and retained population, not just the
display name \cite{v12_la_package_oci_agent}.

An exact generated example makes the financial consequence visible. Take
three strata with masses $(1/4,1/2,1/4)$, offer probabilities
$(.05,.5,.8)$ and conditional net-recovery effects $(-200,100,500)$ dollars.
Direct summation gives
\begin{equation}
 \tau_P=125,\qquad
 \tau_K=\frac{700}{3}\simeq233.33,\qquad
 \tau_{\mathrm{ov}}=\frac{48200}{283}\simeq170.32
 \quad\text{USD per account}.
 \label{exec13:architecture-target-numbers}
\end{equation}
Trimming retains three quarters of the original population. If the offer
cost is 180 dollars per eligible account and lies outside the recovery
outcome, the full-population expected net gain is $-55$ dollars. Substituting
the trimmed effect into that full-population calculation would reverse the
sign. A policy confined to the retained stratum is a different decision and
needs its own eligibility rule. The numbers are authored potential outcomes,
not observations about any bank. A separate 400-unit finite-population
calculation with exact nuisances reproduces all three weighted averages
\cite{exec13_architecture_exact}.

The same problem occurs in graph handoffs. Under one declared DAG, a baseline
distress measure can be a common cause of offer and recovery and belong in an
adjustment set. Under a different timing definition it can be a descendant of
the offer, so conditioning on it can remove part of the total effect. An
architecture should attach the variable definition, information time and graph
assumption to the adjustment result. Caching by column names alone cannot
preserve that meaning.

\subsection{What repeated critics can and cannot repair}

A critic is useful when it brings a distinct check: reconstructing weights,
reading a source passage, evaluating a graph criterion or reproducing a
numerical baseline. Merely repeating the same prompt with the same evidence
does not create independent scientific information. To quantify this
distinction, suppose each of three critics misses an error with marginal
probability $q=.1$. If their errors are independent, majority failure has
probability
\begin{equation}
 q^3+3q^2(1-q)=.028.
 \label{exec13:architecture-majority}
\end{equation}
Perfectly shared errors instead leave the failure probability at $.1$.
Consider an intermediate stipulated law: with probability $\gamma=.05$,
all three fail from a common cause; otherwise they fail independently with
probability $r=1/19$. Each still has marginal error
$\gamma+(1-\gamma)r=.1$, but majority failure becomes
\begin{equation}
 \gamma+(1-\gamma)\{r^3+3r^2(1-r)\}\simeq .05762.
 \label{exec13:architecture-common-error}
\end{equation}
Thus the same individual error rate can accompany quite different benefits
from voting. Exact enumeration over all eight independent-error patterns
checks the calculation. None of these probabilities is an empirical estimate
of a language model or a deployed critic \cite{exec13_architecture_exact}.

There is also an information limit. Consider two linear Gaussian worlds with
mutually independent standard normal noises in each world:
\begin{align}
 \mathcal W_1:&\quad X=U,\quad Y=\tfrac12X+\sqrt{3/4}\,V,\nonumber\\
 \mathcal W_2:&\quad Y=V',\quad X=\tfrac12Y+\sqrt{3/4}\,U'.
 \label{exec13:architecture-worlds}
\end{align}
Both observed pairs have zero mean, unit marginal variances and covariance
$1/2$, hence the same joint distribution. The effect of increasing $X$ by
one is $1/2$ in $\mathcal W_1$ and zero in $\mathcal W_2$. Suppose an
adaptive agent system receives only samples from that common law, identical
documents in both worlds and randomness independent of the world. The first
transcript step then has the same law in both worlds. If this holds through
step $t$, the next tool or agent applies the same conditional transition to
an identically distributed history, so it holds at $t+1$. Induction gives the
same distribution for the final answer. An additional critic operating on
that transcript cannot distinguish these worlds.

This argument concerns the stated information set. Genuine temporal knowledge,
an intervention or a justified scientific restriction can break its premise.
Retrieval is valuable when it supplies such information with an inspectable
provenance; fluent agreement alone cannot do so. The appropriate output before
the added information is available can be an identified set, a conditional
answer or a request to clarify the decision model. It need not be an arbitrary
scalar produced to make the workflow look complete.

Repeated repair also changes evaluation. In a deliberately simple experiment,
suppose a scientifically invalid candidate independently has probability $.05$
of passing a fallible screen on each try. Allowing twenty tries and retaining
the first apparent pass gives probability
$1-.95^{20}\simeq.6415$ of at least one false pass. Without independence, the
union bound is only $\min(1,20\times.05)=1$. This example describes independent
screening attempts, not deterministic replay of the same input, and does not
assign a statistical significance level to real agent review. It explains why
the proposed evaluation must retain all attempts, give comparators the same
repair budget and separate development feedback from held-out evaluation
\cite{exec13_architecture_exact}.

\subsection{Typed handoffs and the scope of recovery}

For the servicing prototype, a useful analysis state contains the decision
contract, data identity and clock, graph or graph class, assumptions with their
source and status, target measure, method applicability, numerical artifacts,
uncertainty statement and request history. These objects should refer to one
another by immutable identity. A revised target or graph invalidates dependent
results even when the data bytes are unchanged. A successful statistical call
must not make an unresolved assumption disappear.

The controller can enforce local invariants. An estimation request must name a
target and population; every variable must exist in the supplied schema; a
numerical interval must have finite, ordered endpoints unless the result type
explicitly supports an unbounded set; and a result must bind the method and
input versions that produced it. A graph-identification operation can check a
formal condition relative to a supplied graph. These checks support meaningful
handoffs, but none proves that the graph or observation law describes the bank.
Scientific assumption status should therefore remain visible alongside
mechanical validity.

This distinction leads to several result types with different continuation
actions. Malformed input calls for correction of the request. A missing backend
calls for an implementation or environment remedy. A mathematical
nonidentification result calls for different information or a different target.
An unsupported method calls for a scoped alternative. A valid set-valued answer
can proceed to a decision calculation that respects the set. Collapsing all of
these into either an empty successful object or a single generic failure would
discard the reason that determines the next useful action.

The inspected CausalAgent server illustrates a concrete boundary to repair
before reuse. Its OLC handler refers to a function not imported or defined in
that module and catches the resulting exception into a JSON error string.
Separately, its output helper extracts text between braces and returns an
empty dictionary on a decoding failure. These are static source findings, not
a claim that this proposal executed the upstream server. A wrapper must
validate the scientific result and propagate an explicit failure before
downstream analysis; successful transport of an error string is not a learned
graph \cite{v12_la_package_causalagent}.

Recovery has a related distinction. A graph checkpoint preserves enough state
to resume an operation; it does not automatically make external effects occur
exactly once. The inspected LangGraph interrupt restarts its node from the
beginning. An application should therefore give an expensive computation a
stable request identity, record its durable outcome and check that identity on
replay. For a remote provider call interrupted before a receipt is saved, the
outcome can remain unknown unless the provider supports lookup or idempotency.
Blind resubmission cannot be advertised as exact-once execution
\cite{v12_la04_langgraph}.

Pydantic AI supplies typed tool boundaries and usage controls, but the inspected
price check cannot enforce a monetary limit when price is unavailable. Some
usage becomes known only after a response. A prototype requiring a hard budget
needs a known pricing contract, conservative reservation and explicit behavior
for unknown cost. AutoGen's inspected save/load methods preserve model context;
they do not constitute a journal of arbitrary external side effects. Its
maintenance declaration and separate code/documentation licenses also enter
the adoption decision. These observations favor a plain controller baseline
before adding a framework whose incremental benefit has not yet been measured
\cite{v12_la04_pydantic_ai,v12_la04_autogen}.

The existing local prototype provides narrower positive evidence. Six authored
offline cases preserve blocked, unsupported, ambiguous and completed outcomes,
including directed-revision recovery and a weak moment set. The saved replay
reproduces those outcomes using real local tools with no live model calls.
This supports selected semantics and recovery behavior. It does not test
whether a language model elicits the right servicing graph, reduces human
effort or behaves correctly on an external platform. The library, CLI and MCP
contracts should carry this same distinction when transporting the result
\cite{exec13_architecture_local}.

\subsection{Selecting the next experiment by useful output and total cost}

The minimal comparison has a deterministic analyst template, a single assisted
controller and, if justified, a controller with a critic. All receive the same
documents, permitted tool implementations and task budget. Generated cases
should include correctly identified effects, ambiguity requiring a set or
refusal, misleading variable clocks, a target change after trimming and a tool
failure. A held-out task split separates adaptation of prompts and templates
from evaluation. Numerical truth comes from the declared generator, while
semantic scoring needs an independently specified reference and ambiguity
rubric. A correct refusal is a successful answer to a nonidentified task;
unnecessary refusal on an identified task is a separate error.

Let $N$ count all eligible assigned requests and $U_i$ indicate that request
$i$ produced an admissible, correct and decision-appropriate answer under the
rubric. A useful workflow summary is
\begin{equation}
 \widehat C_{\mathrm{usable}}=
 \frac{\sum_{i=1}^N(C_i^{\mathrm{tools}}+wT_i^{\mathrm{review}}
                         +C_i^{\mathrm{other}})}{\sum_{i=1}^N U_i}.
 \label{exec13:architecture-cost}
\end{equation}
It is undefined when there is no usable output. Costs for failed requests stay
in the numerator. The statistic should accompany the usable fraction, error
categories, refusal behavior, latency distribution and conditional numerical
accuracy. Reporting only accuracy among completed estimates can reward a system
that abandons difficult requests or hides configuration errors.

For planning, suppose manual review costs 15 minutes per request at 120 dollars
per hour and yields a usable fraction $.9$. Its ratio is $30/.9=33.33$ dollars.
An assisted workflow costing 3 dollars in tools plus 6 review minutes, with
usable fraction $.8$, gives $15/.8=18.75$ dollars. At 20 review minutes the
same tool and quality assumptions give $43/.8=53.75$ dollars. Equating the
assisted ratio to the manual ratio yields a review-time threshold of
$71/6\simeq11.83$ minutes. These stipulated scenarios omit fixed build costs;
they show which quantities to measure, not that assistance saves money
\cite{exec13_architecture_exact}.

The next justified experiment is consequently a bounded public/generated task
study measuring semantic failures and total review effort, with matched tools
and frozen denominators. A live-model performance claim requires a recorded
backend revision, actual calls and measured usage. A literature and architecture
proposal can proceed without that claim. Authentic bank experiments become
worth considering when the prototype isolates an uncertainty whose resolution
could change the build or investment decision. The unresolved questions are
specific: how often assumptions are elicited correctly, whether criticism adds
independent information, how much adjudication is needed and whether the
resulting gain survives a change in task population. None is answered by adding
agent roles to a diagram.
\label{exec13:agent-architecture-end}

\section{Choosing an agent architecture for a servicing decision}
\label{exec13:agent-architecture}

A bank considering assisted causal analysis faces an architectural choice
before it faces a model leaderboard. It can give a language model a broad
notebook environment, surround a fixed statistical pipeline with conversational
assistance, or ask several specialist agents to negotiate an analysis. Each
choice changes which mistakes are easy to detect, what must be reviewed by a
person, and how much an apparently completed answer costs. The useful comparison
is therefore between complete analytical paths with declared scientific
obligations. Counting agent roles or successful tool calls gives little guidance
about whether a servicing decision has been answered.

Consider a manager asking: ``Should we offer an early restructuring review to
customers entering arrears?'' Let the unit be an eligible account at its first
qualifying arrears date, $X$ the information available immediately before the
offer, $A\in\{0,1\}$ the offer, and $Y$ the discounted net cash recovery over a
fixed following horizon. The offer is distinct from acceptance and from the
eventual restructuring terms. For a specified eligible population $P$, an
initial target is
\begin{equation}
 \tau_P=E_P\{Y(1)-Y(0)\}.
 \label{exec13:architecture-target}
\end{equation}
If $Y$ excludes the incremental cost $c$ of making the offer, an expected-value
decision compares $\tau_P$ with $c$. If costs are already inside $Y$, subtracting
them again is wrong. An agent should make this definition explicit before
requesting an estimator. Neither an offer-acceptance prediction nor the effect
among customers who accepted is automatically an answer to this question.

The information clock is equally consequential. A field can carry an event
date before the offer but be entered into the database after it. The admissible
record is the version available at the decision time, with the extraction and
revision rule specified. A distress assessment obtained during the offer call
cannot silently become a pretreatment covariate. Multiple accounts held by one
customer, branch policies and shared collection teams require an explicit
sampling and interference analysis; calling each row an independent customer
does not settle these issues. The simple point-treatment example below assumes
one eligible unit, no interference and a declared independent-unit law. The
longitudinal construction earlier in this chapter is needed when subsequent
contacts and evolving distress become part of the intervention.

\subsection{What the competing architectures actually contribute}

The primary literature supports several distinct proposals. Zhu and colleagues'
CausalAgent routes processing, structure learning and reporting through agents
and MCP tools. Its four-page demonstration uses the Sachs dataset; quantitative
effect estimation and counterfactual modules remain among its stated future
directions. Its conversational interface is evidence of an interaction design,
not a demonstrated solution to the servicing target in
\eqref{exec13:architecture-target}. Han and colleagues' separately authored
Causal Agent instead illustrates named graph objects in tool memory and a
generated question benchmark. Keeping these two systems distinct prevents a
result from one from being attributed to the other's implementation
\citep{v12_la_2602_11527,exec13_census_causal_agent}.

The actor/critic design of oci-agent addresses a closer statistical problem:
point-in-time observational effects under supplied unconfoundedness. It exposes
specifications, notebooks and diagnostics to a human principal. This can reduce
the effort of reproducing an analysis or finding a failed overlap diagnostic.
The critical question is whether a proposed revision preserves the target.
Removing unsupported parts of the population may make an estimate more stable
while answering a different banking question. That is a substantive decision
which an attractive report must not hide. The paper's benchmark results remain
reported source findings, and are not reproduced live-model results of this
proposal \citep{v12_la_2607_22443}.

The causal-learn+ position takes a stricter approach. Agents assist data
inspection, method explanation and interpretation around a protected discovery
core. Their proposed edges, orientations or constraints do not automatically
become scientific evidence. This reduces one path by which language-model
beliefs enter a graph, but leaves assumption elicitation, variable construction
and statistical method choice as important tasks. Its call for future
benchmarks is consistent with treating the architecture as a candidate for
evaluation rather than an established performance advantage
\citep{v12_la_2606_23608}.

ORCA emphasizes shared relational state: joins, variable roles, graphs and
estimation configurations. This is especially relevant when banking data are
spread over account, customer, contact and transaction tables. However, the
paper's conversion of a consensus PAG into an actionable DAG introduces
orientation, reversal or deletion decisions. An analysis conducted on that DAG
inherits these extra choices. The architecture should expose them as additions
to the assumptions, and preserve the original uncertain graph. The numerical
comparison is also narrower than its headline suggests: the inspected table
reports completion rates of $.83$ and $.75$, whereas the abstract claims a
42-percentage-point gain. Completion is defined as producing an ATE regardless
of its accuracy. These are reasons to preserve the source discrepancy and to
design a better denominator, not to invent a corrected experiment
\citep{exec13_census_orca}.

Two further architectures broaden the comparison. CausalSmith makes a formal
statement, proof dependencies and compiler results explicit; its own limitations
separate proof checking from unvalidated model judgments about statement
faithfulness and research quality. Model Discovery Agent proposes executable
mechanisms, then uses numerical fitting and experiment design to compare them.
The latter's model-disagreement criterion approximates information gain within
a changing candidate set. Its reported predictive tests do not establish
causal identification, and its illustrated experiments use open-loop policies.
Neither formal proof search nor mechanism proposal alone replaces the
observational assumptions needed for the servicing target
\citep{exec13_census_causalsmith,v12_la_2608_09696}.

\begin{longtable}{@{}P{.19\textwidth}P{.35\textwidth}P{.39\textwidth}@{}}
\caption{Architecture choices for a bounded servicing prototype. These are
proposal decisions based on inspected sources.}\label{exec13:architecture-choices}\\
\toprule
Design & Useful intermediate object & Proposed reuse boundary\\\midrule
\endfirsthead
\toprule Design & Useful intermediate object & Proposed reuse boundary\\\midrule
\endhead
Conversational causal tools & Named variables, graph objects and explicit
tool arguments & Adapt interaction ideas; independently check graph encoding,
tool scope and malformed-result handling.\\
Actor/critic notebooks & Analysis specification, code, diagnostics and
criticism & Adapt review artifacts; restrict execution to a frozen supported
analysis and require a new target declaration after trimming.\\
Protected discovery core & Distinct suggestions, decisions, parameters and
graph outputs & Prefer for an initial discovery assistant; retain graph
ambiguity and test the advice surrounding the core.\\
Shared relational state & Joins, populations, candidate graphs and estimators
& Adopt the concept of typed intermediate state; keep every consequential
join and orientation inside the scientific review.\\
Formal proof workflow & Exact statement, definitions, imports and proof
& Use for selected derivations; review semantic fidelity and satisfiability
separately from compilation.\\
Mechanism proposal loop & Executable mechanisms, fitted weights and experiment
candidates & Consider for a later controlled simulator; inspect model support,
action coverage and approximation error before causal interpretation.\\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}

These alternatives suggest a restrained first prototype: one application-owned
controller, a bounded set of numerical and graph operations, and optional
language-model assistance for drafting and criticism. Multiple personas can be
an experimental arm. Their added value should be measured against the same
tools, information and total repair budget available to a simpler workflow.
This choice concerns the proposed product; it does not claim that the reviewed
external frameworks have been installed or integrated.

\subsection{A target can drift while every tool succeeds}

Suppose consistency, conditional exchangeability
$(Y(0),Y(1))\perp A\mid X$, positivity and the stated sampling law hold.
Write $e(x)=P(A=1\mid X=x)$ and $m_a(x)=E(Y\mid A=a,X=x)$.
The familiar augmented inverse-probability score is
\begin{align}
 \phi(O;m,e)={}&m_1(X)-m_0(X)
   +\frac{A\{Y-m_1(X)\}}{e(X)}\nonumber\\
 &-\frac{(1-A)\{Y-m_0(X)\}}{1-e(X)}.
 \label{exec13:architecture-score}
\end{align}
At the true nuisance functions, conditioning on $X$ removes both residual
terms, leaving $E\{\phi\mid X\}=E\{Y(1)-Y(0)\mid X\}$.
Consequently, averaging over $P$ gives $\tau_P$. Estimated nuisance functions,
cross-fitting, dependence and uncertainty require the additional arguments
developed elsewhere in this monograph. Calling this score does not establish
exchangeability or those rate conditions \citep{hernan2020}.

Now let an overlap diagnostic cause the workflow to keep only
$K=\{x:.1\leq e(x)\leq .9\}$. A uniform average of the score among retained
units targets
\begin{equation}
 \tau_K=\frac{E[1_K(X)\{m_1(X)-m_0(X)\}]}{P(X\in K)}.
 \label{exec13:architecture-trim}
\end{equation}
By contrast, define the overlap-weighted target explicitly as
\begin{equation}
 \tau_{\mathrm{ov}}=
 \frac{E[e(X)\{1-e(X)\}\{m_1(X)-m_0(X)\}]}
      {E[e(X)\{1-e(X)\}]}.
 \label{exec13:architecture-overlap}
\end{equation}
Equations \eqref{exec13:architecture-trim} and
\eqref{exec13:architecture-overlap} integrate against different measures.
They coincide only under additional restrictions, such as a constant
conditional effect; their labels cannot make them equal. If $K$ is estimated
from the same data, uncertainty about the selection rule is another issue.
The present calculation uses known propensities and a fixed rule so that this
additional difficulty does not obscure the target distinction.

In the inspected oci-agent notebook, the branch labeled ATO calls a propensity
trimming function and then applies a uniform AIPW summary to the retained
pseudo-outcomes. The serialization retains this label and exports retained
indices separately. This source path supports a trimmed-population
interpretation under the relevant assumptions; it does not implement the
weighting in \eqref{exec13:architecture-overlap}. The appropriate adaptation
therefore reads the implemented weights and retained population, not just the
display name \citep{v12_la_package_oci_agent}.

An exact generated example makes the financial consequence visible. Take
three strata with masses $(1/4,1/2,1/4)$, offer probabilities
$(.05,.5,.8)$ and conditional net-recovery effects $(-200,100,500)$ dollars.
Direct summation gives
\begin{equation}
 \tau_P=125,\qquad
 \tau_K=\frac{700}{3}\simeq233.33,\qquad
 \tau_{\mathrm{ov}}=\frac{48200}{283}\simeq170.32
 \quad\text{USD per account}.
 \label{exec13:architecture-target-numbers}
\end{equation}
Trimming retains three quarters of the original population. If the offer
cost is 180 dollars per eligible account and lies outside the recovery
outcome, the full-population expected net gain is $-55$ dollars. Substituting
the trimmed effect into that full-population calculation would reverse the
sign. A policy confined to the retained stratum is a different decision and
needs its own eligibility rule. The numbers are authored potential outcomes,
not observations about any bank. A separate 400-unit finite-population
calculation with exact nuisances reproduces all three weighted averages
\citep{exec13_architecture_exact}.

The same problem occurs in graph handoffs. Under one declared DAG, a baseline
distress measure can be a common cause of offer and recovery and belong in an
adjustment set. Under a different timing definition it can be a descendant of
the offer, so conditioning on it can remove part of the total effect. An
architecture should attach the variable definition, information time and graph
assumption to the adjustment result. Caching by column names alone cannot
preserve that meaning.
